reviews.comment: The class structure is half lectures and half case study presentations by other students. Lectures of this prof are interesting and entertaining but case presentations by groups can sometimes be very boring. He takes attendance every class and wont give you full credit unless you answer his questions or ask him questions. Good professor overall.

So I just missed one class and he graded me 1/5 in class participation very unfair. Juniors you can just skip his all classes as he will give maxium of 2.5/5 if you attend all lectures. He will just brag about his life achivements in lectures. Exams are easy.
Best professor in Texas, USA

The course is mainly a collection of business cases, some of them are really interesting and educating. He worked hard on making video lectures entertaining, but very often the tests are quite far from what he gives you.

I took two classes IT Management (5375) and Blockchain (5392), both at the same time with Dr. Chai. This is one amazing professor. Gives interest examples from variety of companies and case studies. Can surprise you with his knowledge. Funny guy but his tests can be hard, especially the midterm. His final was on the easier side and high scoring.
Tells good stories about his life. Just way too much talk outside the topic. Kinda looks down on ya.

Lectures were fun and Dr. Chai has great stories. However, his tests are very difficult and covers details on materials that he may have skimmed over during lectures. Says book is optional but I don't know how you'd pass without reading it since the lectures don't cover much.

Took her for MATH1421. She skips a lot of the textbook material because she thinks its not important. She also was gone for two weeks before one of our midterms so it affected our final grade a lot in the class. I feel like everytime there was a big exam, she wasn't able to go over the material that we need on time and it would cost us our grade.

no shade i barely understood anything in her class, uses a lot of “mathlish” as she says, and for someone who has took previous maths awhile ago it makes it hard to understand. she lectures as if it's a review but not teaching as if it's an unlearned topic

She's nice but teaches very slow so we're often behind. She teaches well in class, but she also skips over a lot of problems so I end up reteaching myself the material while doing the homework. Textbook required because that's how she takes notes. Attendance mandatory as well. There is homework due at the end of the week over each topic learned.

I loved Professor Calderon! She is super sweet and a great teacher. Attendance was mandatory, and there was a lot of homework. She is also very understanding and was helpful when I needed help. Overall, this was an easy class with a good professor!

I loved having professor Calderon as my instructor. She's super nice, fun to learn from, and explains everything well and concisely. There's always homework you gotta do by the end of every week, but to be honest it's not too many assignments and they're all actually helpful, plus exam reviews are extra credit as well. Do the work and you'll pass.

Cleaver is probably the best professor that UTA has to offer for Chem1465 (compared to Raj and Griffith). His explanations are pretty good. My main issue is that he writes small so it can be difficult to see the board but he provideds premade notes to follow along with that help out.

Doctor Cleaver's lectures were really interesting, and I would recommend attending them. For success in this class, be sure to do the problems at the end of the book because Cleaver wrote those problems, so they'll be similar to the test.
He's a great professor that genuinely cares about his students. He will meet with you and provide ways to get your grades up, and he's just a really great professor overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Cleaver is very willing to help and listen to students. The only criticism I have from his class this semester (Fall 2025) is that all exams throughout the semester were open response and very math heavy, but the final ended up being multiple choice which made it very vocab/memorization heavy. Overall I really enjoyed his class.

Nice guy, will work out problems with you. Highly recommend doing the practice problems on the textbook. Lab was probably the most tedious part. Curved my 88.6 at the end of the semester to an A. If you get a good grade on the first exam, you are honestly set. If you like math questions, take him. If you prefer concept questions, take Griffith.

Professor cleaver is great at explaining concepts and works through them step by step on the board. He usually responds to emails promptly and gives great one on one feedback and explanations during office hours. All the lectures are recorded on echo 360. Definitely need to do the practice problems and review the past exams to succeed in this class
Awesome professor to have for chemistry.  He goes through examples on the board and explains things very clearly.  When he says work extra problems on your own time, he means it!

awesome professor for chem and great lectures. he provides you with everything, but its your job to study it. chem is generally pretty hard, but I never once blamed him for my test grades. do practice problems, study, etc. it's best to reach out to him bc he genuinely cares about your success

I took Dr. Cleaver for Gen Chem 1 and 2. He is one of the best professors I have ever had! He truly cares about his students and wants us to do well. The class is not easy at all, and you must put in the work, but he is an amazing teacher who doesn't add to that stress. Go to his office hours if needed! Definitely take him for CHEM 1441 and 1442!
wish he taught o chem

TAKE CLEAVER FOR GEN CHEM!!!! He has been my favorite professor out of all of my classes. His lectures explain the material very well and prepare you for the exams. You do NEED to do homework outside of class to do well - you can't get a free pass in chemistry. He is very friendly and wants you to succeed.

I got a D in this class with Cleaver but then I retook it over the winter at a CC and got a B! I have Dr Cleaver to thank for my knowledge. Going to his lectures is so beneficial. He's helpful as well during office hours, but he can be a diva LOL. Chem is a hard class overall so you shouldn't slack off; know that Dr Cleaver wants to help!

Prof. Cleaver is a pretty good professor, his lectures are usually quite easy to understand. He does move very, very quickly. He's also pretty corny and funny. There are a lot of exams (5), but no quizzes, all multiple choice. The labs for the class are pretty fun and interesting too.

He is a very good lecturer. His speaking is easy to follow and he writes most things on the board. He is approachable for questions. He gives weekly homework assignments that are not too difficult but still helpful as well as 4 midterms and the final. I took CHEM 1341 so the midterms were all open response, and he gave very helpful feedback on them
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor! My lectures were more fast paced than the others but that is because I took the Chemistry major designed version" of the class. The exams are all free response, so make sure to know your stuff before taking exams. Very fun professor, easy to participate in the class. The homework can be long, but its per chapter, textbook based.
so cool, very knowledgeable about cars.

Chemistry is hard no matter who you have but avoid Dr. Cleaver at all costs. He is very passive aggressive when answering questions and sometimes he will even laugh if you ask a question. He doesn't care about any sickness or emergency you have you can't make up the attendance. He brags about his low test grades. I don't think he has any empathy.

his lectures were very clear and precise, with lots of examples and just enough detail to fully understand the concepts needed for the homework, tests, and labs. He teaches on the board, making it easy to take notes, but attending class was crucial because its difficult to record this. you can tell he really cares about what he does, TAKE HIM!!!!!!

He focusses too much on conceptualizing concepts instead of providing examples. However, he is the best for 1465. This class just requires a lot of studying. Also read the textbook before the lectures, if you slack off then you are going to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cleaver's class was better than I expected, when he started his course he informed us of how the test average was about 55% which worried me. He is very good at lecturing and covers most of what's on the test, but to get a good grade (i.e. doing well on tests), you NEED to study the textbook questions, some are almost verbatim on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cleaver is an amazing lecturer and will explain every concept like he's explaining it to a 5 yr old, HOWEVER, this course is very difficult. It's not the professor's fault, it's just the nature of the class due to university requirements. Cleaver outlines steps you need to succeed and it's very clear he wants all of his students to pass.

Just because he's an awesome professor does not mean that this class is a free pass. It's a tough course for ANYONE and you'll need to put in the effort. General Chemistry courses at UTA are textbook-heavy anyways and he just goes off of the book. He's a gifted speaker and showing up to lecture genuinely did help me understand the material.

Lectures are basically from the book. Just read the material and take notes before the lecture to get a grasp of the concepts. Overall, good professor, he just says "HMMKAY" a lot. Tests are just the practice problems from the book but they can be difficult. He simplifies the materials in the lectures which was nice.

Dr. Cleaver is great! He tries to make lectures fun, interactive and interesting. He is very accessible outside class and truly wants you to succeed. He meets you at the level you're at and tries his best to get you where you need to be. He does take attendance. His lectures follow the textbook EXACTLY, so very easy to follow along/take notes

He is a great lecturer and was able to break down chemistry into understandable concepts. Since I am a chem major we did get free response midterms (which weren't terrible since he was a pretty lenient grader). He is a funny guy and will try his best to answer to any confusion you may have.

Eh, I chose him because of these reviews and boy do I regret it. I dropped because his test are SO math heavy and not really like his lectures at all. I am now taking Crowell and I am crying/having less stress. I mean it's chem, so it's hard but Cleaver makes it worse.

I had him for 1341 and 1342. The absolute best lecturer in the department. He makes sure you understand the concepts first, rather than just throwing equations at you. He makes chemistry easy, and is very organized with his lectures. He also is incredibly caring, wants you to succeed in your academic career, and keeps in touch after the class ends!

Very understanding, tests aren't too bad if you study. I had him for 1342 (chem majors) and so all my exams were free response and he is a nice grader. Exams are more math based and not very conceptual.

Dr. Cleaver is such a nice professor. His tests are fairly easy if you do the review he posts on Canvas, they're essentially the same, but he just switches his number. He tests more heavily on math compared to the other professors.

extremely boring lectures, his voice is very monotone like mr.mackey from south park. (he says Mmmkay a lot). He is the melatonin everyone is looking for. His notes are very messy in a way. Lots of work to do.

Dr. Cleaver had amazing lectures. He went through all of the information needed for the exams, as well as explaining the reasoning for each topic. This made chemistry as intuitive as chemistry can be, and aided in memorization of the content. You'll do well in this class as long as you put in the effort to learn and review the content.
The only who can teaches chemistry in this department to be honest.

There is NO free pass to passing chemistry if you needed that reality check. There is a lot of homework and you HAVE to read the textbook to pass. He's a good professor who sets clear expectations for his students but you also need to do your part.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: His lectures were fast paced and organized. Many materials to access outside of the class. Take your own notes from the book outside of class and DO THE BOOK PROBLEMS. The exams problems are very similar to the book problems. If you feel confident doing the book problems and practice exams that he provides, you are guaranteed to pass the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's lectures are really good just because he knows how to pace the class and get through all the material needed in a realistic manner. He's exams are usually tolerable as long as you review and work on the textbook practice problems. Overall enjoyed his class

He's very clear when it comes to what's expected of you. Is always reminding you of deadlines, what needs to be done, what is important and what isn't for exams. And he gives tons and tons of practice material and review. The lab part of the class was probably the most annoying. I loved this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you see this, im warning you!!! I signed up for this class solely based on the reviews on ratemy. This class was extremely hard lectures don't help. I practically read the whole textbook and studied so hard for exams. HIS EXAMS ARE SO DIFFICULT COMPARED TO OTHER PROFESSORS!! IF U WANT TO BE HAPPY DONT TAKE CLEVER!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I dropped this class, Dr. Cleaver for the time I had him was a very great professor. His Practice Exams were basically his test, so as long as you understood those, you were fine. Chemistry is a hard subject though, so I will say to pay attention and do the textbook problems. They will come in handy when you need them.

Cleaver genuinely cares for his students, as he teaches clearly (& also quickly) and will happily answer any questions during lectures with a great sense of humor, unlike Dr. Raj. His homework is light with tests taking a majority of your grade, and both his notes and test problems are straight from the textbook (which you can get online for free)
He is a great chemistry professor, most of my classmates either finished the class with an A or B. He actually gives back your exam with feedback and corrections.

Cleaver is an excellent lecturer over the others. He really breaks down the "why" of phenomena well, and extensive formula sheets are provided each exam. He can be a bit sarcastic when answering some questions but he answers them nonetheless. Attendance is for a grade. The lectures being available on Canvas really helps when it comes to notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor and very understanding. Lectures are at a good pace and has many examples.

He is an engineer chemistry professor so prepare for the notes to be very squished together and hard to understand if you are taking gen chem. If you take this professor, be prepared to not only do his lecture notes but also the book work, aktiv chem, other teachers note, and tutors because he does not teach good.

For exams you need to work textbook problems, the lectures and hw will not be enough. His lectures are always posted before class and he does read word for word from the notes. Great professor I have some friends in the class who are doing well in his class. Workbook is not required it is posted online. I would definitely recommend this professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Cleaver is an amazing professor. His lectures are really helpful. He is also hilarious at times. I just love the way he teaches this course. You can tell he is passionate about chemistry by the way he teaches this course. I was terrified by chemistry but Dr. Cleaver's lectures are so good, it gave me assurance that I can pass this course.

Dr. Cleaver ACTUALLY teaches. He introduces a topic and does multiple examples to help you process the info. Very knowledgeable and accessible outside of class.  Lots of HW, but stay on top of them. They're not that bad to do and help prepare you for assessments.  Buy the online textbook and lab manual, no hard copy needed imo.

- Great professor who answers your questions; accessible outside of class and responsive. - STAY ON TOP OF HOMEWORK; really helps prepare for assessments and your grade, and not that bad to do. - Don't PROCRASTINATE; the workload may take a bit, but it's really not that bad - Extra credit - Only buy online txtbk and lab manual, not hard copy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: 4 exams 30question homework Points for attendance Lab. Posts note outlines recorded lectures practice exams. Textbook problems and practice exams are must to pass exams. Class is very fast difficult but manageable. Drops lowest lab an quiz, final replaces lowest exam. Will help u calculate grades u need to pass class. He's the best for chem1465

Dr. Cleaver is extremely knowledgeable and passionate, both about Chemistry and teaching it. His lectures cover everything you need to know, but the book contains excellent practice questions, which really help. Attendance is worth 5% of overall, but it's worth every point.

He is Chem lab coordinator. Sliced my had real bad with glass. The most unprofessional thing I've ever seen. Did not know what to do, there was NO first aid kit in lab. TA had no idea what to do either. Were not in coordination with health services. THE WORST

Dr. Cleaver is a good professor. His online lectures are funny and informative. This course is pretty difficult and lots of learning to be done, but not horrible. Quizzes are easy/helpful, homework is lengthy, and exams are difficult. They make you use 3 websites (which sucks) . Make sure from day 1 you do the BOOK PROBLEMS. Study the BOOK.

Doctor Cleaver is intensely knowledgeable about chemistry and will prepare you well for engineering. This class is not easy, it is CHEM 1 and 2 put together (in less detail), if you do not put in the effort you will not pass. The Textbook is mandatory and invaluable as it supplements lecture. The exams cover both lectures and textbook but is doable

This class is hard but the profs lectures are good. There is hw over chapters due every sunday. I personally didnt read the textbook bc the lectures were enough but reading wouldve made hw easier. After every lecture u have to answer participation questions for a grade (easy). The labs we did were tough, and exams were quite hard imo. Study alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Having Dr. Cleaver as my CHEM 1465 class was a blessing in disguise. I was genuinely surprised at how easy to understand and intuitive he made the lectures given my bad experience with chemistry in the past. Watching the lectures and doing the homework is mandatory to do well but he seems passionate to help you learn and grasp the subject.

From my experience, he is a good professor. He is more fast-paced than others but tries to make everything as clear as possible and genuinely cares for his students. His tests are a bit tricky and the homework can be long but help is always available.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Great professor. Is willing to help but beware the class is very hard. Just prepare to work and show that you're willing and he will help you. He teaches very well and makes the lectures interesting so the hour and a half doesn't feel like a drag. His pop quizzes are fun and make you laugh. Just be ready to work and put in effort and you'll love it

While his lectures are fairly well done, he is not kind outside of class. He is inaccessible out side of class as any problem you have whether is be grades or lectures he will basically say it is your problem and your fault even if it isn't.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher! I wish I could take him for every science class. He clearly explains every concept, teaches at an even pace, and is really patient! Go to every lecture and you'll easily pass the class. He offers exam corrections so if you get a B then you can bring it up to an A. I'd recommend him to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the best professor i've ever had! He is super patient with you when you dont understand a topic. Exams are not hard if you study and he lets you correct them for to redeem some of your points back. He's great and if you get the chance to take him i recommend 10/10!
Great professor, real nice man. Goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material. Would def take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! He helps you when you need it. Definitely recommend going to class because he goes over a lot of material. Homework is online through ALEKS. Tests are super straight forward. He is willing to meet with you and talk about your grades.

Fairly easy science credit for non-majors. Don't skip class - he covers a lot of materials in one lecture, and attendance is required  as a grade. Tests  short answers & comes straight out of the end of chapter problems from the book. He will help you with the problems if you visit his office. Lowest test grade can be used to opt out of final exam

Very good teacher, pay attention, take notes and do the mastering homework and you will do fine. The hardest test was the final which was departmental and so some the questions were phrased differently than what he normally had.

He is a great teacher; he's very clear and thorough with every topic he teaches and he knows his stuff. You will actually learn a lot from his class! However the only downside to his class are the exams! He is the toughest Chem prof in UTA. People actually feel sorry when they hear I attend his class and his exams because it is that hard!

1. Chem 1465 = Chem1 & 2 combined. Moves twice as fast, into the same depth. 2. Dr. Cleaver knows his stuff, he expects students to keep up and work hard. Lectures are fast and covers main points. 3. Have to do online hmwk to fully understand material.  Rumor is, 1465's passing rate's about 30%.  Course is HARD, but  Dr. C. is a good teacher.
Great teacher. Knows the stuffs what he is teaching well. Very clear and friendly. I would definitely recommend this professor.
Great lecturer! he is a great teacher and helpful. you do need to study for the multiple choice test tho because he test are kind of like rogers.

He is the bestest teacher in UTA..Very clear with what he wants and needs to teach..I never had to read on my own..whatever he wrote on board were my notes that i went through maybe twice before a test! :D But you HAVE to attend the class..you miss one, you're out of place and feel lost
He lectures mostly on a fast pace. Provides no note outlines. If you only attend his classes for the test and just read the book on your own you'll probably save yourself time.

Very nice professor!Dr.cleaver used the lecture time for introducing subject. You need to study further with the text book. His test is not the multiple choice questions, you need to show all your work to get the full credit. but he gives partial points for what you did right even if your answer is wrong. Test is not so hard if you throughly study.
Decent lectures, mostly read off the slides, but will stop to make sure the class is understanding the material.

She's very caring and does her best to help if you are confused, but her lectures are fast paced. Her class is lecture heavy, and is quite difficult to catch up to if you fall behind (been there done that). It's hard studying for it in the beginning, but it gets easier as the units pass by.

Took BIOL 1301 with her but it wasn't an option. Only graded based off of homeworks and exams so exams can really affect your grade. I love Dr. Maynard and thought this class was relatively easy. Content is not heavy nor hard. Will replace your lowest exam grade with your final exam grade if it is higher.
Awesome class

Took for Bio 1301 she was a great person but not a great professor. Felt the class was made hard for no reason. She would make reviews and review in class but it was very vague. Only like 10% of the review was on the actual test. She says to study the review(s) but basically every slide is on the test so she's going against herself? No extra credit

LOVE her. I was sad I couldn't take her microbio because it conflicts with another necessary class. Beware: she does talk super fast, so I highly suggest printing out the slides prior to attending each lecture so you can take notes directly on the slides. She is amenable to spending more time, though, if you ask. She's FANTASTIC. LOVE her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
I took 1301 but that wasn't an option since this was her first time teaching this course. 
The class isn't hard, she's really sweet, and the tests are straight from the lecture slides. The tests are done in person and they're on lockdown browser with webcam. You have 1 assignment a week and then the tests, so the tests really affect your grade.

In lectures, she's lowk just reading off the slides so I didn't pay much attention. A week before each exam, I just went through the slides of the modules and did the practice homework, and I still did fine. It's a little stressful if you do that, but it's manageable. Overall, the class is easy. Professor is nice and doesn't take attendance.

(Taken in Fall 2025) If you study and work for it, you'll get an A! 4 practice exams, 4 exams, and repeatable homework for each module (10 total). Professor Maynard is so caring of her students and you can tell she knows her stuff. She gets excited talking about the content, but my class asked her to slow down and she did, she takes feedback well!

She gave me a love-hate relationship with this class, she's very nice and gives feedback but she just reads off of the slides. If you want to pass you'll have to do most of the studying on your own or maybe reteach the content to yourself. Practice tests taken as actual test grade, barely any homework. Overall its okay, depending on preferences.
Very good professor just reads of slides though but answers any questions students have. She is also very caring about her students. But if you really want to pass you have to study a lot.

I liked this professor alot she genuinely cared for ur grade in the class and offered various support resources in order to help you succeed in her class. I never used the textbook but all long as you study the PowerPoint you'll do well

This class relies heavily on slides, sometimes 150+ per exam, which is overwhelming. The professor is kind and wants to help, but often seems unsure when teaching. She says all slides could be on the exam, leaving us with too much to study. Many slides aren't even needed, making it hard to focus on key material.

Microbiology is heavy on memorization. There are around 150 to 250 slides that you will need to go over for each exam with 4 exams and a cumulative final. This is a pretty tough course so do not try to cram study the material. Maynard drops the lowest exam including the final exam and usually curves exams to get a class average of 70.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The low ratings on Dr. Maynard regarding Microbiology are from people who weren't expecting the class to be hard. This subject is challenging, so be prepared to spend a lot of time studying! The class is lecture and exam-heavy, but she gives extra credit (6+ points) if you attend the lecture before the exam, & the curving is super generous as well.

I thought this class was pretty easy and wasn't bothered by Dr. Maynard's teaching style. If you go to class, do the homework assignments, and study, you should be more than fine. Dr. Maynard is super sweet and helpful, she is truly passionate about what she teaches and her students.

She is a very nice professor, she lowkey js reads off the slides tho, but I don't find it to be a problem because if you go to her office hours for a question to clarify things, she is very helpful in understanding concepts. Her reviews are helpful and the slides are informative.

Really easy EC opportunities (up to 5% added to grade avg), bonus pts on exams if you attend specific classes, and generous curves. She's nice, easy to reach through email, and always eager to answer questions. You could get away with self-studying the entire course as lectures are just going over powerpoints. Should be very manageable
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Micro is a super hard class in general and a weed out class for all the people that can't handle it. Most of the bad reviews have a problem with the course DESIGN and CONTENT. Maynard herself is ok at reviewing but she's getting better and the curves for the exams are always good. She always replies super quickly. Lots of extra credit opportunities

I thought she was excellent, but many of the bad reviews are from freshman who did not expect a semi difficult biology. Yes, you have to do homework, yes you have to study; but she gives all the resources for that. She taught efficiently and was kind all semester. Her lectures weren't impressively interesting, but were direct and helpful.
This class is lecture heavy and the study guides never matched the material on exams. I would take her classes again as Dr. Maynard is nice and helps a lot more one-on-one.

This class was so hard. Exams will have some random info from lectures and barely any practice problems but there's extra credit and a curve. She is caring and nice but her lecture isn't that great, feels like she's unsure of the info not great at explaining. She does help by emphasizing what will be on the test. This class is purely memorizing.
bffr she only canceled class 1x & it wasnt before class… anyways shes sooo sweet & helpful! the amount of ec we get it SO GOOD! & she tells us what will be on the exam :) oh & lec are recorded

Grades are heavily just based on your exam grades. It's a shame the amount of slides we have to study due to the lack of homework/practice problems provided. It's either you thoroughly study the 200 page slideshows or you're screwed. We pay thousands of dollars to be provided with the bare minimum, it's not fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER FOR MICRO. Take dr. Dylan Parks or dr. Ida Klang. All Maynard does is read off the slides like a robot as such showing up to lecture is pointless. As a professor she does little to teach and add to the material like dr. parks or dr. klang do. Maynard seems like a very genuine person but she is still very lacking as a professor.

I took this class for micro biology and she is a VERY fast teacher who doesn't even let you understand the material first before quickly rushing to the next topic.. she LIED about how her class was just like 1345 but it is NOT. This is the HARDEST class I ever took in my LIFE. DO NOT TAKE HER
One of my favorite bio teachers so far!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The workload was not heavy. Professor Maynard is an amazing professor! She had in-class activities (like kahoot) that really helped me to identify which topic I was not familiar with. The class atmosphere was really light, I enjoyed it.

Like others say, she's very kind. She offers reviews before exams such as in kahoot games, which I heard other biology profs don't do. This shows she puts in the extra mile towards making sure we remember what we learn because she truly cares. Attendance isn't required while class participation isn't required but heavily encouraged!
A lot of memorization from a bunch of slides, but the class is relatively easy. 10 homework assignments that you can repeat until you get a 100.

Professor Maynard is super kind and caring about all her students! The class is very test-heavy with 4 exams that are directly from her lectures so you should be fine as long as you study and take good notes. The class also consists of practice exams and practice homework that helped many students and myself succeed in the class!

She's very nice. Always open to help and answer questions. She drops a few low grades and offers many resources for her lectures and exams. Her study guides tend to be over only a few topics of the unit but it is nice that she even offers it. Practice exams had 2 attempts, exams are similar to practice exams.

She was a really good teacher. Loved that we had 2 tries on the practice exams. Her exams can be tedious because of the little details. READ every LITTLE details in the lectures because they could be on the exams. Just wished her reviews were better because sometimes felt they were a bit broad.

Professor Maynard is very kind and does her best to help her students. Her classes are all lectures with some review days, and the class is graded mainly on exams. The lecture slides have everything you need to know for the exam, so as long as you take good notes and memorize the material you will do fine on the exams.

Super sweet and really cares about her students! She can be okay at times but most of the time she isn't. Her political views show a lot as well and it is hard to approach her with questions. Mrs. Conner would be an excellent high school teacher, but she shouldn't be teaching college English. She gives vague feedback, and usually, she only gives okay feedback to you in person with the most booming voice possible so everyone else can hear it. In addition to this, she ONLY unlocks assignments the day they're due unless it's a major grade.

He grades really harsh and homeworks are so heavy that it's easy to fall behind. Exams are based on reasoning behind the topics and so are quizzes every week. Do not take this professor because the class is already hard and he makes it harder!
go to office hours i cant stress this enough

he's great lecturer, keeps me engaged. BUT his homework/quizzes do not align with the exams AT ALL. PLEASE AVOID THIS CLASS AT ALL COSTS, NIGHTMARE.

a good and knowledgeable professor. however you must study hard or you will fail

such a nice man. just study the slides and you will be fine!
