reviews.comment: I took Prof Chatterjee in the fall of 2015. She talked the entire class period in a low monotone voice with the help of a microphone. She never directly answered questions when she was asked. She makes your group write down all the names of their member who were in class and uses that as the daily grade so if you skip, you can't make up the points.

So this class sucked because its a big class and very very long, half the time everybody is on there phone because this women talks and a low monotone voice that puts you to sleep half the class is watching group present projects over the chapters which no on really understands to begin with so be prepared for group work and dull powerpoint class

She's got a ton of really good real world experience and is a published author on some cool topics in communication. Generally sweet and interesting to talk to personally. However, the grading is all over the place and seems arbitrary. Her instructions don't make sense week to week so it's hard to know what rubric to follow since it changes.

Never question her, she will turn it into some kind of mind game of emotional blackmail making it your fault to have questioned or some technical  rhetoric to examine your need to ask -something that you can't even believe is happening, waits to submit final grade until last min and does not provide feedback on grade unless you question

She teaches well, but she grades in ways that don't make sense. She does not round up grades at all. At the end of the semester, I needed 0.03% to have an A, and she refused to round up.  Don't need the book in class, but good to read outside of class for the tests.

Her class is really easy if you actually read the book. You will not need in class, but to study for quizzes. Sometimes the internet can help, but I would not recommend relying on it. After her individual quizzes each week, there will be group quizzes covering the same material. One big project throughout the semester, but nothing terribly hard.
it is hard class, be ready for it

There aren't any tests in this class so as long as you go the one day a week she holds group quizzes, you'll be fine. There are individual online quizzes as well but if you have the book (or even Google) you'll be fine. There's also a group project where she assigns your group so be ready to present in front of everyone.

She grades group presentations as a whole not individually, made a C- on group project because 3 of my group members did not do their part.. she assigns groups in the beginning so make sure you are all on the same page..

Group work sucks, but class is easy. NO FINAL. Grade consists of group project, and mostly quizzes. Quizzes are on two chapters that week. You take the individual online quiz over the weekend and take a group quiz on Tuesday. Really easy, since you can look up the answers.
The quizzes are online. and there is a group quiz once a week and a presentation. that's it.

I stopped going to her class on Thursdays because it was more beneficial to my grade to stay at home and study then to sit through class. READ THE BOOK! There is no way you can pass her quizzes without reading it. The drill quizzes online help also if you take those before the quizzes. First presentations get better grades also.
The grade for this class is based straight from the quizzes you take on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Lecture isn't helpful at all, make sure you read the chapters before attempting the quiz!!

Organized, laid-back, sweet, interesting, and helpful. Super straightforward class (structure is different but meant to help you learn). An 'A' is super achievable, but you have to earn it. Just pay attention in class, read the book, use the online study guides, remember your quizzes, and do the extra credit. Not a blow-off but not hard either.

If you cannot read text book prior to the class it means you are not College ready. This is not a freaking high school so be prepared to thoroughly read text book. In order to get a decent grade read text book, ask questions in class, and also try to meet her in person. Also, she offers multiple extra credits take full advantage of it. Good Look :)

No tests. Group & individual quizzes worth a lot. READ textbook. Lecture is useless. Barely any extra credit. Group quiz based of individual quiz on Tuesdays, lecture on Thursdays that no one goes to. She is an awful professor is you're lazy. NEED TO STUDY BOOK TO PASS QUIZZES. Quiz is time limited and can't go back to change answers
Dr. Chatterjee is an excellent professor. She is understanding, caring, and an overall kind person. I have really enjoyed all 3 classes I have taken of hers.

Her lectures are clear and engaging. The class size is huge (around 140), but she manages it well. Reading the book is key to preparing and doing well on the quizzes. If you make an 89.9 - Your grade is a B.

Lectures are useless. Read the book and you should pass, however the questions and answers on the quizzes can be convoluted. I can not understand why a COMM prerequisite wouldn't have more than one option for the instructor. Also, she has made some outrageous statements(ex. the Greeks didn't have written language or alphabet(not joking))

I really do not understand why everyone is rating her negatively. She is a very nice and understanding teacher. Yes, she can be boring during her lectures but that is the only issue I had. Buy the book, do the review, do the silly assignments and you'll be fine. YOU have to have the motivation to do well in her class.

Basically it goes as follows: Tuesdays you go over her lecture notes before a quiz. Take the quiz by yourself, then as a group that's randomly assigned. Thursdays you critique (or do) a presentation on a theory chosen for your group. Yes, there's a group project and it can be quite annoying depending on availability of your classmates.
Powerpoints/lectures are extremely unhelpful.READ the book and memorize the book if you want to pass. 10 Individual Quizzes, 10 Group Quiz, Presentation

I decided to change my major from Communication after this semester because of her...can't take any more of that, she clearly doesn't care about anyone but herself and her own motives, if you take her don't say you weren't warned, she is dishonest and unethical

Watch her behavior on days when she has professor in room doing her evaluation, then notice how she brings her entire class bagels when time for them to evaluate her...she knows how to play the game for her own benefit but she does NOT care about students, everything is a means to her end
The most disorganized professor EVER... Not easy to talk to at all...Must read book because she really doesn't teach... Wouldn't recommend anyone taking her

Bless her. She tried. Not clear on what she wants. Presentations won't help your quizzes so be sure to read the chapter if you want to do decent on them. Oh and pick a good group for your presentation or she will pick for you.
Worst teacher in history of teachers, so snappy and disorganized.  Do not sign up for Nessarose's class !
Ms. Nessarose is everyone's favorite!!!!!!

The class is basically self taught. You are assigned to a group then have to give a presentation over a chapter, then she grades you over how well you taught the chapter. The rest of your grades are exams over the chapter. If you show up to class, you should easily get a B.

ABSOLUTELY DO NOT RECOMMEND.  Take only if you need her class to graduate but prepare for her disorganization.  She loses papers from beginning to end of class on several occasions which means she will lose the paper you hand her before the end of class.  BEWARE
lecture is all over the place plus assignments additional to the syllabus, class material is all over the place, save yourself if you can

COM theory or any level she seems to think her job is to prepare you today for grad school,lecture is all over the place, she'll add assignments after distributing syllabus,your life will be stressful with her class
After having her for one undergrad class, she is the sole reason that I will not be pursuing a M.A. in Communication at UTA.

Her reviews are crazy long its like the entire chapters that you will be tested over are on the reviews. She doesn't have an outline SHE COVERS EVERYTHING. Her tests are applied situations and there are 40 questions with 3 tests overall. I don't know what these people are talking about. If i were you, I wouldn't take her. Attendance mandatory.
Quiz every week, but they are easy. Her lectures cover all of the material.  One major project over a movie, kind of fun.

The lectures are pretty useless and incomprehensible, she tends to just ramble on without a clear outline. She is very nice though and understanding of medical/personal absences and will allow you to make up work or re-do some work she felt wasn't up to par.  The class is pretty much self-teach though, you have to read the book.

Her class makes life difficult for no reason.The review is a compilation of the questions at the end of every chapter but she doesnt post the review until 5-7 days before the test. Do this class online or with someone easier. Life isn't meant to be painful.

She is an excellent teacher, and she cares about her students. She uses her notes and the text for her 2 tests in this class. Her tests are challenging, but as long as you finish the review and read the text you will be fine. She has her students do weekly journals, but as long as you do them its an easy 100!
She is really good teacher.  Super smart.  She is hard, but study the book and you will do good.  She have about a letter grade cushion, but don't take advantage.  I am taking her again.
she is sooo kool!! the most sweetest professor in all of UTA show up to class u will be fine.
great class...im actually taking her now...shes very easy..if you have any problems with her class, she listens :)

She was an amazing professor I would highly recommend! There were in class assignments, weekly quizzes, and only a few tests. Overall it was a really light work load. She has a way of doing notes called a "yellow word doc", this will save you and be so helpful! Overall a great professor, she was really sweet and funny and loves what she does!
Amazing! You just have to be attentive and precise to succeed with her
She speaks really fast and she moves from one topic to another very fast, if she can correct it it'd be very interesting to study with them again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The type of person who will proudly announce that she loves it when students argue with her, but gets super angry if you actually dare to challenge her on anything. Getting feedback is an ordeal that has a 70% chance of resulting in not getting any kind of answer and also feeling like I'm a terrible human being for even having to ask.

She was fine! Dont need to buy the textbook at all, used it 2 times the whole semester, lectures are some what interesting, attendance is by getting a code from her, mostly happens every monday and not wednesdays. Her lectures are recorded, quizzes every single friday, but they are all open notes and not proctored, included all the exams.

Strong chaotic ADHD vibes, but she's never boring and her lectures do a great job explaining the material. You do have to attend basically every lecture because in class activities are like 15% of the grade and she doesn't really follow the schedule, so missing 1 lecture could really hurt. Megan is cool, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: LOVE HER! She kind of reminds me of Ms. Fritz. Her lectures are easy to follow along if you read material before class (10-15 minutes go a long way). She sends out reminders for quizzes, exams, extra credit, etc. Her TA is super helpful, I enjoyed having her for lab. Even though I wanted geography, I'm actually glad I took geology because of her!
Good professor. The class is fairly easy and I'd recommend it. There is a quiz due every Friday which is pretty easy as long as you read the textbook.

Her lectures were confusing and she gave conflicting info. She said the midterm would be multiple choice and it was mostly FRQs. She was unprepared for classes, but was available to help in her office hours. The TA for this class did a good job teaching and explaining the labs, but the labs were written horribly.

I think she had interesting lectures. Some professors go on tangents that have nothing to do with the lecture, but her stories were very relevant and perfectly complimented the class. Actually, her lectures made me want to change my major to geology. Very much enjoyed her class.
Exactly what you would expect for a rock professor. Quirky, goofy, and full of exciting stories to share. Her class is always a "good vibes only" and we are here for it.
Not a horrible professor, but there are easier ones available for this course.

Very easy class. The lecture grade was 60% exams. The exams are online, non-proctored, and very easy. The quizzes were slightly challenging but they are nothing to worry about. The labs are not designed well and can be confusing, but that should not sway you from taking this class with this professor.
Great professor, she is passionate and caring.

She is always ready to respond to you emails especially during exam days. Really chaotic sense of humor which is fitting for a geology professor. Read your textbook and take your lecture notes, those are your golden tickets to passing. Got a 100 on my final exam.

You would get a weekly quiz which would be over the topic discussed in class over the week. Exams are pretty easy and are online with no lockdown browser. Mostley the quizzes and exams would grade you on the vocab learned in class.

While she is clearly knowledgable about the subject material, she also seems to be under the impression that she's doing standup routine and makes "wacky" sounds and goes on tangents about "funny" stories. She's also very passive aggressive and gets mad at legitimate questions. Oh and some tests questions aren't being covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Her passion and knowledge for structural geology is out of this world. You will come out of this class feeling like an amateur geologist with her lectures, mapping, labs, discussions, and mini field work. I can't wait to use what I've learned in this class for my future jobs and research. 2 tests (midterm and final) with generous curves.

Attendance is not mandatory but occasionally there is something called a poll that is a short quiz randomly during lectures throughout the semester. Sometimes she might go off-topic with her lectures but it isn't too bad. The exams are online and open-book. Overall a pretty good and not stressful class for majors needing to take a science credit.

Megan is a great professor! All of the quizzes and tests are not proctored and online. She has great lectures and gives great study material. The textbook isn't really necessary (I wouldn't get it). Overall I love that class.

The class is not very hard at all but Korchinski can go off on tangents unrelated to the material making it hard to keep up and stay on track. She is very nice and caring but I wouldn't recommend her as her lectures can be confusing. All tests and quizzes are a mix of lectures and book - so make sure you read.

I love Dr. Korchinski but by god this class was easy. Very fun professor to talk with. All you really need for the exams is to have the yellow words organized and accessible and you'll be golden. Online exams which are open book/note and that's all you'll need. She is a bit disorganized, but it helps break up the monotony of the lecture.
Lectures were hard to follow and not very useful for understanding the material but were helpful for exams because they go off vocab from the lectures. Communicated deadlines very well.

Professor Korchinski's class was a bit difficult. Presentations and lectures do not really follow along into the exam. The "yellow words" (vocabulary) were the only thing that was helpful to pass the exams. Only graded through a few things, quizzes, a group discussion board, and 3 major exams.
Good professor overall. Lectures are easy to follow along. Exams are a little hard, but if you study are easy

Just watch the lectures, take notes & do well on the pop quizzes. Prof. Korchinksi is in her words"Chaotic" but she'll manage in the end. She's a new professor so just be a bit patient with her sudden alterations.

The only way you could fail this class is if you don't try. Read the lectures, memorize what's necessary, do the labs and you'll pass. Lab TA's were unusually harsh graders for what was essentially fill in the blank lab assignments, but as long as you show up and turn in the work, you'll pass. Same for the lecture.
A fun teacher that kept the class engaged and was easy to talk to and get a hold of, though sometimes I felt like I wasn't fully prepared for her tests.
I'm not a great science student but Professor Megan is the sweetest and will make you excited for class. Definitely recommend her class!

She tends to go off topic during lectures, but thankfully her quizzes/tests are open note. Beware!! Sometimes the questions are something we were never taught, so just choose the best answer & hope for the best... Besides this, she's an amazing and caring person; will correct herself, add points, and apologize if you see the mistakes that she makes

Absolutely love this professor! She is super chill and makes the lectures super interesting and fun. She is so passionate about the subject and it is absolutely contagious. There's a fair bit of reading, but it's definitely doable and pairs well with the lectures. Overall, if you show up to class and pay any attention at all, it is a fun and easy A

Megan is very sweet and understanding of your circumstances. The lectures have everything you need and really help when it comes to the exams. The quizzes are easy if you take notes and pay attention to the lecture. I didnt really use the textbook because the presentations are all you need. Pretty easy class and shes theres to help!

she's a very sweet professor and really loves her job. Pay attention and take good notes of the lectures and you'll be able to pass the exams. has quizzes every week and you get two tries to do well on them.

She knows what she is talking about but goes off on unnecessary tangents during lecture, you are better off reading the book or reviewing the slides to learn the material. The quizzes and tests are easy. Has "quirky" questions in some of her quizzes. Feels more like a high-school class than anything.

Do not take for linear algebra. Tries to fit as much content as possible within the time frame, which ends up him rushing important information in the last 5 minutes. Seems brain dead when lecturing and looks like he didn't even make his notes.
Excellent Professor. Among the Best in Mathematics .He is an inspiration. I would like to take other math courses with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: His classes are highly structured, notes are impeccable, and lectures are something beyond "best". He teaches like real mathematician. Other professors just administer tests, he actually teaches. He teaches with some aroma of real math, not just problem solving. He is great professor. No body knows math more than Dr. Laurel.

He's a really good explainer. His classes and notes are super organized and easy to follow. Calc-II is a tricky class in general, but he'll make it easy to follow for you (you gotta practice tho, otherwise nobody can save you). He was amazing!

He's great with easy-to-understand lectures, somewhat caring attitude, chill and patient. His notes are pretty comprehensive and easy to follow. But he is also "don't care" type, and he is very strict about rules and regulations, and I've seen him reporting students for using the wrong calculator in the final exam to the student conduct.
Calculus 2 is a hard class no matter who you take it with, but Dr Laurel makes it fun. His lecture notes really are a lifesaver.

His lecture notes are super helpful! And the classes are actually fun and engaging because you can tell how much he enjoys what he's teaching. Dr. Laurel is very approachable, and will always make sure to solve any doubts you have. Highly recommend taking his class.

This professor was genuinely my FAVORITE professor ever. I would like to state, he's a pretty calm individual and he's young so he understands us more than some. He's very lenient and at the very beginning when everyone is getting back and at the very end where he opens all the homework's again. Honestly calc 2 was a breeze with him :)
He's really good, pay attention in class tho

Took him for calculus 1 and found him to be the perfect math professor for me. He goes quite quickly through the material, but all the information was clearly conveyed. The homeworks I was given are great practice, and I found his lectures really funny! Great intro to Calculus as someone who's never taken it before.

Best professor for Calc 3 anyday. He loves teaching the subject, and puts in a lot of effort to make his notes student-friendly. Calc 3 midterms are made by the professors, and his exams are the best by far. There are lots of opportunities for partial credit, and the MCQs are pretty doable. Super chill and funny, proud of his pHD, as he should be

Best math professor I've ever taken. Explains things in a way that even a kindergartener can understand. The homeworks can sometimes be long, but they definitely help reinforce the concepts. Would absolutely recommend.
Overall, he is good. Just go through Homework and in class pop up quiz. He is great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: So, overall he is good. But what i think is he is strictly into his lecture notes, and its kinda tough to follow the classes. I did well, but i had to read all day on weekeds to catch up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: He teaches at a fast pace, so it's important to prepare before attending class. However, he truly cares about his students. If your goal is not only to excel on exams but also to gain a deeper understanding of the material, he's the right instructor for you.

He is possibly the best math teacher you will ever meet. Knows his stuff really well. His teaching abilities are substantially powerful. Your perception to math will change he is possibly the best math teacher you will ever get at UTA. Actually UTA doesn't deserve teachers like him, he should be probably teaching at Ivy League.
Great professor ever. Remembers you and tries to teach everything.

He's a funny guy and great at explaining heavy concepts. All his lecture materials are very clearly written. He tries hard to give students a chance to succeed. The final is hard nevertheless so try doing good on the midterms.

He is a fantastic professor. Whatever grade I end up with unfortunately weighs on the departmental final and myself. He cares about his students' success and definitely shows it. If he is reading this to the class, you guys chose a great professor. Just put in your part, work hard, and keep up with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Honestly could not have chosen a better professor for calc 3 the subject is hard but he comes to class prepared with detailed notes and articulates the topic clearly. Dr Laurel stands as the BEST option for a math class at uta. overall if you want a prof who cares about you, and will really teach the topic look no further than Dr Laurel.(severance)
Great professor, tough subject. Stay caught up on the homework to be prepared for the weekly quizzes and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: No. Do not take. Wouldn't Recommend.

A great professor for suree... Comes to lecture PREPARED, explains thing reaally well, understands the material also very well, it is very comfortable to ask questions, very understanding and offers hands on assistance in labs. The TA was also wonderful and very nice. Just make sure to pay attention in lectures and do hw!

Highly recommend this professor for Calculus II. While he course is challenging, he explains the material clearly and makes it easier to understand. He also brings a positive attitude to class. Lecture notes are posted on Canvas, quiz solutions are shared afterward by the TA, and he provides helpful, thorough answers to students questions.

Dr. Laurel is the absolute best professor I've had so far at UTA! He makes an effort to get to know his students and adds personality to his lectures. I'm sad he's not teaching any of my other required math classes. You will still suffer when you take Calc II but taking it with Laurel makes it worth it!

He is easy to approach and likeable. The only con is that he teaches Calc II. There is lots of homework and the tests do make up a large portion of the grade but that's just the course itself. Overall, fun professor and would take again.

Dr. Laurel is a great professor. He talks quickly but will pause at any moment to clarify. With the pace of the lectures, he requests that detailed questions wait after class. The class is homework-heavy, but the labs are short and typically completed within the lab period. He tells you what the quizzes will be about a few days before too.

Laurel is a nice enough guy. He is incredibly antisocial and rather awkward. He knows a lot about math and the subject, however he does not explain anything. He does not prepare you for what is on the exams. If you ask a question during lecture he will make you feel incompetent. I know he means well, but he doesn't teach well.

Professor Laurel was honestly a good professor. It was kind of obvious this was his first semester teaching, but he did well. He was super open to answering any questions and helping out with homework. Lots of homework, stay on top of it. Exams were medium difficulty, make sure to study the review. One group project that was pretty easy. 9/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: For this being his first semester at UTA this dude is easily one of the best math professors I've ever had. Only person at UTA that I know of that takes time to explain concepts in class rather than skipping over 10 steps expecting us to know what happened in between. This class is still extremely hard cause it's is Cal II.

Good and entertaining lectures, but difficult to communicate with or get clear directions from. Also the website for homework crashes often, which is not his fualt, but he is not much of an extension giver when things like this happen. Also he messed up the instructions on the final project and it wasnt fixed until about 2 1/2 weeks after posting

Laurel is brand new to UTA but has very clear experience at other schools. Young, down to earth guy. Don't miss a lecture or you'll get behind EASILY. Responds to emails quickly, will help students when they see other methods to solve problems, and is overall pretty funny and a relatable person. He has a clear passion for math!

The lectures are long and boring almost impossible to stay awake during lab half of the time is just mandatory homework time that you have to wait an hour for the attendance to be taken and she over explains everything to the point where she makes things more complicated than they need to be

Mrs. Stabler is a very sweet professor, but the lectures are long and boring. Attendance is mandatory, she puts a code at the end of every lecture and lab. She uses a system called STAT coins, it can slightly boost your grade. This class is tough, especially if you don't like math. You WILL have to teach yourself. It was a miracle that I got a B.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you don't have a religon, you better get one and pray. I DREADED this class every week. I actually wished I had changed majors to avoid it. Take this anywhere else with any other professor. 99% confident the positive reviews were written by her or her own children.

Lisa is a nice lady, except the lectures do not help one bit, neither does ALEKS. You basically have to teach yourself in this course, and if you fall behind, good luck to you. Attendance is mandatory and won't be taken until the end of class. Everything that she teaches is 90% off of Excel, and you can't use that for your exams.

This professor does not compare to any of the other faculty at UTA. It is clear this job is not a priority to her. She frequently does not respond to emails, or she reads them, and admits weeks later that she forgot to do whatever you asked for. Edits and fixes incorrect info on the lecture slides during lecture. Overall just not organized at all.

Talks forever, and confuses everyone so bad, you don't know what she is trying to say. This is a retirement hobby for her, but its our education. You will hear all her life story, but not learn how to solve test problems until two days before. ALEKS is AWFUL, and does not help or work well at all!! She only has office hours right before class.

Professor talks way too much during lectures, and then only a day or two before the exam she explains how to actually solve the problems. By that point, it feels too late. There isn't enough time to study the material properly. Yes, there's ALEKS, but anyone on campus can tell you it's not the same as having a professor teach the content directly.

Nice lady, but takes way too long to explain basic concepts. Started using a new HW software this semester, and it has tons of errors and is very weird. Labs aren't hard. Non-lab days are just free time, but attendance is still mandatory, and must stay the entire time, which is absurd. She also has no history as a professor, or an instructor.

Uses aleks to complete assignments. She's really nice, but I had to learn majority of the information myself because aleks is weird. However, her lectures did help. Attendance matters, and in lab you have to do lab assignments with your group. There is also an sip assignment which was a lot of writing but not bad. Lots of extra credit.

Do not trust these other reviews like I did! Take ANY other professor! She rambles A LOT, and tries to make a joke out of everything. She takes attendance at the very end of class and lab, so you have to stay the entire time, and often there is not a lab, so you are just stuck listening to her random life stories, and her repeating the same stuff.

Mrs. Stabler is super sweet and truly cares about her students. Her reviews match about 95% of the exam, so just show up, focus on reviews, and you'll do great. I studied maybe ~30 hours total and made an A. There's a lot of homework, but it's manageable (ChatGPT helps). Dont skip out on the extra credit, it'll boost your grade a whole letter.

Although there are a lot of homework assignments, it is easy to earn good grades and there is plenty of extra credit offered. She has a very dynamic personality, and although the class itself is not interesting, she makes it a whole lot better. If you are ever confused, go to office hours and she is more than willing to help!

Lectures can be dull, but the curriculum is straightforward. With effort, passing the class is easy, and failing is unlikely. All materials are on Canvas and Pearson, and there are weekly assignments and opportunities to improve grades.

9 units with a homework assignment each and 4 exams. Exams are MCQ and 21 questions, 5 points each. He wrote the textbook and has prerecorded videos that I watch before class so I can just listen while he lectures. His lectures are very easy to follow and he breaks it down as much as he can. Very nice and energetic.

great prof, very passionate. lectures r cohesive and the practice problems he gives are what will appear on the exam. he emphasizes/repeats most important concepts, goes over problems & explains it step by step that even i (whos bad at math) understood it. js make sure to practice the textbook problems & youll be fine.

If you're looking for a class that you can understand for Chem 1441, I can't emphasize how much I recommend Dr. Rogers! He is one of the most engaging and a hilarious professor that will make sure you understand the topics he teaches. He even cracks jokes and and the atmosphere is like no other.

Before this semester, the only experience with chemistry that I had was when I failed it as a sophomore in high school. With Rogers as my professor, I was not only able to receive an A in his class, but his lectures and coursework expanded my critical thinking skills immensely. He makes great examples, practice questions, and informative lectures.
This man is national treasure!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He has online recorded lectures, in person lectures where he tells insightful and relevant stories, a really good textbook with explanations and office hours. His lectures are so organized, but he can be fast in lectures, but after you can watch his echo360 recorded lectures if you need assistance. He is very funny as well!

Professor Rogers is the BEST in the entire department. He teaches in a way that you can tell he does want us to succeed, you just have to put the work Exams are easy and similar to the book, attendence is mandatory though. go ahead and take rogers for 1441 he's like the LeBron of Chemistry.
Take this professor? A HUGE YES!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chill guy with great lectures. Tests are somewhat hard and the grading is inconsistent, which could be a fault of someone else if he has others helping him grade.
dr rogers is the founding father of chemistry. hes the best there is.
Jimmy Rogers might be the next coming of Christ.

Dr. Rogers is obviously very passionate about teaching chemistry. He tells stories in class to describe certain concepts, which are very helpful. He's also very slow paced, and while that did lag the syllabus, the GPA makes it worth it. Very nice man, just make sure to read the textbook before you ask him any questions, because he wrote it.

Please, please, please take Dr. Roger's!!! I was not looking forward to chemistry but he made it not only manageable but actually enjoyable. He is such a sweet person and was very funny in all of his lectures. He really does care about the students and is always willing to help you understand concepts. He truly cares about what he does and it shows

Dr. Rogers is an amazing professor and is passionate about what he teaches. His textbook was the most useful tool, and as long as you pay attention to the lectures and follow the textbook, you'll be set. He would often try using interesting stories to keep his students intrested and help them memorize the material. I highly recommend taking Rogers.

I enjoy his lectures. He's easy-going, chill, and his class is pretty easy. He goes on wacky tangents and is overall just a goofy guy. The exams are a lot like the practice problems in the textbook which is also nice. He has the most interesting stories to tell in class and would highly recommend if you want to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr Rogers was an amazing and very understanding professor. You can tell he cares a lot about his students and I absolutely LOVE his notes and the way he conducts lectures. Take him 100%.

I'm not a fan of chemistry and since my major is non-science so I was just taking this class as an elective. But through out the course I learnt a lot from him. Read the textbook, watch his video and study ahead and you will be fine. Exams are based of previous semesters and some questions are in his textbook. DO NOT PROCRASTINATE!!

CHEM 1441 is a difficult class no matter the professor, but I highly recommend Dr. Rogers. He's one of the kindest and most helpful instructors I've had. The class requires a lot of effort outside of lecture, but Dr. Rogers is always willing to help. The textbook isn't required, but I found it useful for reviewing and understanding key concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Chemistry is not a class you can slack on, and expect to pass. With that said, this professor in my opinion is a true gem. The practice problems in the textbook are great for studying since they are so packed with information. If you feel lost, he is more than willing to help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best Gen Chem professor at UTA I've had

Use his textbook. His test questions literally come straight from the textbook. And I would highly recommend watching his Echo360 lectures ahead of the lecture. I only go because attendance in mandatory tbh otherwise I don't see a need.
Absolutely Recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class itself has a lot of concepts to remember, but actually working the practice problems in the textbook really helps. You probably won't do very well by only studying the homework. Grades are mostly just homework, exams, and lab credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As a person who has struggled sitting in a class for years and comprehending what the teacher is saying, Dr. Rogers actually engages with students to learn. He makes it easy for students to listen to him especially when he goes on about goofy tangents. He is the type of professor that makes learning fun!
Pretty good professor. But lectures didn't really help me book and practice reviews did.

Dr. Rogers is THE professor to take for general chemistry. His exams are exactly like his practice questions in the textbook he wrote. Genuinely wants to help you understand chemistry rather than memorization. Always accessible during office hours and wants you to succeed. Wish I could have him for every chem class!

Rogers is amazing. You NEED to work through the Klein textbook. The notes he gives are good but not enough to score well on the exams, especially if you want an A. Start studying for the exams 2-3 weeks before because most of your grade is based off of them. He typically offers extra points (graded out of 110). You can get an A if you study well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rogers is a great professor. 4 midterms and a final. Tests are exactly what he teaches in class. He wrote the textbook. Lecture notes are amazing. Very organized. HOWEVER, you HAVE to put in the work, or else you won't pass. Study 2-3 weeks before midterms. Make use of practice exams. Final replaces lowest test grade. Do not procrastinate... EVER.

Your only grades are the 3 exams (final is comprehensive & optional) and attendance (5%). But you will want to attend lectures if you aren't familiar with chem like me. I dropped the class due to it being my first time studying chem & I didn't want to ruin my GPA, but I am retaking it with him. He provides MANY resources. Best chem prof at UTA imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A passionate and experienced teacher. He explains the material thoroughly which sometimes causes us to fall behind (but he omits what he doesn't teach on the test). But because there is so much to be covered, this class requires a lot of self-teaching/memorization (something I did not grasp). Make sure to take advantage of all resources he provides

reviews.comment: This course is hard, but the prof. It's super nice. Make sure to practice every day. The lecture won't help you retain info, in my opinion, it's only to introduce the material. You need to be reading the textbook and doing the practice problems; otherwise, you will bomb the tests. Four midterms come sooner than you think, so don't fall behind

This class is hard. The professor is only there to make it easier, which he does. His lecture videos and notes are the best thing ever and only make class easier. He does explain things so nicely, but for the class, you have to do all the practice problems from Rogers videos and the Klien Textbook. For exams, study atleast a week before, it is HARD

reviews.comment: While the prof. was very nice, I found his style of lecturing to be difficult to follow. He tends to get off topic, trying to make a connection between real life and chemistry, usually failing. Often did not finish topics which would be taken off exam. But study his textbook and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Roger's General Chemistry I class during my first semester of college. He is the absolute best and has exceeded any expectations I could have had. He is personable, sets out clear expectations, and does everything in his power to ensure that you will be prepared to do well on your test. His lectures are also genuinely entertaining. 10/10

Took this class a while back, so I can only really speak for him back then. OChem is a difficult class, but Dr. Rogers made it easy. His after-lecture quizzes forced me to stay on top of things, and he had plenty of study material. Even if you did miss class, he doesn't deviate from the textbook. Overall, the gold standard for chemistry professors.
Professor Rogers is great at making a tough class understandable. Attending lectures and using resources like unstuckstudy ai are key to doing well. Expect to put in serious effort, but it pays off.

Dr. Rogers is very knowledgeable & has an extensive background in chemistry, however, it feels like he expects everyone else to as well. His lectures are very organized, but often a bit too advanced for beginners. He explains things as if everyone is on his level. If he could slow down and simplify things more, it would be easier to follow along.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor with lots of knowledge. He wrote the textbook that was used in class, so as long as you complete the problems in the book and the practice exams, you'll do great. The test questions are exactly the same format as the textbook. Chem is not an easy course, so you have to be willing to study and work. Lots of extra resources are given.

The most organized professor I have ever seen. Not a single person who left a negative review actually put effort into the class. If you ask anyone who has taken Rogers, you will only hear good things about his class. He's clear to follow through with his lecture notes and gives students more study material than any other professor.

No complaints about the prof - straight forward and if you do the practice exams he throws you a bone and sometimes a question is on the test. Also very available if you need to see him, for those with a dense working schedule. If you suck at MC questions, prepare for those - tests are a majority of points there, including the final.
Terrible. Would not take again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly I was really intimidated about taking Organic Chemistry, but he is a great teacher, you are ACTUALLY learning! My tip is, read the textbook for things you are struggling with, and make sure to do the practice problems in the textbook. Make sure you do ALL the lecture note questions as well as the past exam questions.

To get 100's on exams which is very possible, you need to not only memorize the rules of the chapters in full detail, but also and more importantly be able to apply the rules to the questions you practice prior to exams. If you memorize the rules only, you will get a C or D at best. Do not slack or you will not understand the following chapters.

Rogers is simply the best. Kind, caring, approachable, and really wants the best for his students. He does expect you to know that material, so don't expect a free A. But he's such a great teacher that an A is attainable, even in such a famously difficult course. Built in bonus points on exams, final replaces the lowest, etc. Take him.

Dr. Rogers is probably the best chemistry professor in the department and truly cares for his students. He's very straightforward about what will be on the test and what subjects you should take notes on for future endeavors (i.e., MCAT, DAT, etc.). He is also always open to questions and wants to ensure you understand the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers is a great professor. A lot of people here fail to mention that the exams he gives have built-in additional points. Meaning you could score higher than a 100, sometimes, as high as a 120. Dr. Rogers is also very clear and understanding and very easy to meet with outside of class. This course does require lots of studying and practice!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Just as a general note, this class requires a lot of practice. He is clear with the material as he can be, was always willing to meet me outside of office hours (I work a lot), and has sat through my frustration with material. He tries to make the class fun, and wants you to do well. You honestly have to practice the concepts in order to do well.

He is great at lecturing & telling u exactly what to do to pass the class BUT gives absolutely no curves like other professors do & as they should, will take off points wherever he can, and adds in more material to know in his lectures than the textbook goes into. Very difficult, not impossible, but just take another professor, Rashidat or Foss!

Dr. Rogers is easily the greatest professor I have ever had. Although OChem 1 is a very difficult course, he ensures that he prepares his students. He even developed his own lecture notes so that you can easily follow along. Echo360 videos were SO helpful. Work as many practice problems as possible and ATTEND CLASS! It's hard, but not impossible!

The exams will test whether or not you really understand the material. He is serious when he suggests doing all the practice problems and watching any extra videos available on canvas. Gives a lot of little tips and repeats the important parts until they come to you naturally. Very approachable and funny, great class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers is an amazing professor! I took him for both of my gen chem classes. He wrote the textbook and he writes the tests, so the practice problems in the book are very good at preparing you for the test. Chemistry classes are a lot of work in general, but Dr. Rogers keeps it very straightforward. You can also tell that he really cares!

One of the best professors I've ever had. He manages to make a notoriously difficult course so clear and understandable. He doesn't try to make things difficult. His goal is always to ensure you have a good foundation before building up on content. There are things I never grasped in an entire year of gen chem that he can easily clarify in minutes.

One of the most amazing professors at UTA. Really cares about his students and knows how to teach his material in a way that students can understand. Has great lectures with fill-in-the-blank notes and a textbook he wrote himself. He's head of the department for a reason. The tests were tough because he required you to fully understand the content.

Rogers honestly is a really good professor his class is just a bit of a cluster, test scores and averages specifically will be all over the place there is no true learning it's more memorization and if you don't memorize those formulas or compounds the final will hunt you down.
Excellent professor

Although Ochem 1 kicked my ass, Rogers was honestly a great teacher. He is really passionate about what he teaches and wants his students to learn. This course relies heavily on test grades, so I wouldn't miss any lectures, but also be sure to read the book. He prepares you very well for the final exam so you feel ready for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff but he doesnt really care about his students, feels a bit like he has this god complex and gives attitude when you go to his office hours.

Dr. Rogers is an ANGEL. Very caring guy who loves the material and knows it really well (he wrote the textbook). It's pretty challenging stuff but he makes it enjoyable. Be ready to be present and pay attention. Do your work and you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers is one of the best professors in the Chemistry department. His lectures are very clear and he has his notes printed out which you can buy at the bookstore. He demands a lot of time from his students but if you just watch his lectures and fill out the notes, you will be ready for the exams and can easily pass this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you care about your GPA at all, steer clear from Dr. Rogers. While he is a nice enough guy, he does not care if his students succeed. He does not curve even when more than 50% of the class failed. At the end of the semester, 20 students had dropped the class and half of the students failed.

He is an amazing professor but makes you work for your grade. Make sure to watch lectures, do homework as well as read the textbook. If you want an easy A then take someone else, however, if you actually want to learn and challenge yourself then he's the one to take. Teaches you everything and is funny too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chem II is quite the hassle especially if your chem knowledge isn't the best. Luckily, Jimmy really goes into depth in his lectures. This man wrote the freaking chem textbook so he is the best UTA has to offer. He is also quite funny with his cringe jokes. Don't be afraid to ask for help regarding specific concepts he is there for ya! 11/10 burgers

1442 is much tougher than 1441, but my grade was almost a letter higher in 1442 thanks to Dr. Rogers. He is by far the best professor I have had at UTA so far. He is anything but boring, very nice, and quick to emails. Watching his optional practice problem videos are crucial. My other chem prof. provided no such thing. Do not take this for granted

You won't do well in this class unless you reduce the number classes you're taking or if you already have a strong handle on the material. Its unfair how many topics and formulas he makes you memorize, the amount of hw you get, and how fast paced this class is. It really caters to people who already know the material and not regular students.

I am absolutely awful at chemistry but Rogers explains it in a way that is digestible. Notes are very clean and plays an important role in your comprehension so keep up with them. Lectures seem super long but absolutely none of it is redundant. Cuts the fat out of learning and gets straight to the point. Please take him. Please.
Tough class. You WILL have to put in a lot of work for an A. Dr. Rogers is an excellent Professor. If your goal is to do well then start immediately. Procrastination and cramming will NOT work.

Such a sweet man! Chem is hard anyways so do not slack off, one of the best out there, he is the head of the chem department for a reason. 4 exams and quizzes, one gets dropped in the end. All is provided, its just you who has to do the actual work and study for it! Slacking off will not get you passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Too many topics, rushes like crazy, and if you're taking any number of classes, you will have a hard time passing. The only people I knew who did well either went to good schools or are retaking .

Don't listen to others that say, if you work hard you will pass. This is the the hardest class I have ever taken in my entire life, calc 2 was easier. Tough lab and homework/exams. Professor is awesome, but course requires memorization of every single material you ever learn or you will fail badly. Try at a community college. Engineering major btw

Very difficult class. If planning on taking other challenging courses along with this, good luck. Labs are almost a whole separate class and the amount of work you get it overwhelming. Kind of difficult being able to pass due to everything online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rogers is a good professor and person. You'll actually learn in his class because there is no other way to pass. Each test is based on the type of questions in the back of the lecture notes and textbook (which he writes himself), so make sure to practice. He is the best chem professor in the whole department.

Overall I think his class is quite easy. It's true that I receive a B in his class, which is due to the fact that his test time is too short, but overall if you write your note, read the textbook to do the problem, you should be fine.

A very good guy and a hella capable teacher. Knows his stuff. The issue however, is the class itself. There's WAY too much material, WAY too much cramming, and the lab I had to deal with was an absolute nightmare. Unless you've had a very good experience with chemistry in the past, prepare for hell. DO NOT TAKE if you even *think* you're not ready.

reviews.comment: Wastes class time and rushes through material then overwhelms students with hw. Should be teaching high school

Dr. Rogers is the best professor in the chemistry department. His lectures are amazing! He uses his own textbook which makes it that much better. He tells you exactly what to prepare for and he is very kind about answering questions. He also mentions what topics will show up again in more advanced classes. He is very passionate about teaching.

Say goodbye to your grade if you are taking multiple classes. Unless you already have a strong foundation in genchem then it's going to be an uphill battle the entire time in this class. Covers an unreasonable about of info and makes you memorize a ton of formulas. There are better profs
Lectures are a waste of time. Study independently because he covers too much information to get anything worthwhile from lecture. Rude during office hours. Overall a mediocre professor

Probably the worst prof I've taken at UTA. overwhelms you with topics and shoves you off when you ask for help. Tries to treat your time like his class is the only one you're taking. Wastes students time

I loved his class. Chem 1341/1342 is Chem for Chemistry majors, and he was really great. Funny and really good at teaching. Does go a bit fast. Overall, you have to study. Go to SI sessions if available, and find study group. Lots of resources to study from, including old exam q's, which he uses to make tests. Got A's for both classes.

Definitely read the book and do those practice problems!

reviews.comment: Drowns you in busy work so you hardly have time to study for exams. If you're wanting to make a decent grade in this class while taking 3 or more other classes then get ready for misery. Worst time waster of any professor I've taken at UTA

I took Dr. Rogers for Gen Chem 1, 2 & organic chemistry (during COVID-19 online structure). He is so kind and will help you in any way that you need it!! He loves teaching and loves chemistry so he shows that through his lectures. He is going to make you work for your grade and you have to do A LOT of problems, but it will be worth it in the end!

reviews.comment: Best chemistry professor ever, such a great professor he will teach you everything the proper way and actually cares about you learning rather than just throwing a bunch of tests at you for simply having grades

reviews.comment: Gives way too much busy work. Wastes all your time that should be used studying for exams
Jerk anytime you ask any questions. Tests are not reasonable. Talks down to students and basically says you're stupid if you can't understand a new topic right away.

Rude during office hours. Gives too much work and tests you on concepts he doesn't cover in lecture. Hardly anyone even finishes the exams on time because he gives way too many problems. Just a bad prof who is making a FRESHMAN level course more complicated than it needs to be. Should be teaching highschool.
Too much information. Talks 100mph and hasn't finished a lecture on time once. There are better, more more realistic professors or there when it comes to work load.

Lectures and midterms are super detailed that you end up never studying enough. Don't expect an A unless it's the only class you're taking or already have a great handle on the material. Terrible class and professor. Too many topics , too little time.

Terrible professor that overloads students with too much work. This is only a 3cr class plus lab but if you want to make an A you will be spending 7+hrs a week on the HW plus lecture and anything else he randomly pulls out of the air. Then you need to spend another 2-3hrs a week on lab reports. NOT REALISTIC for any normal student. Waste of time

Great professor! If you go to class and follow along with lectures you will get most of your studying done for exams. The online homework is tedious but if you do a little everyday its not too bad to keep up with.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Ignore the bad reviews, they're just petty they didn't get the grade they wanted. He has so many resources outside of his lectures that could help such as old exams that he reuses, a textbook that is exactly how the lecture is ordered, and quick replies to emails. Your attendance is around 5% of your grade so technically its mandatory.
He is an awesome lecturer. if you go to his class and practice the problem as he says you can easily get an A.

HW are due weekly and he occasionally willing to move the due date. His test are FREE RESPONSE but he does give partial credit so I would recommend doing all the practice problem in the book and having a decent understand of the concept behind it. I know it seen like a lot of work but this will be the foundation for your later year in chemistry.
Fills your times with busywork online-HW that takes forever and not even related to the exams. Wastes your time when you should be studying for exams , labs, and other classes.

Only people who were doing reasonably well retook once or twice or already had a very strong handle on the info. Unreasonable work load and does not prepare you well for the final. If you just want to pass, you will pass, but if you're going for an A get ready to sacrifice your entire life for this one class. Miserable experience.
So glad I switched to a diff prof.. Rogers is a good prof but there's just too much for what is only a 3cr class.

All memorization.. memorize formulas, memorize trends, memorize terminology, memorize bond orbitals and angles. Jam-packs the semester with so much info & HW you can't do anything but resort to memorization. On top of that, he picks the trickiest questions for exams strictly aimed at screwing you up. Literally the worst professor I've had at UTA

Very hard class due to sheer volume and memorization. The lecture will not help with the exams but attendance is mandatory. Additionally, you will have a lot of trouble trying to figure out your grade because of all of the components. I don't recommend this prof unless you already know the material or aren't taking too many classes.
Worst instructor I've had at UTA by far. Unreasonable and unrealistic workload. Expects you to memorize a lot of material including all the formulas.
Over half the class fails the exams. Too much material, too little time. Bad professor

The worst. Piles way too much work on you. Out of touch with how long it takes to do all this stuff AND find time to study for exams. Lectures at 100mph because he tries to cram way too much info on you. Take someone else

You won't make better than a C if you're taking this class with two other classes. Overloads you with busy work then wonders why students aren't doing too well. There are better profs out there but if all you want is a C then Rogers is OK.

Rude in office hours, talks down to people, and tries to trip up students with odd information not in the book and hardly covered in lecture. There are much better profs who aren't out to ruin your gpa

Chem 2 is much more difficult than chem 1 and Rogers makes that clear. If you do all the practice problems and UNDERSTAND them a few times then you will be fine. The review sessions and the chem clinic are some great ways to do well. Even though chem 2 itself isn't great, Dr. rogers is the best prof to get you through it. There is still aleks.

reviews.comment: This is supposed to be an entry level chemistry course but he treats it like you need to be a master to pass, average for his first 2 tests are in the 50 percentile. reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers is hands down the best chemistry professor. He assures that the students actually master the material they're learning. Go to class, read the book, do the practice problems and you're set.

reviews.comment: Prof Rogers is the best at his job. This class does have quite a work-load but it's manageable. Just put in your best effort, go to class, do LOTS of practice problems, do ur best in lab and read the textbook, IT HELPS. I managed to get a high B while taking anatomy and physio class so it's possible to do really well if you try your absolute best!!

The worse professor I've had by far. Overloads students with junk work. If you don't have 10-15 hours a week to do the online HW, book problems, practice exam problems, and CONTINUOUSLY review old material weekly, PLUS another 5 hours a week for lab, prelabs, post labs, and lab reports, then there is no way you're earning a reasonable grade.
He is an awesome professor

Pros: good lectures, really caring, and if you can do the practice tests you can do the actual test. Cons: sometimes tells stories, gets behind, ALEKS online homework, and lab is really ahead of lecture. Tips: Work wayyy ahead

Very well spoken and enthusiastic. SI sessions are clutch. Gave multiple resources for additional help. Has practice exams, practice problems in book, practice problems in notes and videos of him working through all of them one on one. Concise notes packet. I hated Aleks with a BURNING passion but it taught me a lot. Best Professor!!!! So adorable!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr Rodgers is an extremely fair professor. If you read the textbook and pay attention in class, there is no question you should get wrong on any exam. He gives you ample resources and practice questions that nearly mirror what he asks on thetests. Overall, I would recommend anyone to take his class. If you want to get an A,just work at it. you will

Hands down the worst professor I've had in college. There is no way you can do all the book problems+onlineHW+practice exams in time for exams. Tack on the lab reports and anything for your other classes and you basically become a hermit. I think he's confused - this is a freshman Genchem course and not an honors class or upper level chem.
Wastes you time with a bunch of busy work then crams everything at the end of the semester. Take someone else if you value your grade and your time.

Yes he gives lots of homework on ALEKS, but ALEKS is department wide so he has no choice in that matter. Even if he did,it is benificial to do the problems for practice. If you want a good grade in here YOU HAVE TO READ THE TEXTBOOK AND WORK ALL OF THE PRACTICE PROBLEMS! Look. Rogers wrote the book. He also writes the tests. So do the book problems
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers is one of the best professors at UTA. He makes chemistry interesting. Don't listen to those who are giving him a bad review based on how much ALEKS is assigned, every professor gives out ALEKS homework, so it's unavoidable regardless of the professor you take.

Dr. Rogers is one of the best professors I ever had at UTA. I've taken chemistry before, and I didn't understand a lot of the material in the past until I took his classes. He explains everything well, and is always available to help out his students. I found his fill-in-the-blank notes and problem sessions to be very beneficial study tools.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You might as well study and do all the problems a week ahead of lecture because the lecture is always behind lab. It's a good waste of 3hrs a week but points deducted if you don't show up. It is what it is.

Perfect if you live at home and don't have a job, otherwise this professor isn't for you. He will overload you with non-tested online work until your eyes bleed. He is definitely filtering out students who don't have 20 hours a week to blow on one class because the sad truth is none of the material is difficult at all.

Buy the Aleks, buy the iclicker, buy the notes, buy the book, pay for exam practice sessions. Spend 8 hours a week on forced, unrelated online HW. Spend "a minimum of 2-3 hours" a week doing prelabs, lab problems, and a weekly lab REPORT. When is anyone supposed to find the time to do the actual, TESTED, book problems? Hope you don't have a job

Exams are based on the book problems and not the Aleks(online HW), yet you have to spend so much time doing Aleks that you never have enough time to get to the book problems or practice exams. Overloads students with junk work. It would be an easy A if it's the only class you take, but the workload is unreasonable otherwise.

Dr. Rogers was great, actually. The grad-level questions on his exams are structured the SAME way in the textbook and the back of our notes. The practice problems in the textbook are a perfect example of what your tests will look like. Practice those until you dont need to look at the step-by-step procedures and youll pass the exams :)

reviews.comment: Dr. Rogers was easily my favorite professor for my first semester at UTA. He was clear on grading. He made jokes every now and then to keep the class interested. Go to class, read the book, solve practice problems and you should be fine. Lab & Aleks are the worst of this class, however he isn't in charge of either. This class is NOT easy & very overwhelming, however Dr. Rogers is the best

His lectures aren't as bad as everyone makes it seem, you spend A LOT of time on ALEKS for homework and his tests are a bit tricky. But CHEM 1442 is a weed out class so it is going to be hard, just put in the effort to read the textbook and do the practice problems and you'll be set for the class.
Tests are difficult and wastes so much of your time on HW making it hard to study for the tests.

THIS CLASS IS SO HARD!! Let me repeat... HARD! Don't get me wrong, out of all the professors, he's the best. However, the tests are ridiculously hard. Don't even get me started with the final.
