Great lecturer. Definitely recommend taking him for any course. Made one of the most dreaded courses in the program enjoyable. His assignments are difficult, but he's fair and loves to give out partial credit. Attend lecture and put effort into the homework and you'll be prepared for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He canceled class at least once every week. Was more concerned with his full time job, which is understandable, but don't take the responsibility of class if you can't make it. Didn't seem to grasp the material and couldn't explain assignments well. Wasn't knowledgeable of policies. If you want to learn, don't take this professor.

Health policy was a bust. Over half of the classes were canceled by the professor - sometimes last minute causing people to commute to campus for no reason. Professor was never prepared to teach the material. When he did "teach" it was through youtube videos. Graded easy - but did not appear to actually read the work turned in.

Christopher Avila seemed very uninterested in teaching Seminar II. He gives off a vibe as if he does not want to be there. He gets annoyed when you ask him questions, and does have an attitude at times. He also takes his time in responding to emails, if he responds at all. His people skills are lacking big time. Easy class, crappy professor.

Avila seemed he could care less about our seminar class, since he is a adjunct. He never commented on our required internship journals. Feedback on things was minimal. Was on his phone during class presentations, if he can't even be respectful of students present, what can be expected of other classmates.  Attitude problem btw.
Really enjoyed his class. Was really kind, funny and helpful and genuinely wants to see students succeed. Take him if you can

Professor Atkins is a really understanding professor, he gives good feedback as long as you go find him in person because he isn't good at responding through email and such lol. I love his class and his humorous teaching style.

Very chill dude. For an intro-level course, his class lifted some weight off my already heavy workload. As long as you already know how to write essays and cite sources correctly, you will easily get an A.
He was really cool and chill throughout the semester and very understanding. He is lenient with late submissions and is always willing to work with you. Take him if you can!

Although he moves at a quick pace, he teaches the material well. He engages with students, wants us to learn. However towards the end of the semester he sort of flew by topics and held a few classes online. HW was given through an online site for all Cal 1 courses, it is almost the same problems as the Exams. Opened all HW till last day of class.

Hands down the best math professor UTA has to offer! He's one of those rare professors that have so much passion for the subject, it lights up the room. I don't like math, but I truly looked forward to his lectures. Super flexible with labs/quizzes/homework and wants everyone to succeed. I sincerely recommend you to experience Dr. Atmai's class.

Best professor ever, yes its some times hard to catch up with his lectures but he records them and you can always go to office hours. He will explain everything and makes sure you under the material. He is super flexible for the homework, labs and quizzes. He even lets you correct them for a better grade. I WOULD RECOMMEND HIM!

reviews.comment: I took a calculus class before this. Atmai is the friendliest guy you'd ever meet. I enjoyed calculus, and he wants to share that same enjoyment. Professor Atmai wants you to pass his class. Math can be a challenging subject but he will put in the effort to help you pass if you ask him. Overall he very good teacher who is very knowledgeable about his subject and I highly recommend.

He puts so much time into his students. I wish I could have him as a professor for every class. There is absolutely no way you listen to lectures and do the homework and not get an A/B. Yes, CSE 1310 was tough; I took the course last semester (Fall 2016) when he was still teaching it. If you're considering taking a graduate course with him, do it. His teaching style isn't the best (explains the 4/5) but he will give you the resources you need to succeed. Got a B in his class and will pass with an A in CSE 1320.

Professor Athitsos is one of the best professors I've had so far. Professor Athitsos is very clear on what he wants and how things should be done. The homework he gives is very precise and gives you plenty of practice. He doesn't expect you to have everything memorized and allows you to bring any resources you want to the exams. Great lecturer.

The worst professor ever. He made me hate Artificial Intelligence and anything related to it because of his bad teaching skills and unclear lectures. Horrible teacher. His tests are brutal. He teaches one and gives tests really hard. If this is your first computer science course, I wouldn't recommend him he makes you think you are not fit for that field. Looks like have to retake the course.

Great guy. Helps you whenever you need. Most likely to curve the final grade by almost a letter (But that's cuz his grading is really tough). Would totally recommend him if you wish to solidify your programming concepts for the future.

Takes the lowest of HW & test grade as final average. HW via comp, tests written (no comp) but open book. Gives simple examples and throws out intense HW problems. 16 week course. 12 assignments all two parts; a very difficult programming assignment and a insanely difficult written part usually around 7 problems each with 3-5 parts. he is inspiring and motivational. this class was much more than i could ever ask for. loved every bit of it. i do not understand the rating. he's exams are fairly easy if you pay attention in class.

I barely understand. The pain was that he taught us just typing on the word documents before finals. So hard to understand. don't take if you want to learn easily.

I took this class this summer. As the class says, it is intro, but it is not. It was so hard class. This professor is very hard. It is very hard to pick his lecture. Worst class I have ever taken.  Try taking other professor. Homeworks are super hard.  It says into class, but it is not intro, it is crazy class. Dont take with him.

Anybody crying about how tough he is means they expect an easy A. This class is not an easy A. You will learn and you will be satisfied. Attendance is essential.

Vassilis is the kind of professor for people who actually want to learn. If you are taking this class only because you have to, you will not have a good time with him. He also is willing to talk about test/assignment answers and change grades, and gives a huge curve.

Very hard professor, but very smart, he will asked high level of knowledge. Sometimes he will answer you with another question, he will put trick questions on test. This was not an easy class.  He is a great professor but you cannot slack off an expect to know what is going on.  He focuses on making sure you know what you are talking about instead of just being able to go through the motions.

Professor is pretty tough. His tests and homework are pretty rigorous. Some homework take 15+ hours and usually wont help with them until after they are due. He DOES curve but if you are still failing at the end of the day you will NOT be bumped to passing.He is pretty smart, knows his stuff but expects to put you on his level of thinking.
Horrible professor! Doesnt teach! Expects you to know everything. Doesnt curve. Doesnt know his own answers to his homework questions he has to look at the solution manual to find the answer.
He assume you knows everything in C. If you forgot or do not know everything or most in c, just drop or take another prof.

Run for you life! He makes the class super tough, expects you to know everything. This is an introductory class he makes it theoretical and he makes his own test question that don't make sense and are super long. you will regret if you take it with him.
he expects you to be a super genius. He really makes you do a lot of work. He don't want to teach. He really needs to think being a student willing to learn.
I really enjoyed the course. It was challenging and had lots of assignments and a project but I learn't a lot. Very helpful and motivating professor.
Not obsessed with the language but emphasizes how important the concepts are. One of the most articulate teachers I've had so far. Very helpful. Would definitely recommend everyone take for CSE 1310.

He was very helpful. Not very lenient on homework assignments, so turn them in on time. He considered my 75 to be a B. Overall great teacher. A lot more helpful than programming professors I've had in the past. All tests are open book/open note.

My main concern was that prof didn't care about his students at all and his TA's were horrible. I learned everything from books, online examples, chegg and even evening labs did not help. Tests were disorganized and without webcam which cost many students' exams to be evaluated by student conduct and almost everyone is facing some cheating issues.

I was not happy with the format of the class. The class meetings were purely practice problems. No lecture. This professor was also terrible about responding to emails and was often not helpful to students.

Professor Athavale was a good professor but like many of the 1250 ENGR teachers did not necessarily 'teach' during his lectures rather than go over examples. Watch Dr. Ewing's videos before class so that you are able to practice the examples in class. The test are pretty simple as long as you study a day or two beforehand.

Mr. Ateek is now at Collin College. I cannot express how much an inspiration he is as a human being. I learned a lot thru our discussion based classes. There are barely assignments this is a free A class. This is acceptable to me because the things I learned in this class cannot be measured by a test score.
Professor Ateek is an amazing teacher.  He is very kind, has great stories, and genuinely cares about the field of social work.  I highly recommend him! :)
He is passionate about social work and has lots of very interesting experiences.  More interested in helping us to be social workers than drilling material into us for testing!
I've taken Ateek for Group Counseling Methods and Couples Counseling. I learned alot and I will take him again.
No Comments

Dr Cindy is carng, kind, and a tough cookie! She'll listen, let your cry on her shoulder, and make sure all the while you earn your grade. She talks a lot. She is an amazing teacher and loves her students and her job. probably too much too much, you'll see what i mean... you must take her for the internship class! easy A, easy upper level hours, you don't even have a class to attend but 2-3 times, and she will do anything she can to help out.

Easily the best teacher in the department, and may be the only one soon, as the dean is trying to run off all the faculty. She is extremely helpful, will stay after class or meet elsewhere to help you. Very understanding and wants to see her students excel.

If we were to get personal, there are all kinds of negative things I could say about her. However, none of them have to do with her class or her teaching, which is on the level. "...." that's all I have to say.
Great teacher. Lots of energy and excited to help students out. You'll do well if you turn everything in on time and go to her with questions if you are confused.

Professor Awe is one of the best professors of statistics. She is very thorough and cares about her students. She helped and gave students several opportunities to improve their grade. I really enjoyed her class

She seems annoyed every time you visit her office for questions on the materials. Her reviews are nothing like her Exams. Her exams are difficult and lectures are confusing. She went over the materials really fast and expect you to know it. It doesn't help that she has a very strong accent. GPA killer! STAY AWAY!

Awe is a good person but NOT a good teacher.  Don't take her for bstat3321, her exams are nothing like her lectures or reviews!  If you take her plan putting in work to make an A on the first exam, if you don't you will struggle throughout the semester.  GPA killer, difficult exams, not clear on lectures, long lines outside her office for help!

She is very nice, responds to emails quickly, and stays after class to answer questions. But I would NOT reccommend taking her. She moves really fast and gives you a lottttt of information. Hw is easy but not on the test, and the test are very tough and tricky. Avoid her if possible. The class is doable though if it's your last option.

Run for your life!! I am a 4.0 student and got a c in this class. Her reviews are nothing like her tests. She crams way too much information into an hour session, and slows down for no one. Talks to you like your an idiot. Homework was super easy but none of it was on the tests.

Awe is a great teacher, but her tests are very hard. She gives great informative lectures and is very helpful. Her reviews are very easy compared to her tests and don't often correlate towards her exams. You get to work in groups for homework, which is only 20% of your grade. Final is cumulative.

Passionate and informative
Good stuff!!!
This is one of the best professors I have taken in my college life. I have developed a very keen interest in operations management after taking her class.

Easy class !,Tests are open ended but just go over the HW problems and you should do fine and few concepts but focus on hw problems. one pg cheat sheet, lectures are boring, you don't need the book at all, all the material is on the slides. I would recommend her for Opma
Very good professor.  Explains all concepts slowly and clearly.  See her during her office hours and she will always be willing to help you understand anything.  Tests are relatively easy. Made an A.

I have heard lots about how difficult this class is, but Professor Awe made it so simple that you wouldn't regret taking Operation Management. Just go for her if you want to get good grade on this course. Attendance is mandatory and assignment is of essence for each exams. Just go for her she is the best.
Not really good at teaching, had to teach myself. The exams are written so be ready to memorize. She doesn't curve.

I didn't originally plan to take this class. During one of the exams, I noticed what appeared to be two students cheating, but it did not seem to be addressed. reviews.comment: She responds to emails very quickly, which is a big plus. Overall, she is nice and clearly cares about the class. However, her grading system does not match Canvas and is usually about 10 points lower, so if you think you're earning an A based on Canvas, you may end up with a B. She can sometimes come across as very assertive.
The professor is friendly and delivery of course content is best as she makes you understand the concept with interactive sessions.

This class hit me like a cold brick wall. Just the level of difficulty this class was just unimaginable, and had I knew I would've dropped it the first week of class. The calculations are so long that they take up probably a couple of pages. Tons of hws, 3 midterms, a final, and a long project. I would not encourage you to take this course.

Average class. Aside from the fact UTA decided to cram 108 students in a tiny room, the lectures were just so dragged out and boring. He is a great professor. HE IS THE BEST PROFESSOR AT UTA! HE ACTUALLY TEACHES THE CLASS!  I wish all of the professors were like him. He is THE BEST of THE BEST! I don't understand why the other professors are not like him! HE IS THE BEST! <3

Bless for all. BEST OUT OF BEST ONLY IF YOU WANNA TO HAVE AN A FOR A CLASS.
HE IS THE BEST! I passed his class with an A. HE IS JUST AWESOME!

Really great professor.. Very easy.. If you just study his review you will pass his class. And less homework. Take him. Easy A :)

I would recommend her class. She makes the material interesting. A lot of reading though!

No Comments

There's 3 big units with 3-4 chapters in each one, and each chapter had their own quiz questions (use quizlet for these) and written assignments. She gives you a lot of time to finish each unit, and also gives you a couple of opportunities for extra credit.

This online course was more involved than other online courses I've taken. Each chapter has a few quizzes with required written responses, and it's all accessed very easily. Extra credit is offered at the end of each unit. You can learn quite a bit in her course! Exams are a little difficult, so utilize the practice quizzes!
I took her online, but she is very friendly and accessible. She made sure that everyone was on board for her class constantly.

I love Prof Baldridge. I've taken her classes before and they're easy and actually help you learn. This class is like all her other classes. Quite a few assignments are due every week but split them up and it's easy. Quizlet is your friend and she gives a lot of extra credit so you can get ahead.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great Prof! The class was async online and easy. Quizlet is your friend. There's a lot of lessons and work but if you manage your time well and do a little bit each day you will do very well in the class. The tests were easy as well. There is a textbook but I barely used it and still did well. She gives a lot of extra credit too if you need it.

She is organized and gives lots of reminders for due dates. She is clear about grading criteria. The textbook/weblink was a mandatory purchase, and all HW/quiz/exams were completed through there. You have to read the chapters, note key terms/concepts and then take MC quizzes. The four unit exams are proctorio, the final is open-book proctorio.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This course is very book heavy. I studied the lectures like crazy and still did terribly on the tests. After I started really studying the book, I did somewhat better. I feel like my effort toward the class is not accurately reflected in my grade. Try not to wait to the last minute when you're managing your own Unit work. You need time to study.

SUPER easy course! The course had 3 units, and each entire unit would be due on a certain day. With time management (doing one chapter a week), the pace of the course is very slow and easy. Coursework and exams are on McGraw Hill connect. Lots of the questions can be found on Quizlet. The professor was very communicative despite this being online.

This is a super easy class for an A. 
The material is split into three modules which you have several of time to complete at your own pace. It took me about two weeks to finish one module if I dedicated my time to it. Left me with a lot of free time. Easy assignments.

Material is VERY dense so please make time to read the PPTs and book. Having access code is VERY important or you will fail (code comes with the book on McGraw Hill). Theres always extra credit, but still try in class, bc u might just get an A. Teacher is always responsive, so get to know her! I learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Shes really cool as she just administers the class really. She gives extra credit through every unit. Which really helps. You must put in the work to complete it. Its reading while answering questions, an activity, and a quiz for each chapter. Will require you buying McGraw Hill book. Take her if you wont procrastinate as there are deadlines.

The course is taken at your own pace with deadlines for each unit. Homeworks take about a hours. There quizzes and some book modules as well to complete. The only thing that is on lock down browser are the exams. There are 4 and one final comprehensive. Psyc is not field of study so it never really appealed to me and with some to letter effort pass

This class is not hard, unless you procrastinate. She is very good about communicating when deadlines are approaching, so be sure to frequently check your announcements. Reading the textbook is extremely important, do not underestimate the three unit exams. Overall, if you are a very self-motivated person, I would recommend this class/professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is not difficult, as long as you do not procrastinate. Professor Baldridge is very nice and kind. She has multiple reminders to remind to do your work. Also provides extra credit for every unit. If you procrastinate, I would take this class in-person. Online Async requires motivation and responsibility. I would recommend her class.

She's a great teacher. Provides plenty of extra credit if you turn your assignments in early. Online classes where whenever you get on and do the homework at your own times. Loved the class, would recommend to take her for all psyc if you have too.

This class was online asynchronous, and all our assignments were on McGraw Hill connect. Everything was very structured and straightforward. Quizlet helped me with the coursework, and there isnt a lockdown browser for the test. The key to succeeding is just managing your work and not procrastinating Bc u do everything in your own time.

Social Psychology is really easy for any course, especially an upper level course. Exams are proctored, but content is very similar to all assignments and quizzes. You must read the textbook, but chapters are not particularly difficult. Grades promptly and provides ample opportunity. Really easy class for an upper level PSYC elective!!!

She sends out reminders to students a couple weeks before the due to remind you to do your work because the unit due dates are spaced out. You cannot put off work to the last minute. This is a class where you have to work at continuously little by little each week because if left to do all at once, you will overwhelm yourself. She gives ex credit.

I took Mrs. Baldridge's PSYC 1315 as an online asynchronous course this semester and it was great. Although the course is designed to work at your own pace, she is still happy to help you if you have any questions. She is very thorough in explaining her expectations for assignments and gives many reminders on deadlines too. 11/10 would recommend!

I took her social psychology class and it was beyond time consuming. This class was unnecessarily tedious as we already had 3 exams, multiple quizzes and tons of assignments. My advice is to do every assignment because they count for a major portion of your grade. She is not understanding at all to any circumstances.

I took this class online. You have the ability to do the assignments when you want to but they are due on a certain date. She gives extra credit.  She is a very enthusiastic and nice professor. Be prepared to read and be prepared to pay for a $60+ book on McGraw Hill.

I took this class during COVID as an asynchronous class and it was AWESOME! The chapter assignments do take a while but you get a 100% every time. Literally all of the material is on quizlets so there is no doubt this is an easy A. She also gives multiple extra credit opportunities! Overall, love her and would definitely take this class again :)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is amazing I recommend taking. easy class
She always gave personal stories as examples and was so chill. She definitely gave you high school teacher vibes in a good way. Notes are how you'll do well on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Best Psych professor you can take. She gives great lectures and does not bore you. She does not take attendance and gives a lot of extra credit. The homework assignments are easy as well, but require you to buy the textbook. Tests are basically definitions from the chapters and can be found on Quizlet. Take her!!!

She was one of the best professors I have had. She said this was her first time teaching social psych but she made the class super interesting and easy to understand. She gives lots of extra credit! She has so many in class activities that helps students understand the concepts better as well.

Everyone talks about the extra credit but she doesn't give any. Not lenient at all with grading and doesn't care to help you the way other professors were. I was so excited for this class but ended up being so disappointed. Only reached out when assignments were due. Doesn't respond to emails. However, everything is on quizlet and you can get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Baldridge is very funny and laid back. She gives a review and the tests are all application based. She also offers extra credit questions. All the assignments for a unit are due when that unit test is due, so you just have to keep that deadline in mind. If you decide to skip class, that's okay just go to the review day.
Shes great, I just thought she was boring! I never went to class and I ended up passing with a B!

This was her first semester teaching Internship in Psychology. She is very kind and open to your feedback. You have to show up to class, but it's once a week. Make sure to pick a great internship and keep track of your logs. There is a research paper with a presentation as well.

She is such an amazing teacher and gives students a lot of extra credit. Utilize the extra credit because it will bump up your grade a lot. Make sure you go to class, so you can get the extra credit questions on the test. Love her to death! Highly recommend!

I mean, its an online econnect, mcgraw hill class. yktv. super long and tedious, but not hard. there's a "read about it" button, click that and it takes u to the answer. pretty easy. here's a secret: download an app called socratic, it'll change ur life. take pic, find answer, fill in, REPEAT. boringg but its an easy core filler. learned some stuff

EASY A! there are so many extra credit opportunities. when she reviews for the test make sure you're there, super helpful. she drops the lowest test grade but not the final. I didn't really attend class that much but when I did they were super intriguing and fun.

amazing class! gives extra credit, its very very cut and dry. As long as you try, do extra credit, and pay attention its easy. You probably dont even need to go to class but i found it enjoyable. 100% take her again
Overall the class is very easy. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunity options throughout the entire semester. She is funny and does explain every topic thoroughly. SHE IS GREAT.

I personally could not stand going to class. Rachel says um every other word and gets off topic very easily which is very distracting for me. Half of the time lectures are doing a self-quiz to see your personality or something so its a hit or miss on which days you choose to not show up. Exam reviews are key to passing, and theres extra credit

Hands down best professor I've ever had. She does take attendance, but her lectures are great and she's so funny. She's kind, provides clear grading criteria, gives extra credit opportunities, and plenty of (relatively easy) assignments, so you'll be okay if you have trouble with quizzes, tests, etc as long as you actually do those assignments.

She is one of the best professors I had. Pay attention to the exam review, you will do good on your exam. At the end of the exam she gives the extra credit point if you answer the examples that she used during lecture, so don't miss the class! There are bunch of extra credit opportunities too.

She is an amazing teacher. She makes the lectures interesting and everything she teachers corresponds to what is on the test. Tons of extra credit opportunities. Definitely go to the lectures before the tests because she gives extremely helpful reviews.

She's great. She thinks of psychology as an element you can see everyday and gives you examples to prove it so, while other psych teachers teach it as if it was neurology science and your final's gonna be a brain surgery. She's chill and I love her. She makes the class fun and I looked forward to going to her lectures.

Loves class discussion, which is a pain in a class of around 200 people. Almost an excessive amount of extra credit. If you take the notes online by yourself, you learn just as much since she practically reads from the powerpoints
I loved this class! Take her if you have the chance. Her lectures are amazing and if you put in the work you can get an A.

She is one of the best professors I have taken. She gives great examples of the material. You will have 15 homework assignments which is a completion grade so if you don't do it than you will get a 0 but she only gives you 5 free 0's. The exams are relatively easy and she give many extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.
Psychology was a really difficult class for me because of all the vocabulary and I failed all of her tests, but because of all of the extra credit she offers I still ended up with a B.

I loved Professor Baldridge! Her class was very fun to go to... and I never like going to class. Her tests were easy, if you studied for them. Also she gives a review on what kind of questions will be on the test, so be sure to go to class, at least the day before!! She gives A LOT of extra credit. I did all of them, and it didn't take much time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I absolutely love this professor! Her class was my favorite hands down. If you can, defiantly take her. The exams so super easy and she tells you exactly what to study for them. The lectures are very lively. She offered a ton of extra credit and the LearnSmart assignments are pretty easy.

She's great. When teaching her lectures she practically gives you the test throughout the lectures. Make sure to read your LearnSmarts though, especially the highlighted portions of the ebook. This is important; Make sure you read the highlighted parts of the ebook on LearnSmart.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Baldridge is amazing. Her lectures do not go too fast nor too slow. She incorporates a lot of funny stories into her lectures. Class is very comfortable. Often times, class ends up just being people sharing stories. The tests go along perfectly with lecture, so take good notes. She offers LOTS of extra credit opportunities.

Sometimes I wish she didn't just lecture by reading slides, it gets boring, but I understand that it's hard to teach this subject any other way due to all the vocabulary that is involved. If you study the test reviews you will be fine in her class. She took attendance randomly, so you had to go to class to not get points off.

She gives out a lot of extra credit so its really hard to fail the class. Her lectures are boring however her review sessions before the exams are spot on. She is funny and can be sarcastic at times. This class overall was a total waste of time. Thought it would be more intresting and fun but it wasn't, unfortunately. However it is an easy A.

4 exams, tons of extra credit, funny, caring, relatable, and overall pretty chill. The only downside would be that she takes random attendance which starts to get strict towards the end of the semester but she gives you 3 free skip days so you should be fine. Her exam reviews help with the exams. She makes the course enjoyable & easy to understand.

Professor Baldridge was an excellent professor. She gives out SO much extra credit, her reviews are like the test, and overall very caring. She's funny and relatable but she DOES take random attendance, which shouldn't hurt too much since she always 3 free skip days.
Tons of extra credit, only four tests, randomly takes attendance, great reviews for the tests. Lectures can be interesting, gives a lot of real world examples. Don't buy the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Baldridge is a very chill professor. She offers lots of extra credit and generally isnt too tough on attendance. You get a max of three absences before they begin to hurt your grade. Study up for her tests, they can be a little tricky, but if you prepare itll be fine!

Dr. Baldridge is an okay professor. She doesn't give homework other than exams and the textbook is not mandatory to buy. She tends to get off topic really easily and quite often. But her lectures are very interesting & she is very caring and funny

Professor Baldridge makes class interesting and engaging. She made all topics applicable to real life and gave a lot of personal anecdotes. Her reviews were literally what you expected on the tests. She offers so much extra credit, that it is totally possible to make an A in the class. There were only 4 tests and 1 participation grade + EC.

AMAZING professor. Very funny, and keeps the class entertained with her stories. She is very passionate about psychology and will make it very understandable for everyone. Tests are doable as long as you study. She does test reviews in class so thats a bonus. She also offers a ton of extra credit.

She's new but she's really nice and well respected. She takes random attendance so you never know when she will. She is passionate about the class and gets the class involved with discussions. She gives extra credit opportunities as well. She is also very pretty and young and her stories are great so that's a bonus.

If you can avoid him...do it! Some majors can't avoid him because the math department only offers his class(unfortunately). You learn a lot of new material 4 days before an exam, which will, in fact, be on the test. Pages of review are given A DAY before exams. UTA, please organize a range of organized professors for the sake of students' success.

Worst professor I've ever taken! Everything he does is from a textbook, and he is always lost as to how to solve the problems. Confuses the whole class, and the class splits into groups, which is annoying after only getting videos as "lectures".
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is pretty ok for a college class. You get extra credit which is nice and you are provided with videos from the math dept for learning. This is where the good things end. Hes not good at remembering things, he gets confused, he doesnt really teach you, and mildly difficult to get emails back from. If you struggle w math stay away...
AWFUL professor not only do you have to take like 6 test you have to do an end of the semester signature assignments which is a lot of crap and he sucks as a professor guarantee youll be confused

Literally I didn't learn a thing from him. I relied on the videos to teach me in this class because they were WAY better than anything he did. He already had example problems worked out and literally just gave us the answers instead of working them out with us. If you typically struggle in math, FIND ANOTHER PROF!

If your an active learner avoid this professor. His method of teaching is talking to himself looking down with zero engagement with the class. If you have issues with the online attendance log in make sure you actively stay in top of him or youll get an F. Very unwelcoming cold attitude makes it awkward to even engage and ask questions in class.

Dry asf, but descent math prof. Literally he reads off and does the problems from the workbook. The hour and 20 minutes lecture can go by if you're actively engaged. Exams are usually taken at the LRC Room, 20-25 questions all multiple choice. -HW/Quizzes/Attend. - 15% -Exams - 50% -Final - 30% -Signature Assignment - 5% If I were you, practice!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I personally didn't like his vibe, or how he taught class because he would just read from the workbook. Lecture is quite boring because the videos explain what he says in class, but it is mandatory. However, if you do the homework and watch the videos you should be able to pass.

Pretty dry sense of humor, but he tries. Mainly reads from the book, but isn't afraid to work out the problems you have, which helps if you're fuzzy on how to get to an answer. If you do the reviews before the test, you'll be fine.

Wasn't too hard, Lecture are super long though, but he goes super quick as well. Pretty cool chill professor. Tries to make the exam the same as CompTIA security (he still recommends studying). Group project annoying but doable, labs aren't too bad but do require all your attention. Overall, he wants you to get something out of it.

Professor Bakker was one of the few professors who's lectures I actually looked forward to attending.  In addition to him giving great lectures and being funny, he was always very quick in replying to students' questions in his slack channel.
Class had about 4 homework projects and 3 exams. Exams are manageable as long as you show up for review day and do all the previous exams.

Prof Bakker is very knowledgeable and teaches great. The first 2 tests were easy but our final was crazy tricky but there was a curve. Assignments are pretty challenging and DIY. For quizzes make sure you write your own code and understand it and you'll do great. I never attended OH but could still do good on assignments though think I should have

Start early on coding assignments, attend office hours with questions, aim for full marks on exams (focus on terminology and simple computer math), write most of the review materials on the cheat sheet (highlight keywords strategically), use past exams to prepare, and note that assignment quizzes are tough, so aim for full marks on everything else!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best class and best professor by far in the CSE department, Bakker comes with many years of industry experience and you can see it by the way he teaches. His programming assignments are a trial by fire, but you will come out of them learning a lot. Exams are very straightforward and fair, and his quizzes are free if you actually did the assignment
I have one word to describe him " NIGHTMARE "

Grade was mostly based on coding assignments, which takes a lot of time to do. Very friendly professor and tries to respond to every message quickly. Strict on grading and a bit fast paced for the course. 2 exams, final, and 45% of the grade comes from codes/quizzes. Does give small extra credit opportunities

To be honest, I don't like his teaching style at all. He is very unprofessional and egotistic. He doesn't seem to enjoy teaching and might even ignore you over email or his main communication channel, which is Slack. I highly suggest avoiding him at all costs.

He is one of the best professors UTA has got. Very knowledgeable. His assignments can be a pain to do but if you start early you're good. He also has a slack where you can message him/his TAs asking for help. I usually kept asking questions until things made sense. If you know everything in the review lecture, you're good for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Yeah, those past reviews on this profile are sus because no student talks like that. Anyway, he jitters around a lot, is boring and his way of teaching is "yeah so this is that and that is this". Coding assignments are the worst because they're nearly impossible without help. The saving grace is the tests he gives which are basically his reviews.

Loved his OS class and came back for more when he taught InfoSec. 50% labs and 50% multiple choice exams. Keeps you engaged, and answers questions really well. The class needed more practical demos, and when we requested them, he adapted his style to our needs. Keeps the class engaged with funny stories and videos. I still liked his OS class more.

He is a great lecturer and exams are fair. Review all old exams and available resources, and you'll do fine. Homework is very hard, so start early. If you need help, go to his or his TA's office hours! They are extremely responsive.

This professor is probably the best professor I've taken in the CS department. You can tell he loves the subject by the way he teaches. His coding assignments can be challenging, so it's better to start early, and they're worth a majority of the grade. But oh my, this is the class I've enjoyed the most so far. He is HIM.

This is *the* professor if you actually wanna learn. The way he talks is how you know he really knows his stuff and is passionate about it. His office hours are a great learning opportunity for everyone, even if you do not have a question. One thing, DO NOT CHEAT.

Cool professor, Assignments can take long hours to complete but are interesting and he's available during office hours and willing to spend time to help. Useful lectures on job applications and interviews at end of semester. Exams are largely based on previous exams provided.

Easily one of the coolest professors at UTA. He is really helpful in his office hours and will work with you to solve your problems. The programming assignments were challenging but fun. You will feel really good once you finish them. Exams are very much like the past exams that he provides, so review those. Exams/quizzes are no longer open-book.

Prof Bakker is literally one of the best instructors at UTA. He is really nice and helpful to his students, and you will be able to tell. If you are taking his class, which I 100% recommend, the only thing I'd recommend you to focus on is his assignments because that is the only way you could mess up in his class, if you find it hard, go to his OH!

The professor was great, and seemed to enjoy teaching students. Although the projects were tough, he was available to offer help and would provide examples to help start the projects. Very kinda as well.

Where do I even start, I came into this course afraid because of the rumors of this course and its load. The lectures were fantastic and fun. He cares for his students and their success. As long as you review the slides and attend office hours for the coding assignments if needed, you should be more than ok in this course.

Awexome teacher, his exams are fine, just study the lecture materials, he usually ends the class very early cause he gets lazy lol. But, Very smart and does care about students success. His coding assignments are really hard though, so go to his office hours he helps you with the coding assignment. No Hw, just quizzes, 3 exams and coding assignment

He is honestly the best professor I've ever had. Not only is he incredibly smart but he truly cares we learn the concepts. If you attend the lectures and try your best on the labs (office hours help!) there is a really easy class. His last few lectures focus on interview and resume which is super helpful. I would take him for all classes if i could
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bakker and Rice are the best teachers I have ever had at UTA. Bakker really does go above and beyond to help you. Office hours are open and online. They are very helpful. Exams were open book and always graded fairly. His lectures kept me engaged. Now that I am getting into 4000 level classes, wish I still had people like Bakker and Rice.

Awesome. Honestly, you can't go wrong taking him for any CSE course. One of the best professors at UTA in terms of lectures, policy, and honesty. This course is challenging but Bakker goes above and beyond to ensuring your success. There are 3-4 exams and some quizzes. He doesn't try to trick you on questions but will occasionally throw a curveball

One of the best profs I've had. His lectures are great, they don't put you to sleep and he explains topics so that they make sense. The exams were open notes, the HWs were not too bad he helps on hw during office hours. The final exam replaces your lowest exam grade, that class was an easy A.

Took him during my worst semester yet. As someone who does not like online school one bit, he made my overall experience much more bearable. He provided necessary assistance, even through the ice storm that hit Texas. He has tons of industry experience as well; probe for information related to both the class and industry when appropriate.

Professor Bakker made online lectures an amazing experience. He broke down key topics in operating systems such as job scheduling, memory and file management. Highly suggest to attend lectures and especially his office hours. He goes over upcoming assignments and answers question. Quick tip make a list of questions beforehand! Good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Bakker is a great lecturer and really down to earth. He has a great sense of humor and goes out of his way to help students. He's also an avid Star Wars fan. He almost completely worked through homework assignments during office hours, and his grading is fair. He repeats the important stuff several times so it sinks in. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: very good professor. cares about his students and excellent lecturer. 10/10

The instructor's lecture is very confusing if you don't read the textbook. The quizzes and exams don't correlate to the learning materials well nor it really test your knowledge. Be ready to put a lot of time to read a lot to make sure you understand the materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Probably one of the most helpful and easygoing professors I've had, sure lectures are powerpoint and somewhat hard to grasp at first, but he was very responsive and helpful to my questions in office hours and over emails. Also assignments are both interesting and useful.

Mr. Trevor Bakker is the best instructor I ever had at UTA! CSE department of UTA sucks because of bad instructors but Mr. Bakker is an exception. He is a very practical person. Very energetic and helpful !! I am his big fan. His lectures are quite higher level and it requires you to have some information on the topic being discussed in class.

One of the hardest working professors I've seen. The way he lectures is extremely personable and doesn't get too into the jargon. Assignments are tough, but are explained in depth during office hours. Stays past designated office hours times almost always (to the detriment of his own health!) Easy to approach, friendly, and understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bakker is very nice and helpful and I think he does care about his students. In terms of teaching however, he is one of the worst professors I've ever had; second only to Dr. Weems. He taught like everyone had already taken an intro OS course. His lectures were boring and hard to follow and the instructions for the labs were virtually nonexistent.

He is the best professor. We did not need a book for the class, and he also posts all the lectures online. He posts previous two semesters quizzes and tests, and please study those with the powerpoint for the tests. He also had five labs. If you go to his office, he will sit with you and do 90% of the lab for you.

He presents the material in real world examples because he knows what he is talking about.  He is one of the few engineering professors at UTA that are worth their weight in gold. I wish I could take every class with him.  He doesn't make any part of this class hard, he makes it so you learn what you are doing.

He's a great person. He's a good model for other professors to learn how to teach from. He's very generous with his time. He is always willing to help and explain things. The content can be difficult, but he makes it understandable. The homeworks can be tough but they're doable.

Great lectures, be sure to download notes on your ipad if you can to follow along. Concept is really hard but she breaks its down pretty well. Pop quizzes so I guess attendance is mandatory. Allows you to drop lowest quiz grade if you participate hw questions. At the end she gave us an extra cred assignment that boosts your grade by half a letter.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: pls go to office hours it saved my grade
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: CSE 3315 is a difficult class that requires effort but Dr. Barasch tries her best to help students succeed through her comprehensive lectures and adequate curves. I do not like the pop quizzes but many are dropped and there is a homework every week. Tests do not have much time except for the finals where you have 2.5 hrs to do a 1.5 hr test.

I feel like this class is just another math class. At the start of any math class, you need to solve lots of questions to get comfortable with the topic, and that's literally what you'd do for this class. Make sure when you study for the exams, to set a timer because the exams are long with very short timing. The prof tries her best to make it easy

Final exam the class averaged 50 and that was with a 15 point curve. The last third of the material was the hardest I suggest doing really well on the first two tests. She drops 3 of the 4 pop quizzes if you had already done every other assignment so you can theoretically watch her from home if you at least get one of the pop quizzes done.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is an excellent and nice professor. The material is very difficult but she tries her best to explain it in a concise way. Beware she does do pop quizzes, so try to go class. Tests are pretty difficult, I would encourage you to do study groups and reach out to her for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: It's ALOT like discrete, if you don't know the previous discrete class.She might as well be speaking Greek. This is alot like calc 2 class in that it's A TON of material. Exam 1 & 2 are 25% each final is 30%=80%. The rest is participation grade for the HW & popquiz. If you don't write down "the correct" answers for the hw, & understand you'll fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a hard class, no getting around it. Barasch is a decent lecturer. She always welcomes questions, although her responses may not always be the most informative, you can tell she has taught the course for a while and knows it well. Partial credit on tests all the way, a couple of pop quizzes that aren't too challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Great lectures, very knowledgeable. Class is jam-packed with content but was generally very interesting and highly engaging. Lots of homework but always doable, went over every day it was due for instant feedback on what you're not understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Barasch loves to teach cse-3315 you can tell easy. She makes the material really easy to understand and I really enjoyed her course. This is a hard class so expect to put in hours outside of classroom to understand the topics. She wants nothing but the best from her students.

If you don't plan on taking compilers, then a D is passing for this class.

This is a difficult class, it has been 93 days since homework has been graded. The exams can be harsh, as well as unequal grading for the exams. Someone else can get full credit on a problem, while you get close to 0, then ask for a regrade and get full points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This is probably the worst class I have ever taken. You have multiple assignments every week which will not be graded till the very end of the semester. The class is super disorganized and hard to follow if youre someone who cant really learn from lectures. The hardest part of the class starts after the 2nd exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great professor. Very knowledgeable and she loves what she teaches. Tough material but she gives printed lecture notes so you can better follow along. Tests were a big percent of grade and has a cumulative final. She gives old exams as practice and TA holds review session before tests. Know the practice exam material and similar material!!

This course is definitely challenging and will require good discipline on making due dates. However, the professor really does care for her students and tries her best to make the material more engaging. The best thing I did was watch through Echo360's before each exam and work the hw after each video. You will need the book to follow along with.

Overall, this class was not terrible like everyone was telling e before I took it, but you definitely have to put in the work to pass. I finished the class with a B. I just watched all the lectures the week of the exam and practiced the HW problems. There's a lot of HW for that class too. If you don't watch the lectures, you are not going to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class itself is hard so you have to put a lot of effort outside of class. Probably one of the hardest classes I have taken. Her lectures are very helpful but not enough. Make sure you take advantage of the office hours and online resources. You have to literally study a lot to get a good grade. She gives review topics for the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Partial grading is practically non-existent when it comes to grading tests, but it's very generous when grading homework. Homework is randomly graded, so you won't know if your method of doing proofs is correct. Exams take FOREVER to be graded. The final happens tomorrow and the second exam is not graded, so you don't know what you need to pass.
Amazing professor, but very difficult course. Proofs proofs and more proofs so get comfortable. Make sure to really nail down the first midterm as the second exam will be a lot harder. Good luck!

One of the hardest classes, I have ever taken so far. TA is really a tough grader. Even though the professor says that she believes in partial grades, it will not be seen in exams. A small mistake will cost you the whole points. And also a very useless class which does not make any sense at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Barasch wasn't teaching the entire semester, so I can't rate her. The grading is fairly unjustified. Most of your points lost is from something small. Luckily, I heard this class is pretty "useless". You won't see it again in any future classes, and I don't know anyone who uses this stuff in the field. :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class is hard, though I wouldn't say material is as hard as the class is. Prof is passionate and knowledgeable, and concepts eventually start making sense, but little mistakes on exams are very costly! TA's don't grade well, so beware. Exams even with generous curves were in the 50-60 range. If you're like most students average, expect a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took cse3315 twice - before and during covid. Both times, I had to challenge the grades I got on many HWs. Prof says she's a "true believer of partial credit" but doesn't show it. I lost significant points for minor errors. Ex. My work was correct. Forgot 1 letter in the answer. Got deducted 8/12 pts. Couldn't win pts because "the answer is wrong".
True believer of partial credits, but the grading is ridiculous.
Really tough class but she was an awesome professor. Lots of homework and pop quizzes. Exams are hard as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: professor doesn't allow student to ask questions in class. presenting so many things that is not useful. don't take the class

She is amazing. I had her in the summer, 5 weeks course, therefore, attendance was mandatory. Her exams are long and not easy but she uses the very same example as she lectures or in homework. So write down EVERYTHING she writes on the board and study those and you will be good. Her TA did not grade well. I suggest double check your grade with her

Her classes are fast-paced and because students are encouraged to copy everything she writes on the board it can be hard to focus on the topics being taught. On top of that, echo recordings are not available for reviewing lectures. Make sure you go through course materials beforehand. She does curve generously and exams are fairly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shes literally the only teacher for theoretical but shes an amazing teacher. Theoretical is very seriously the hardest class in college so far. It builds on previous classes such as discrete and algorithms and sort of combines the two while adding a lot of new things and complexity. Do not take theoretical unless you have the time to study
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: grading -- doesn't curve much 88 is A, upto 77 is B, upto 60 is C teaching speed is pretty fast. but easily accessible after class. subject is pretty hard if you miss even a single class attendance--has 15% weightage in final grades homework- doesn't have any weightage in grades simply don't take this sub. in summer.. fall or spring- good choice
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This can be a difficult class if you didn't take an interest in your discrete structures class. Barasch is an excellent teacher, teaching what she obviously loves. If you want a good grade, speak up if you don't understand something. It's likely most of the class didn't either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: This is THE most difficult course in CSE. If you really truly enjoy and understand every single algorithm taught in the book you will do well in this class. If you're like the majority you cannot make more than a C even after a curve. 76 is usually a B and for an A you have to go above and beyond.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hardest class I've taken yet in my CS Major, if you don't go to class you most likely won't pass. Get ready to memorize many proofs and algos
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class is tough but she does her best to break it down. Not an easy grade by any means but shes the best to take it with.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Barasch really knows her stuff and does a good job at explaining everything. The material is pretty hard to follow at times though but she does her best to break it down for everyone. This was my most demanding course this semester. Test averages were around 65 for the first two tests but she curves.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Barasch is a great teacher who works hard to ensure you understand the material if you wish to. In her class you will learn difficult concepts that can play a role in tech interviews or your career. She is a passionate teacher and a fair grader, but don't take the class if you are expecting a walk in the park.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Avoid if you are expecting an easy A. Lectures are amazing, homework assigned every week, tough grading pattern 3 tests 30% each, will explain until you understand the concept, makes you read the textbook thoroughly,  grading is relative to how class performs, she curved my final grade. I had an 86 in the course, made an A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She clears all the doubts while in class while teaching, very accessible and loves when students interact and ask questions. This isn't an easy class, you will need to put in a lot of work. 3 tests, 90% of the grade. Tests are hard, but go over each and every concept, proof and definition in the textbook, and you will do great in the tests!

Very good professor, explains everything in great detail and willing to help anyone that talks to her. She is very understanding. Tests are a little tough and long, usually take the entire class to finish. Must attend class because quizzes and homework are during beginning of class.

I took Dr. Barasch last semester, she is very hard, Although she knows her stuff, she explains thing very quick, I mean very very quick and move on, I couldn't understand things clearly although the class its' self is not hard (Discrete), In the first exam I made something in the 30's , it was terrible, the exam wasn't easy and homework is too long

Dr. Barasch explains the material very well but goes very fast. When it comes to exams she grades extremely tough. Even when you think you may do fairly well on the exam you will be surprised because she will take off full marks for the smallest mistake. Doesn't curve very much either. At least attend class so you can make 100s on the pop quizzes.

I like the material we go over but when it comes to exams she is absolutely crazy. The average for the first two tests ended up about a 55-60 each time and didnt even curve the second test. TA's took two weeks to get tests back and didn't grade on an equally so some people got the question right when both had the same answer. BE CAREFUL.

Outstanding instructor. Very methodical in her presentation of the material and very good at explaining it. Homework and exams were not easy but were definitely fair. Knows the material well and will gladly answer your questions before, during or after class. Would gladly take another course with her.

Theoretical Computer Science.  Dr. Barasch  was prepared for every lecture.  She really knew her stuff.  She invites class participation, her pop quizes are REALLY easy (seriously - write your name down, get a perfect score), but her tests are LONG and HARD.  Basically, memorize everything she teaches and you'll do great.

Took discrete class for summer and it was not easy. Although her pop quizzes were easy. Her exams are very hard it requires you to know the basic concept of every chapter. Her exams are harder than exams. Goes through chapters very quick, but will help you if have any questions. good luck.
I enjoyed class

Dr. Barasch knows the curriculum very well and will help you out, you just have to go to her during the correct hours. This is the hardest CS class I've take so far. Go to class, Study, do homework over and over. Good luck!

Tough class; do all the homework, and study hard.  She tests hard and demands prepared students for class.  I learned a lot and appreciate the content of the class, which is essential to success in future classes.
Her teaching style is terrible,she doesn't care about students and teach 4 chapters in a single lecture.
Hardest Computer Science class i've taken so far. Made a B and worked my butt off. She taught the class very well considering how hard the subjects can be.
She is entertaining and interesting.

She has an entertaining lecturing style that makes discrete math interesting. I also had her for 3315 which is more abstract and harder than Discrete Strucures. I have an incomplete with her because of illness and poor test grades. She is allowing me to retake the tests with a chance to raise my C to a B.

Dr. B is wicked smart.  She is very helpful and willing to go out of her way to help you; when you can catch her.  She's very busy and involved in several areas of the school (advising, introductory courses, etc.).  All in all, this class was my favorite that semester.
I like her for an advisor and as a teacher.  She could be a little more responsive to emails.
Very helpful teacher, lectures get dull and seem unimportant because they are abstract. But they are important!
She's a great teacher. Knows what she's talking about and very helpful when u need her.
Had to take this class twice because its mostly abstact math theory, but she will bend over backwards, create miracles, and move mountains, just so you'll understand the content.
a decent prof.....just be careful if you get her for an advisor....

This is one of the hardest classes for all programmers, so prepare yourself for 2 semesters, BUT! Dr. Barasch has been one of the most helpful professors at UTA.  It may not seem like this class has anything to do with programming; just keep hope alive.

prof has open book homeworks for practice to help understand the material, & big curves on exams. ngl tho i had to self study because i was lost during her lectures & the ppt slides were confusing/unclear to me. textbook is not mandatory but i got it bc i wasnt understanding anything from the powerpoints.

Very nice professor and accessible outside of class. She provides a lot of resources which I found helpful. Her tests are fair and she curves them. Homework is all open note and in class activities are ok as long as you are all caught up with the material. This course is material heavy, do not procrastinate! Final exam is optional.

Dr. Betran was an excellent professor. She used slides that were more helpful than the textbook, which I suggest you don't buy because I didn't find it necessary. There are open-note online quizzes for each chapter, and the tests are fair; she also curves the test scores. Homework is optional, but she is very kind & willing to help if you need it.

lectures were pretty boring but all exam material is based on them. textbook is pretty important but not as important as lecture content. she goes over practice problems in class which are similar to exam qs. exams are easier than quizzes and really simplify the main takeaways of genetics. lots of quizzes but she drops lowest ones.
good slides

Dr. Betran is really sweet and I enjoyed taking genetics with her. Of course some of the content is difficult but if you study her PowerPoints it should be fine. She gives open book quizzes which are easy grade boosters. She does have a slight accent but it's not a problem at all with understanding what she is saying.

Very hard class, like basic biology on crack. Lectures and questions were recorded and solved. Practice and the exams you took are posted for review purposes. Really have to study, practice exams are helpful but you must work for it. 3 exams and 1 final, BUT the final is 3 parts and can make up the 3 first exams if graded higher. Slackno pass
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great prof! Genetics is notoriously hard but it's easy to do well in her class. Do the practice problems. Lectures are prerecorded so if you have questions you'll have to ask during office hours but she goes over a lot of helpful info during that time. Quizzes to boost grade and optional 3 part final can replace any or all of the midterm exams.

this class is really challenging especially w/ pandemic going on and class transition to online the exams are just as hard, workload is the same, and only helped by increasing quizzes overall grade weight by 10%. other professors @uta required students to write essay instead of an exam cause they know how hard it can be. she n't considerate at all
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Betrán is really nice and her powerpoint slides are easy to understand and cover everything on the test. She does have an accent but I never found understanding her to be a problem. Grading is 25% online quizzes with unlimited attempts 75% tests. There are 4 tests including the final and one can be dropped.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Betran is committed to her students - her slides are concise, she provides practice exams/suggests sample problems and is accessible via email anytime. She is also one of the kindest professors Ive ever had. If you pay attention, work through the problems and actually understand the concepts, youll be fine.

Get ready to read the textbook. There's literally no other way around it. She claims the tests are based on her ppt, no. In class, her accent makes it difficult to understand anything she says and it gives us all a headache. This class was a real struggle and i'm most likely going to retake the class, just not with her next time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The practice tests were the biggest help with learning the material. Didn't buy the textbook yet still passed every test I wouldn't say it's needed. The lectures contained a lot of information and were incredibly boring. The lack of any SI sessions also made it hard to decipher the material. Dangerously easy to doze of. Soft spoken.

Getting an A in the class is VERY doable. Quizzes are 25% of the grade and she gives multiple attempts so you can get a 100 every time. Class is so terribly boring I don't recommend going. Instead, read the book and do the practice tests and assigned book problems you should do fine. She wants you to succeed and the practice exams help a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I freaking love this professor, she is literally the most well suited person for her job because she touches all bases on her responsibilities as a professor at UTA. her office hours are flexible, she will take time out of any day to drive down there and meet you if you need help, and she gives you past exams to study from. 100/10 would take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: The practice tests were very helpful for preparing for the actual tests. I feel like she didn't try to overcomplicate anything and she went through a lot of examples which was helpful.

The most difficult part of this class is terminology. Her powerpoint presentations are clear and a key to studying for exam. Test are similar to practice exams she gives. She is more than willing to help understand material and accommodate for exams. Class consists of 3 exams and a cumulative final, of the 4 test grades she takes the highest 3.
She has a pretty thick accent but her slides are easy to understand. Study the important material way ahead of time, make smart friends.

Genetics is not a class you can slack on, and expect to pass. With that said, this professor is in my opinion a true gem. Yes, she has an accent but it's not that hard to understand. Her lecture slides are great for studying since they are so packed with information. If you feel lost, she is more than willing to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although, Genetics is a very complicating subject, Dr. Betran presented the information in a manner that made it much more understandable. Studying is key for this class, if you go over the slides themselves, expect a B, but if you take the time to go over the book material, you will easily obtain an A.I extremely encourage office hours.
Great Professor!!!

Her accent is not that bad... she is one of the most understanding and helpful teachers! In my semester she allowed each section of final exam to replace all prior test grades if it helps overall grade. Tests were very clear on what she wanted and if you knew concepts and attended class you did fine. SI was very helpful!!!
Awful lecturer. Hard to understand and her test questions are nothing like the problem sets in class. Not even reading the book will help you, unfortunately.

Hard to understand. Not helpful. The class was hard and I had better luck teaching myself from the book. She reads off the power points in a quiet and hard to understand voice. Lectures are pointless to attend and tests are difficult. My entire class was struggling.

A very hard class. Her accent is hard to understand. She is not confident and clear about what she teaches. So many people failed the class. Even attend to every lectures won't help to understand the material. I actually have to relies on the book and try to find videos online to teach myself.
No Comments

Game Design course in which he gave tutorials so we could start experimenting and exploring on Unity. Overall a great course where you can learn a lot if you put the time and effort into it. 3 projects with one being a group but just starting early should make the course easy to handle.

A quick summer course, the professor explains the assignments/course objectives coherently. He does what he can to make sure every student understands them. Very understanding, he wants every student to succeed/grow at their level. Learned so much defiantly take him again. He has an Incredible dry sense of humor he makes sure everyone knows it. 5/5

Took his class for a accelerated summer course and it was well worth it. He wants the students to evolve their work and learn to prepare for the world outside college. The work was tough but worth learning how to use programs. Very understanding and helpful. Also funny dad jokes make it fun. If you can take him for a full semester I recommend.
5/5

A lot of sour grapes on here. This class was honestly really enjoyable. A bit rough this semester, but I honestly feel I improved my own knowledge and skills. He provides feedback, especially if asked for. You shouldn't expect someone to hold your hand, especially not in University. He consistently expresses he wants students to better themselves.

Wagley talking about RMP in class and replying to every single rating is crazy. Please genuinely consider our feedback- Wagley did not present well-prepared or consistent tutorials during the semester. Students would constantly have to prompt him to lecture/provide tutorials in the program, & to update dates/grades/important information in canvas.

Maybe stop replying to Rate My Professor reviews in class and actually teach the class when students are asking for help. 
This is a self taught class, with no professional help or understanding of the program we were required to use. Despite no help from the professor, grading was harsh with no explanation for why we got the grades we received.

Oftentimes did not have the code correct for the class and most of the class time was focused on code. I don't mind coding at all and I learned some useful things, but I would have liked to learn things like game mechanics, proper level design, etc. At the end of the semester, he would leave for hours for meetings.

I ended up failing this class as I missed a ton of classes due to health complications related to my disabilities. I felt pretty abandoned by this professor despite having sent out letters thru the SAR center regarding my absences and personal evidence of hospitalization, no steps were taken to follow up with me or provide reasonable accommodation

Professor Wagley would spend the majority of time each class on his own projects and work rather than helping students and giving meaningful feedback. We were instructed to critique each other virtually, and he did not participate in them at all. Feedback was few and far in between, especially with grades. This was more akin to a self study class.

He knows his stuff when it comes to 3-D modeling and animation. Friendly and easy to talk to. He understands the difference of skill when it comes to this stuff, so if he knows you tried youll get a decent grade.

Do all of the HW, even the bonus. Before the tests, go over the lecture questions, the practice test, and the reviews.  Better yet, show up to the lectures so you can get help and participate; this is what helped me the most.  Due to his grading, you only need to aim for a high B to get an A. Sometimes he extends the HW due date, but not often.

Lots of homework, his practice tests that he provides aren't exactly like the actual tests unlike some people may say, but they do help. It also helps that he works out a lot of problems in class and lectures are available to watch after class on echo360. His curves are also insane, bumped my final grade of and 85.7 to an A.

Barry is one of the only physics professors at UTA who will even complete all of the required material on schedule. Is that a high bar? Not exactly, but it is something. In all seriousness, his lectures are great. They're informative, not too long, and all recorded and uploaded to echo360. If you take physics at UTA, take him.

The class itself is difficult, but the professor is amazing. He records his lectures, so attendance is not mandatory, but it is absolutely worth it to attend in person. Be prepared to have him attempt to convert you to a physics major, especially if you are in engineering. He might even succeed (many physics majors are a direct result of this)

Awesome professor, one of the very best I've had. His PowerPoints were very well put-together, and he gave clear explanations. He is also willing to sit with students and walk them through topics until they understand it. Good sense of humor. Passing is not difficult, but an A is well-earned. All tests start off with easy questions and get harder.

His lectures were very fast paced with a couple jokes and stories in there. Make sure to ask questions. Both notes and lectures are available to you by Echo360 and ExpertTA, which is where he hosts homework. He wants you to succeed and will curve grades at the end so about 70% of people get a B, and 30% get an A.

Spurlock is a great professor and seems to actually care about his students. If you can, take him for Phys 1 and 2. He puts out test review to help prepare for exams, and curves test grades. His lectures can be a bit difficult to follow, so definitely set aside time to review lecture content.

If you know how to do about 80% of the exams, finish the regular and bonus homework, and do a lot of problems on your own, you have a good chance at getting an A. He tends to breeze by examples or skim his lectures which can be confusing if you're not keeping up with his lecture notes.

Professor Spurlock curved 70% of the class to a B and 35% to an A however the lecture material was hard to learn from. The tests were also difficult. Reviews are sparsely similar to exams.
