reviews.comment: Although he can be thorough with his grading, I took his class as a history major and I had a lot of fun! You do need to come to class for the lectures, his PowerPoints are mostly for visual reference. He structures his lectures around the four different books in his course, each tying into the time period and topic you're covering for that month.

Dr. Morris is a good professor. His class was just boring to me, but that is my opinion, and someone else may really like it. He is a nice guy that explains concepts well, but gets sidetracked pretty quickly. Make sure you attend class because his exams (all essays) are based off the information in his PowerPoint slides.
Professor Morris was an amazing professor! He really took his time to explain what he required and he gave clear feedback on every essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Loved this class and I don't even like history. His lectures were easy to understand and you could tell he genuinely liked teaching the class. Attendance is not required and because of covid, not many people came to his lectures including myself sometimes. Please go though, he's really nice and deserves an audience. Really easy tests.

I took Dr. Morris for Historical Research. You have to be very disciplined and self-motivated to take this class. He gives very good feedback on your writing. He schedules lots of time off from class for students to write their papers. Overall, this class is a class of endurance. Very easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Hes okay, I took him for 3300 and we had weeks off so we could work on our 15 page paper. He gives very good feedback although he could be rude but its for your best interest. He is semi approachable hes not too mean or too nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Overall, he is a very nice guy and the lectures are interesting, but grades are unclear and if you need an organized professor, take someone else. Due dates are always changing and he is lenient about late work. Exams were all essay questions and the textbook is necessary if you want to pass. Also there is a 20 page paper group project
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, he makes complicated history easy to understand. Read the require textbook and take lots of note from all the lectures and you will pass this class with an A. He doesn't take attendance, but you will miss a lot of valuable information that you can use to answer the essay questions on exams if you don't attend class regularly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This teacher is very difficult on tests. The way they are worded are completely different from the text book which will make tests difficult. He talks down to you as if you are stupid and doesnt realize that this is a class not a major. The lectures are according to the book for a moment then his political views cloud your understanding. Stay away

If you need to take 3300, take him. Unlike other professors offering this class, he doesn't weigh your grade solely on the final paper, but rather distributes points throughout smaller assignments. He can seem intimidating, but he is helpful and readily available to work with you. You'll have to stay on top of this class, but if you do you're good.

Dr. Morris is not the easiest professor but HIST 3355 is an upper level course so you cannot expect it to be easy. If you want to make a good grade you will have to read all the material. At times he is a bit difficult to understand but he is also extremely helpful and if you ask questions he will clear things up. All exams are written essays.

The best professor I have ever had. Extremely interesting and relevant material. If you are a bad student or lazy don't take his class. However, if you want to learn you could not find a better professor.

Plenty of knowledge to convey and quite interesting to hear, but I don't know if he really cares whether you learn something or just want you to listen to him pontificate.  Wasn't helpful when I would visit his office or email with questions.  His feedback to me was consistently negative, yet he gave me an A. Confusing.
VERY good teacher! Keeps his lectures entertaining and teaches well! I never really minded going to his class. Hate history but it was easy to make a good grade in there!
Lectures are very unorganized.  The readings & lectures do not tie into each other well at all.  Talks down to students & very hard to approach.  I don't suggest you take his class.

He's a great teacher. He helps you when you need it,and he's nice to you as long as you don't distract him while sitting in the front, by talking or looking at your computer and laughing. If you're in the back of course, he doesn't mind. He's funny as well so you aren't easily bored! The test are hard though, but they're easy if you actually study.
Very good teacher. Difficult but rewarding. Take him if you are serious about history.
Interesting subject matter but lots of reading. Be prepared to read several books for discussions. Tests are all essays and he grades you as if you were a grad student.

I was excited to take a course in Environmental history but Dr. Morris is a very tough teacher. He is very unorganized and his lectures prove it. The group project was the best part of this class because it did not really involve him. Other posting are right about him grading way too hard. He is very unclear about the midterm and final.

This Teacher sucks..do not take him..he is awful and he talks down to you. He grades like you should have a PHD. He needs to remember he is teaching an undergraduate class. grades very strict and nothing but essays and good luck figuring out what he wants unless you are a mind reader...you will regret this class. excellent topic terrible teacher

I thought this teacher was interesting to listen to, not too bad really, but... He grades too hard, I really put all my effort into this class and made a d.  I am astonished really.  He gives 4 essays, and they are too long, and he grades too picky.  You will regret this class with him unless you are good at essays, he is not helpful in office at a
Hard, only four tests, doesn't drop one.  Tests in class are only essays.  It is really hard to make a decent grade if you don't agree with his highly liberal views.

Morris is a good prof, but very unapproachable and does not respond to emails. takes forever to return any assignments. This is a grad level class & should have been handled better. I will not take him for any other classes.
HE TALKS SO SLOW!

He lectures extremely slow so if you are a daydream in class kind of person, take him. Most of what he lectures is based on the textbook, once in awhile he'll throw in an interesting story. He doesn't give much of a review for exams (only two). I never felt prepared enough for the exams; when he gives a review,he basically says good luck, that's it
Very Poor, in fact one of the worst in the department. Very conceited too.

I enjoyed the class, but all three essays were a little restrictive because you couldn't use outside sources even if they supplemented your historical argument. On the other hand, Morris is a good prof and his class is interesting. There were 5 quizzes (25 questions each) spaced evenly throughout the semester.
I had @ least 3 courses with him, and enjoyed all. He challenges students to think outside the box and express their opinions.  Great discussions, especially upper levels.
Great teacher, an obvious love for history, take him if you actually want to learn something and be challenged.
long winded- you must think way outside the box and love to write essays if you want to take this class- this is not a memorize and pass class.

Do not listen to any bad reviews. For me, the way his lectures and format of how he taught the curriculum were phenomenal. While his classes were large, he was open to question asking and was engaging. His slides and homework were 100% similar to exams as long as you studied and did the practice. If I could've I would take him for other classes!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super good professor and super good intro to bio! While the class was very lecture heavy, he split it up pretty well with non-lecture days before tests (practice problems and practice tests). Homework was light and you could take it as many times as needed to get a 100. Just take notes before lectures and do the practice homework and you're set

Professor Clark was very chill; his lectures really helped me understand. The key to success is utilizing Quizlet and memorizing the lectures, as that's where the test questions are derived from. Very funny and loves to do demonstrations with classmates! Would def retake him. Also, use the hw practice well.  He uses those for the practice tests.

He is the nicest professor I know. His lectures weren't too fast but weren't too slow. He's smiles a lot and likes to crack jokes. The homework's were easy hundreds. The percentages of each assignment and tests don't really make sense but other than that I enjoyed this class.

Professor Clark is very nice. Be sure to use the extra texts posted on Canvas, they really help you understand the material. The course is a bit heavy but definitely doable. It moves at a faster pace, so you need to make time for the work.
great teacher but he focuses on the slides a lot, i did enjoy the physical demonstrations involving the students.

This was a great class. The material is very easy reading, and written very uncomplicated. Lecture attendance is not necessary AS LONG as you read and take notes on the slides. 
Each week is a new topic or system in easily digestible sections
All of the information in the entire class was supplied online, through slide shows.
Great class

Dr Clark is super respected, without a doubt. He is my favorite professor on campus so far. This class is on the more difficult side, but he's extremely open minded. He likes to laugh and smile and crack jokes. He knows exactly what he's talking about, too. I don't like how homework is only worth 10% and exams are 40%, but can't win at everything!

I would say that he is a decent professor. Since he is the chair of the biology department he may seem strict or monotone but he seems like a great guy. His lectures were fine, its best to come prepared taking notes before class and having question for him because he likes to ask the class if they have any questions.

This class is very much self taught. Professor Clark explains almost nothing during lectures and will give example questions but will not give the answer half of the time. If you need to email him be prepared for much attitude IF you get a response. This course is already hard as it is but the professor makes it much worse. Avoid taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Medical Molecular Biology puts to test all the topics you have learned in other classes. This class has you write review papers and will teach you how to research effectively. It is rough if you do not have the best foundation of knowledge, but you are caught up to speed. If you are excited by medical related research definitely take this class.

Get ready to be your own professor in this do or die class! You may have "lecture" only Wednesday's and Friday's, but you're not told that there are also over 40 lecture videos that all average out to be an hour long. Then there's textbook text to read on top of that. Oh yeah, lectures are just summaries of chapters you studied. Abosolutely awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: To be frank, it doesn't matter which professor you choose, they all use the same slides and same material, but they all lecture differently. You're honestly just teaching yourself. All departments are like this, and it is not working at all. This Fall 2020 semester was abyssmal.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best Biology 1441 professor imo. He is really smart and always tries to make jokes to make lectures less boring. The textbook is given for free on canvas and I got a B because I didn't read. Read the book! Looking back, this class was so easy and he gives test questions on echo. Very understanding and is easy to communicate with. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark has been my favorite professor without a doubt. He is EXTREMELY knowledgeable and can answer all of your biology questions. He makes himself super accessible via office hours and holds very informative review nights before the exam. If you familiarize yourself with the slides, you will do good. If you read the book, you will do amazing.

There is a textbook, but it was free online and he posted all of the important material on canvas. He isn't a bad teacher, but he isn't a great one either. I feel as if he just read off the slides sometimes. I would recommend reading ahead and then following along with the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The lectures for me felt slow and boring as the pace was slowed down for weaker students. To get an A all you need to do is read the material on canvas and understand the practice quizzes and graded quizzes. The powerpoint slides are useless compared to the text. Clark makes himself very accessible.

Professor Clark takes his time during lecture. He doesn't rush it so that students can ask questions. Every morning, before class starts, he plays videos related to the topic he's about to teach. The videos are usually hilariously ridiculous but they can help sometimes. The tests go along perfectly with what we discuss in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This is my favorite professor. I had so much in this class. Everyday was an adventure. Biology is now my favorite subject thanks to him. He is a great teacher. Take advantage of his office hours. Practice problems are really helpful when studying for exams.

He is such a good professor. You have to read the book. Not reading the book, you will fail. Its a tough class. The test are hard. I ended up dropping the class and rethinking my path, but he is a true good professor.

Honestly speaking, he's the best professor compared to other bio professors. However, he's also the best at reading off his slides. He doesn't really teach. YOU NEED TO READ THE BOOK TO PASS!!! Don't rely on his ppt because it's the generalization of the textbook. Do well in labs and go to office hours because he's normally always there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Clay Clark is good at explaining the general concepts of the book. Make sure you read the book because that is what his power points and test are based upon. Grades attendance by iclicker. Overall willing to help his students, but have to have good communication with him. Study hard for test, because they are TOUGH. Do good in lab section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: You have to read the textbook. HAVE TO. His lectures are just him reading off the slides and the test questions go way more into depth than his slides do. Just make sure you read A LOT and find other sources you can study and remember the material from.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great professor, in my opinion the best professor at explaining the material. Just make sure to read the textbook, easy A if you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is the best professor there is for BIO 1441. He knows how to teach. If you really understand the power points, you will do well on the test. He tells you everything you need to know, you just have to listen. The book wasn't needed if you understood the powerpoint.

Dr. Clark is a great professor. If you ask him questions about the material he'll answer them for you. If you're struggling with something he'll help you, you just have to go to him for help. He may just read off the slides but he incorporates fun videos that actually helped me memorize terms and such. Tests are departmental.
Horrible Professor, all he does is read off of slides and if he did not make class mandatory i would never go. Just read the book and you can easily get an A in his class.

He pretty much reads off the slides and calls it a lecture, as if we can not do it ourselves. Just to pass, you have to go beyond class notes, you need the read the book and memorize every small detail. He will hold a "review" session the NIGHT before the test but its pretty much him answering questions not like an actual review session.

The class is very lecture and attendance-based and while the lectures are well-made, but Mr. Clark often gets off track which puts ppl to sleep. The grades that aren't participation are very hard without AI (but easy with), and the tests made me cry. My best advice is to participate and ask questions so he respects you, which helps in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Talks a lot of Texas Instruments, goes on about nothing sometimes but is very accessible and gives you outlines for papers so not that hard imo. Just go to class get your attendance in and study a little bit of the information each week. 3 exams all fairly easy. (Grades are attendance, papers, and 3 exam)

If you want a professor who talks all class period about nothing related to the lecture and his time at Texas Instruments, this is your guy. Goes on about himself constantly and tells you you should thrive to be in the top 20% when he doesn't even teach. Gives his political views away 20 seconds into ever class period too, insanely unprofessional.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When others talked about how unclear the assignment criteria was for the final report, they wouldn't actually understand what the professor was trying to convey which is THEIR fault, not the professor's. He made it pretty easy to understand what was expected of us, but due to the students' narrow thinking they never got the memo. Hence the ratings.

Enjoyable summer course that wasn't hard at all! I wrote my notes down by hand and hardly studied. He talks about his life experiences, but I wouldn't say it doesn't relate to what's covered in class. The course was manageable as the workload was just right. The ppl complaining about politics are the ones that can't handle differing opinions. Thx!

Very lenient grader. Each lecture was filled with random storytimes about his life. Truly a flight of ideas. The class itself is very easy, but it was difficult to retain anything because he was constantly going off topic. Would bring up politics mid-lecture while being unprofessional about it at times. Caring professor but isn't for everyone.

Super easy Maymester!!!! Was very manageable with working full time and homework and exams were straight  forward. Goes over every review before the exam and even helped with the essay proposal. Only had part was mandatory attendance and participation MATTERS !!!!

Dr. Clark was probably the best professor I have ever had at UTA.   The exams are straight from the lecture and very straightforward. Just pay attention and you will pass the exams. I do not know why he has such a bad rating, but don't listen to them, it was probably students who don't do anything and put zero effort. Would highly recommend.

If you're good at sitting there and smiling and doing whatever a professor decides to make you do, you might be alright. But for the average student, Mark Clark is going to be one of your worst professors. Opaque grading, 90 is high grade usually. Constant political pandering, career bragging, and no concern for academic privacy.

I honestly don't think he's as bad as everyone makes him out to be. He does steer off topic a lot during lectures but I think his notes package is helpful. He wants his students to succeed and he just wants you to try. Just study the notes package and listen to his lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Words that describe “Dr.” Clark: cruel, arrogant, and narcissistic to name a few. Full of himself that he wants us to believe that he was so well off before getting a PhD when his dad mostly carried his career. Thinks he's the smartest person in the room by his non-stop praise of himself (who asked). Don't ask for clarification or he berates you.

He's full of himself. Harps that his lectures are important and that they are what the quizzes are based off of, but you'll be struggling to decipher what information is actually relevant, and what is him bragging about his life story/ Will ask questions to the class, but cut someone off the moment they start speaking and go into his own tirade.

I took MANA 4322 this summer and the class went very well! The professor lectures for majority of the class, but he has a lot of experience that is beneficial to life outside of school. Quizzes are straight forward and assignments were graded fairly. He really cares about the success of his students. I recommend taking his class.

Absolutely avoid this class! Unclear formatting, unrealistic grading expectations, and useless lectures. Skip semester if only option. Average class grade per assignment was low 60s, highest individual was low 80s, no A's. Forced hybrid which hinders learning.

Tips:Do the extra credit! Work needs pro-industry level, feedback is copy-pasted.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought I would be able to take this course online, but definitely not. If you are taking more than 4 classes do not add this to your registration. The assignments are very extensive and lack clarification plus the professor is a tough grader. These two combinations equal a failing grade. Good luck if you take this course, you will need it.

Do not take this professor. Very specific format he wants everything written in. Is unorganized, and had 3 different versions of the syllabus within 2 weeks. He literally threw a temper tantrum in class because only about 1/4th of the class brought in an assignment that wasn't clearly assigned or explained. Just rants about how important he was.

do NOT take this professor. He likes to brag about himself and rant endlessly. He likes to claim he is "preparing you for the corporate world" but he goes about it by belittling you and saying that he knows more than you because he has worked for many corporations. (once again, bragging about his endless expertise). take anyone else!

He does not lecture, instead he rambles for about half the class time then the other half you work on group projects. After talking about nonsense for half the class, he dumps work on you after no teaching or explanation.  I dropped the class immediately because of the structure of the course. I highly advise to stay away from this prof.

This professor tends to talk about himself a lot as if you were place in a corporate setting in the workplace. He tends to go a bit off topic on the class at times. This professor is good but he's a tough grader when it comes to case assignments. Do ask questions in person or outside of class; very accessible! Quizzes are straight from textbook.

Dropped this class ASAP because prof made it impossible to succeed. Lectures nonsensical and rambling. "In-class" assignments became weekend projects because he gave us no time to work. Cancelled a presentation the day it was due. Changed instructions for assignments as we were turning them in. Expectations were conflicting and changed constantly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is way of explaining assignments is really difficult to be understood. He talks like if you are in corporate setting. His responses to emails are difficult to be understood.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment:
The class itself isn't very rigorous, the only difficult assignments are the group project deliverables. The professor is very egotistical and can be condescending at times. Be prepared to be called-out in front of your peers for an arbitrary nonissue.

Each quiz in the class is online and open-book. Fairly easy to achieve an A.

I loved this class. This class prepares you what it would be like to be in a professional setting. Better to get experience here than in the real world. Make sure to participate and look at how he wants the format to be done. Not a class where you want to show up late or miss.

He's very straightforward when giving feedbacks but they are very helpful. He treats his class like a corporate setting which could help you work more efficiently. Lots of bonus points and extra credits opportunities. heavy on projects and papers. Be sure to follow his examples and guidelines.

I took this professor during the winter. He talks to his students as if we are in a corporate setting. READ the cases and chapters BEFORE class. PARTICIPATE!  He is good at remembering names so it is best to show up to class on time and be as professional as you would be in a workplace (ie don't show up in pj's). Quizzes are easy and open book

He's straight forward and direct. Be prepared to be involved in class activities and to answer questions out loud. He's the best professor to take compared to the other professors in this department. Quizzes/tests are okay, but the project is challenging.

Don't know why his ratings are so high. Worst professor, talks down on UTA any chance he gets especially since he's from UTD. Doubts our generation and says we won't make it. His group project is the worst, he puts down every idea you have, extremely moody to the point where he'd yell sometimes and take students outside of class to "lecture them"

His grading criteria can get confusing.  I felt like I had to read between the lines.  He is very inspirational and passionate about his teaching.  He currently doubts our generation's ability to work in a corporate setting.  Gets sidetracked a lot.  Grading is tough.  Kind of sensitive.  Own expectations are too high.

I took his may-mester 2022 and was SO worried, but it was one of the best classes I took. We did have to go to class to get participation credit and you actually have to do the work which is scary to hear (from someone who only studies in class). Hes very smart and lets you work on projects in class. 10/10 from me. Graded fairly, but do your best!
Good.

Hands down a good professor. The guy is very understanding and knowledgeable. Make sure to connect with him and actually get to know him beyond a professor. The class is meant to be challenging and it takes a lot of work at times.

Took him for maymester and honestly he was great. Hes new to UTA so he still makes effort in remembering names and knowing his students. Basically, if you participate and make sure he knows you're trying, you'll pass. He made the Ford assignment and group case analysis super simple, and the quizzes had multiple attempts. He talks ALOT but worth it!

Ok, this class was far more difficult than it needed to be. I loved her as a lecturer, she's great, but she insists on using archaic testing practices. I didn't even know scantrons were still a thing. She also doesn't let you use a laptop to take notes. Sucks because I think she's a great professor, but given those two issues, take at your own risk

90% of the class is here for the credit yet she still assumes that we all know stuff about biology and anthropology, the tests are pretty much made for people who are actually doing some sort of biology major or anthropology major. There is also so much work and a $90 textbook which honestly shouldn't be mandatory but unfortunately is.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She assumes you know everything before she begins to teach. Her form of teaching is for people who already know the material and/or are studying anthropology not for the people who know nothing about the subject. Goes very fast and you have to pay for a $90 textbook just to do the homework. horrible and would not take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Get ready to memorize! Dr. Cleghorn is very kind and definitely knows her stuff. However, she also expects you to know your stuff. She tries her best to make her lectures entertaining while still packed full of information. I did not think she graded unfairly at all. The second exam is very difficult, but the essay over the book is graded easy.

Idk why there are so many negative reviews! I have taken many classes with Dr. Cleghorn and have only had truly good experiences. She always includes extra credit and is understanding of life, which can't be said for a lot of professors. My favorite classes have been with her because they have been the ones I have learned the most in. Recommend!

I can't stand this class. While the material isn't hard, it's too much information at once and too much work, because this lectures are fast and feel pointless. Mandatory $90 book with built in quizzes. Reading aside from the class book and an essay on it. If you'd like to have time to actually focus on your major, pick another science core.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I wish the university would hire someone else. She seriously has a quiz due the same weekend we're supposed to study for the midterms...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Stay away. 

Unfortunately, Pearson bought her out to sell a book with homework locked behind an 80-dollar digital book.

Are we really that far from education that we are now PAYING to do homework...?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor feels compelled to make her class the hardest one possible. You go from one section to the next with no chance of mastery of any of it. The tests are incredibly challenging. She makes everything comprehensive and then just tests the tiniest amount. She focuses on muscles and ligaments even though it is an OSTEOLOGY(bone) class.

The class is cool because you're working in a lab with real bones but the exams are ridiculous. Students don't have adequate time to learn the bone features & there's no word banks for the exams. As an intro level osteology course, the professor has ridiculous expectations of what she wants the students to learn & doesn't make the lab portion fun.

Cleghorn is an AMAZING teacher online, but her in person lectures are really rushed and the exams are rough. A lot of the content that you're expected to know isn't in the text book and you don't have much time with each bone set. No extra lab days offered and the cast skeleton that you can check out isn't great. No extra credit or grade curves

I LOVED and learned so much from this class and Dr. Cleghorn. You will have to work for your grade though, it's not an easy A. Practical quizzes every week, notebook drawings, and two exams seems pretty daunting and it would be if not for the extra credit. If you give an effort you will get so much more from this class than just a letter grade!

Get ready to read and do your part. She gives you everything you need to do well but it's on you to pass. She offers plenty of extra credit for her osteo class, not for her theory class. Quiz every Friday in both classes. She knows her stuff and is obviously very passionate. I'm looking fwd to bioarch next semester.

Really loved this class last semester that it made me change my major to anthropology. Class was pretty fun, pay attention to lectures not everything is written on the power points t good notes. Quizzes. Taking her again this semester for Human Osteology.

I am taking her again for another class this semester and plan to take her yet again. Very clear cut. Gives opportunities for extra credit. Made me fall in love with anthropology so much I am doing a minor in it.

She's a great professor and really cares about her students and the material. Tests are extremely tough, so be ready for that. You have lab grades and worksheets to help your grade out though. Overall, I would definitely take a class taught by her again, but if you don't need this class or aren't that interested in the material then I would pass.

Dr. Cleghorn is a fantastic professor. Her lectures are packed with information, so take copious notes, you'll need them. Her exams are tough, but doable, just study and you'll pass. If you flake out, then you'll have problems. Her labs are a lot of fun, lots of hands-on work. Would recommend to any AnthropologyArchaeology majors.
Amazing professor. Obviously cares about teaching, and goes the extra mile for those who show that they will put in the work.

Dr Cleghorn is an excellent professor, well versed in topics, giving applicable exercises, and very invested in the success of her students. Exams are hard, make sure you study, but they are doable. She is a fantastic lecturer and professor in general!

Dr. Cleghorn expects a lot because we are college students. The class was very interesting, challenging, and she goes over material numerous times.  Loved the grading system and test were challenging but she offers extra credit that goes directly towards your final grade.  Go to class, and if possible, go to tutoring and SI.  Loved her class!
Dr. Cleghorn is extremely fun and down to earth. She welcomes questions and provides a great learning environment. I will be taking another class of hers next semester!
AWESOME CLASS!!!!

When I enrolled in this class, I was REALLY excited about it. I am a biology major, and have taken some seriously challenging courses, but I got a D. Her tests were unnecessarily hard. During the final, one student put her head down and visibly "gave up." She offers extra credit, probably because she doesnt expect anyone to pass her crazy tests.
I could have taught this class better than this woman. She is unclear, and boring!
Great teacher and awesome class!!! You just have to be willing to do the work.

Dr. Cleghorn is passionate about what she teaches, which makes the class interesting and fun. She is very thorough but relies on you to read the chapter ahead of time, which is easy-reading. There are 3 midterms, one final, a few online worksheets, and PLENTY of extra credit. She also brings fossils to class! Cleghorn is my fave, hands down!

She is a good prof. She is not always clear when she lectures, she doesn't always emphasize what is what actually on the test. Just make sure to cover all of the bases and LISTEN when she give the review. gives LOTS of extra credit opportunities

Amazing Prof! attedance is NOT mandatory however, i reccomend showing up because the slideshows arent enough to understand the content. The tests arent extremely difficult, you will do fine as long as you study.

Dr. Clark is one of the best teachers I had for my first semester as he actually cares about what he teaches and his students. Some of his exams may be tough but as long as you put effort into the class it's definitely doable. He also does in class demonstrations that are pretty funny

Amazing teacher! He makes sure that the class understands concepts, and the class is not difficult at all. The exams and homework were super easy as long as you paid attention in class. The attendance as not graded but it is smart to attend classes since the exam is lecture heavy. Very fun professor over all, recommend taking him in the future.

This is a very easy class if you engage with the material and also ask any questions while in lectures. Dr. Clark is very knowledgable and is very accessible during his set office hours so do not be hesitant to ask for additional help when needed!
Grades are really only affected by practice exams and exams. Make sure to study for both of them even the practice ones. The lecture is kinda boring, but I still went because he's nice.

An excellent professor! Super engaging and explained the bio concepts really well. Don't be afraid to ask questions during class, he's very patient. DON'T skip class! Everything you need to know is said during his lectures. He provides additional material for to look through for extra help. Put effort into this class and you'll do good!

Watch and take notes over pre-recorded lectures BEFORE CLASS. His lectures can be a bit boring and overloaded with info. He provides plenty of study materials in Canvas. if you put in the time and effort, you'll do just fine. Take advantage of office hours and supplemental instruction (UTA ASC)

You cannot pass by only reading the book. The prerecorded lectures are what helped me the most. There are many study materials provided for each module. Go to his office hours -- they are very helpful. He is encouraging, and I recommend him for Bio 1441.

Don't need textbook if you watch & take good notes over pre-recorded lectures. You CANNOT pass just by attending in person lectures. Office hours very helpful. 13 Module quizzes. I put in 10+ hours a week. (A) on all 3 unit tests. All 4 tests including final equally weighted, lowest dropped. Work hard through the semester, final can be optional.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He gives us videos for each module which really helped me. Overall Id say if youre able to put in the work this class is not difficult. It is time consuming but he does a good job at explaining everything.

Dr. Clark is a great professor and he is very attentive to your questions, so don't hesitate to raise your hand during class. He posts all his powerpoints and even provide extra materials to prepare for exams. The subject is quite difficult if you don't spend time with it, but with everything that is given in class, you will do just fine!

Dr. Clark is a great professor. His lectures do get a bit boring, but his powerpoints are very straight to the point. They cover a lot of what's on the test and really do help. An A is possible with studying. Tests are departmental. Take advantage of his office hours, he is willing to help explain concepts and is overall a really nice professor.

Professional but approachable. Very solid lectures. Plays biology music videos before class that can help you remember some topics. Attendance is taken through eco360 (free online version of a clicker). Definitely knows his stuff. Gets through the info but doesn't rush it.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is wonderful. He is caring about your grades. If the class doesnt understand something, he explains it in a different way. He makes jokes and loves when you the class laughs. He also shows a lot of videos too which makes his class less boring. Everyday you also answers questions (doesnt have to be right) for attendance.

Hes honestky amazing!! His voice is a little monotone so class may tend to get boring every once in a while but DONT skip!!!! Dont skip. You will need lecture to pass. I never read the book & did fine, do practice quizzes & NOTECARDS!!! It is a pretty difficult class but he made it enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is a strong professor. Lectures are good and include videos and pictures to help illustrate the more complex parts of Biology. In lecture, his voice is a bit monotone, so grab whatever you need to stay up in his class. Do not be afraid to ask him questions, he'll respond to you. Overall, this class was with him was good.

He is the best BIOL1441 professor, so if you have the opportunity, TAKE HIM. His powerpoints are effective and neat. I found that the best way to get an A in this course is to read the book and do the practice tests on Mastering Biology. Take advantage of his office hours to ask him questions. Skipping is not a winning strategy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is the best 1441 professor at UTA. His powerpoints are nice and condensed with lots of visuals. The tests are departmental, not many trick questions. If you go through the Clark's powerpoints, read the book, and do the practice on masteringbio, you will be set. Unfortunately, he doesn't teach 1442. I don't think anyone can compare.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is such a cool and caring guy! He plays Biology- related music videos at the beginning of every lecture and always cracks science jokes. He's kind of like a cool, sciencey grandpa. The course is pretty easy to understand, but will consist of a lot of reading and studying. Overall, great professor and I would definitely take him again!

His lectures are straight out of the book but that does not mean you should not read the book. Most of the concepts for the test are in his slides but are more descriptive in the book so it would be best to read. He is pretty funny at times but can be pretty monotone as well. He is better than other professors that teach this course so I've heard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: i believe Dr. Clark is a really cool person and he explains things really good in his lectures. He warns everyone to read the textbook, which you SHOULD. I really wished I studied a bit harder because even if i felt the tests were easy, I didn't get the grade i wanted. Use his office hours if you can and study biology pretty much everyday
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Clark knowing he was probably a new prof because he didn't have a rating on here yet, but I personally think he's the best prof, besides Frederick, to take for 1441. His lectures are easy to follow and his notes on Echo are great to review from. He DOES warn you to read the textbook so take his advice before complaining about lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark makes solid attempts to provide the material in many different forms: powerpoint, music videos, and educational videos. The pace of the class is fast by design, so reading the material before class is imperative to a good grade. You will not get an A in this class if you do not read the book, his lectures simple supplement the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's not that great of a lecturer and is kind of boring. And he is super vague when it comes to question. Rarely gives a direct answer because he want you to connect the dots. You'll really have to study on your own to pass these exams. It's not that they're hard its that there is so much information given in a short amount of time. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is really awesome, shows lots of videos. Easy to relate to. Class is test heavy so you better show up to lectures and read the book. Not an easy A, you need to put a lot of work into the class. 3 midterms and 1 final compose of grade. Overall really a cool dude and a great professor.

Physics in general depends on a lot of self-studying. Overall, he did have a rocky start but it was his first year teaching. People complain about the practice exams, but it's just supposed to be used as a reference and give you an idea of possible exam questions/the format. Redo the HW, make sure you understand the concepts, and you'll be fine.

He seems like a nice guy but doesn't know how to teach lectures. He wants you to get the material but has a hard time getting points across. He also put out “practice tests” that apparently aren't supposed to be reviews? then didn't get why the test averages were still 50s. He will round the class, nice, but thats not useful for learning material.

Although very knowledgeable, I just do not think he is a good teacher. He does not know how to deliver points across to students and just can not teach in general. He is very caring and even gives a 30% curve at the end of the semester, however, if you really need the material for majors then you are lowkey cooked.

He's amazing and is extremely passionate about physics. Will bluntly tell you what you got wrong/need to improve on. He is also accessible outside of class during his office hours or (optionally) on discord. Always updates class in-person, canvas, and/or discord which you have to try to not see. He will laugh in your face... if you CHEAT OR USE AI.

The TA was very negative and rude. He talked down and mocked students, laughing in their faces. His favorite words were "its not my problem" and "oh well". If we had any complaints for the lab coordinator he said "he will laugh in your face". He announced the exam through a discord channel that was optional and the syllabus date was wrong.
A very caring Teacher, most fun Lab I have had here at UTA and he understands the struggles of being a student and ensures you learn the material while having fun.

Lectures are pretty boring and not super useful if you normally don't respond well to lectures. I would read the book and use the guided notes she posts. Does test reviews in class. Overall not a bad teacher, very encouraging.

I feel like I learned everything from Adults from either YouTube or Ms. Roberts as student success. Her lectures are long and boring and she takes super long pauses during them then kind of trails off from her thought process. Exams aren't too hard but definitely attend the student success exam reviews

It feels like she just reads from the slides, so I feel like there is no need to attend class. She takes these awkward long pauses in between bullet points like she's reading what to say next. There is not another professor to take for this class as it is required to take so just be prepared to teach yourself

i did not go to class, mainly just used the powepoint slide notes to make my notes and watched lecture from echo360. her kahoots had some important points that were on the exam so pay attention to her explaination to the questions. USE SAUNDERS BOOK!! it helped with the practice questions some were similar to the exam.

Medsurg is the most difficult class of J2 (imo), however, I found it easier than foundations because tests are straightforward and content feels like review. For tests, use the PowerPoint speaker notes to study, and focus on topics covered in the blueprints (also student success). Use dynamic quizzes to study for CAP. Final is easy. Good luck!

Accidentally released two different ATI exams and only made a statement after everyone had started the assessment resulted in many students preforming under expected proficiency level . Refused to take accountability and ignored all emails regarding problem . Unprofessional and lacks necessary communication

She's pretty great compared to J1 professors. Answer emails fast and to the point. The lectures are a bit dry. Use her PowerPoint notes since she copy & paste them from the textbook. MedSurge can get a bit boring and that might get to you. Final Exam is a saving grace.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I really liked her lectures. If you ATTEND HER LECTURES, MAKE GOOD NOTES AND PRACTICE SAUNDERS NCLEX QUESTIONS, YOU ARE GOOD.

Professor Cleary is a great teacher, her lectures were good there is lots and lots of reading the worksheets are very helpful but again there is a lot of reading and writing, the worksheets will help on the exam do good on the ati to score a level 1 or higher if not you will have to do the templates and it's a lot, overall great teacher.

Her lectures are terrible and consists of multiple typos and grammatical errors, making learning the material difficult.  I find it quite disturbing this is overlooked when UTA expects otherwise from students.

Hardest class of J2 nursing right here. Although professor Cleary is nice and answers emails pretty quickly, the material in this class is heavy. I couldn't find the right way to study for her exams until the last one. However, she does give an optional way to boost your CAPP phase 2 grade and that's an awesome opportunity so don't miss out!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Donna is pretty nice. This class is kind of moderate in intensity. Easier than research and psychiatrics for sure. Do the reading and use Saunders NCLEX practice questions. Option to up your CAPP score by completing learning templates. 2nd half of med/surg content with textbook covered in critical care so they give opportunity to boost grade!

Med/Surg was one of the easier J2 courses for me. With that being said, it is not easy. She is a little dry as a lecturer, but she is nice. Make sure to prep for the CAPP testing, its a little tough for this course. Option to move up a level on the ATI CAPP testing!

Mrs. Cleary is pretty nice. This class is a lot like foundations, just focusing on fewer areas, but more in-depth. An A in this course is definitely possible if you do all the reading. Use ATI and Saunders Practice Questions to study. Use her blueprints as a guide. This class is not difficult to pass!

This class was a little hard. I thought Cleary's lectures were useless. The best way to study for her exams is to do her reviews and do LOTS of practice questions from places like PrepU, Saunders, Student Success etc. Her handouts just had too much useless information and didn't really help. Focus a lot on how to apply nursing interventions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had no trouble with Cleary she seemed okay enough as an online prof. Take advantage of PrepU as EC, exam blueprints are helpful and actually reflect exams & ATI was the most challenging for me. It does actually cover MedSurg/Critical Care so I would begin practice ?'s/Cathy Parkes on YT ASAP. You can redo quizzes at the end for a higher grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Her tests are hard. Some of her test questions were very oddly worded and she does not give much direction as to what she wants you to focus on when studying. I did not find her reviews very helpful. You really just have to know your stuff to get through the exams. Another fun tidbit, the ATI exam covers material from both Med-Surg & Crit Care.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not caring, not friendly, and doesnt belong in the nursing program. She doesnt give you the time of day.

She is not clear at what she expects out of students as a clinical instructor. She doesn't have a caring attitude. Also, she is not interesting in talking to her students. My clinical group barely saw her smiles every week. I would not take this professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class is really easy. There are a lot of projects, but as long as you work on it throughout the semester, you should be fine. There are tests every couple of weeks, but you get to work on them in a group. I would definitely take Cleary. She tries to make it interesting, she let us leave early sometimes, and she made us cookies.

This class should be an easy A for all students. The class feels very overwhelming in the beginning (lots of assignments), but none of the homework is very hard. Make sure you start your Portfolio project early.  A laptop is recommended because Ms. Cleary goes through her lecture slides very quickly.  She rarely kept us for the entire class period.

Great professor I strongly recommend! Took his class as a summer course and the workload wasn't bad. He has quick response times to emails. Overall he was an awesome professor and I would definitely take another class of his

Took his online 8 week course. Textbook was used for a couple questions on tests and for the group project, I would recommend just getting it free on Libgen. There were 4 exams that were pretty easy. He gives test review flash cards that basically gives the answers to the test. Gives nice feedback on assignments. Easy grader and cool professor!

Took 8 week class. Bought book but don't need. Very organized w/power points; tests come from here. Only 4 exams, simple group project, discussion board. Quick to answer emails or offer help. Very knowledgeable. Wants you to succeed. Grades quickly. Highly recommend Dr. Clark.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took his class online in the summer and it was organized pretty well. It allowed me to do the lectures and exam whenever I could as long as I met the deadline so I had plenty of time to study and still enjoy my weekends plus work full time. The lectures have everything you need to know for the exams. Not difficult at all and not heavy workload.

I took his accelerated online comm law class, which was pretty simple. Didn't require much work for an accelerated course. His recorded lectures are super informative, and he's quick to respond to emails. You're graded on some discussion posts, a simple group project, and five open-book tests that he has nice reviews for.
Great professor, lectures are lengthy.
Don't remember much from the class but Prof. Clark was very helpful. Probably the best usage of tech of any professor I had during the semester. Can't recommend highly enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Clarks class was very insightful and thought provoking. I took him for the summer five week session and the course load wasnt as heavy as I thought it would be. Theres plenty of lectures but as long as you take good notes and fill in some gaps from the book, you should pass. Would definitely take again

Straight to the point, just watch the lectures and you will be good. He even had specific videos to help prepare for the exams, I took 8-week class so it was a lot of work since the class was short. Had group assignments but they were really easy (summarizing a court case and then make a creative way of presenting it like an infograph)

Class was fully online. Content was broken into modules with 3-4 midterms, non-cumulative. Lectures covered the chapter material well. Tests were easy. We had a group project where we had to study a comms-related court case. Easy enough course, and it was asynchronous so you could watch the lectures whenever so long as you took the test on time.

He's great at specifying in his lectures whether something is for informational purposes or if it will be on the test. His lectures are clear, interesting, and relevant. A paper is due at the end of the semester, but he provides an idiot-proof template. He's responsive. His tests are not passable if you skim the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this course online earlier in the year and would definitely recommend it. The material can be more interesting than you might think. I enjoyed this class much more than I thought I would and it also was not difficult. No surprises or weird grading, everything clearly laid out in syllabus. Would take him again.

You HAVE to come to class in order to pass. There's no other way. There's specific things he covers in lecture that reflect exam questions. Hard to earn an A. Most class get B's and some C's. Does exam reviews which help.  He's very kind and lenient but expects alot from you. Four exams- 60 questions. 1 legal brief, and a discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Go to class, take notes (he doesn't post them to BB), and make an effort to study notes. You have to do a law brief that is specific to communication and the U.S. He'll offer some insight if you ask for help. The tests are difficult. Also, make an effort to at least attend one class the first week -- he does not check the list every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is really cool. Very approachable about everything. If you can, take this class over the summer. It's kind of boring, but Dr. Clark makes it interesting by relating it to our culture.
If you're good taking notes, you won't need to buy the book. Tests are fairly easy.

His lectures are long and kind of boring and it's not exactly a class you'd look forward to going to every day. The tests are 60 questions and he likes asking about specific court cases, so make sure you study those. It's not the most exciting class in the world, but it's not terribly difficult, either.

You have to go to class in order to receive the notes.  He utilizes Blackboard, but doesn't put notes on it, if you attend class & take notes there isn't a need for the textbook & the study guides are also posted online.   If you plan on being absent buy the textbook!  4 test, 2 discussions, & 1 legal brief.

Dr. Clark is a mediocre prof. I had to do extra readings from the book to do well on his exams. There is a lot of material covered on each exam, and you need to start on the study guide early. He is helpful if you ask him questions. Class was boring and long but some topics were interesting.

I'm not sure what the hype about Clark is. He's a mediocre lecturer at best-- glossing over the material. In addition, his reviews are useless. I felt at times we were tested over material that we didn't go over.

Great teacher! He knows what he is talking about and has a sense of humor too! I did not buy the book and have passed with a B or higher on each of his tests. You MUST attend class and take notes! There is no other option, if you want to pass. I would recommend him!

Clark is one of the smartest professors at UTA, you could try and blindside the man with a thesis like question and he will give you a strong response. An easy A I got a C but missed 2 months of total class time

He is one of my favorite professors. He is very helpful and honest. Definitely on of the more understanding professors i've had as well. He has high expectations for students but truly wants to help you reach that.

I took the class online during Fall 2014 (8 week). Just watch all the video lectures and take detailed (outline format) notes. Glance through the terms in the chapters and summary at the end- then take the test. You'll pass every time- no need to read through the chapters as the lecture has 97% of everything that is going to be on the test. Easy A.
Great professor. Makes a relatively boring class somewhat interesting. Tests can be tough but just go to class, take good notes and study the reviews.

The best guide to this class will be taking good notes!! Attending class is a must because the power points presented will only be shown during class time and not on Blackboard. Try to keep awake, this class may get slightly boring as the long lectures continue the entire semester.
great professor explains everything well material is boring but uses recent cases to try and keep it  interesting
Tough guy to listen to. Don't bother buying book. You don't use it. Boring Class. Watched Videos for 80% of course.
If you go to class and take good notes, you'll do fine.  Never needed the book!  Everything is on the powerpoint presentation, and he'll help you if you ask.
Great Teacher. Easy to understand and clear. Test questions come from powerpoint. Very nice guy!!! I recommend him for this class.
ONLY professor you can take for Electronic News...class is an 8 a.m. class...he is monotone...doesn't talk about his experience much...he is Dr. Andrew Clark so go figure.
best teacher at UTA
Clark is a good teacher, his intro class is a bit tough, but for everything else he is pretty easy.
He might be easy for radio classes, but dont take him for intro to broadcasting. His tests are hard for an intro class.
No Comments
This guy is a good teacher, sorta hard sometimes, but he wants you to learn more than most in the department do.

would not take again, unreasonably strict on daily grades, okay lectures but will grossly understate the importance of certain aspects of assignments making it difficult to know what she really wants out of you.

I love her, she is funny and she explains everything well. even though attendance is mandatory she makes it easy to go to class and she often has off days which balance it out. her no phone policy is easy to follow. 10/10, this is my 2nd semester taking her class and i have no regrets!!

Cindy Malone is a great professor she loves her work, and she is always willing to help most of the people who say she is bad just don't understand that she wants the best her work is not much, but it is challenging, attendance is required but she does give off days and does let out fairly early. Just respect her rules and you will pass. Best one

To put it simply: just don't. take someone else for English. If you do decide to take her, the main problems you'll encounter are: attendance strict, no phones, unreasonably strict grading, ans not understanding.

Great teacher, she is strong minded but her lessons truly are great. The explanations for the essays is very helpful. She explains class very well and is actually funny. Does peer reviews which I find really great ! One of the best English teacher I've had. If you do the work you'll get an A.
Although she explains her slides well, when she grades things she grades them very roughly. She does answer questions her students have though. I would say she is also a little strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory and absolutely do not be on your phone. It felt like I was back in high school when I was in her class. There are no exams but occasionally quizzes over the book you have to buy. 3 excused absences and once you reach 9 absences, it is an automatic fail FYI :). Dont pay for this class

Requires attendance at her very bland and pointless lectures; additionally, she bans phone usage as if we're not grown adults in college. Please never get sick or skip a lecture, as you will have points docked, and she rarely responds to emails. If no other professors are available, take 1301 next semester.

As long as you show up to her lectures and do the assigments as she instructed, you will be fine. I   personally am not the strongest when it comes to language arts and yet I was able to attain a good grade. Her lectures are key to passing the class.
Do NOT listen to the reviews in here they are all lying and sad they can't use AI for their assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Malone isn't what a lot of her reviews state she is. There's a lot of slander, but I strongly believe that these come from people who did not understand or find a middle-ground with her. She WILL talk to you, she WILL support you. She has passion in what she teaches and prepares you for. Inspired me to swap my major to English.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She grades very harshly, gives little feedback, and struggles to explain the material. Her lectures are boring and unhelpful, and she often seems confused about the topics. Avoid this class if possible — she should not be teaching.

She is very very funny, she will teach you want you need to know and what you need to pass. Dont come to class= dont get a good grade. most classes you can get away not going. It might be worth your money to go to this one.

I understand where some of these other reviews are coming from, its the people that dont show up to class. I come to a good bit of classes, but if you miss a class expect to miss vital information. She literally couldn't make it any easier for you to get the papers done as she does it with you.

Her feedback when grading is subpar to put it mildly, and she'll give you a rude attitude if you ask questions. Extremely unforgiving grading that's flat out arbitrary, and I received a 5/100 because I was accused of using AI when I didn't even use Grammarly, nor use AI of any kind. Whimsical grading and unreasonable workload, NEVER TAKE THIS CLASS
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She can be a bit blunt but she is overall a very straightforward professor and always tries to keep the class engaged. She grades very well and usually prefers paper work to digital.
She is a very detailed teacher, she will help you if you need it. She is a bit strict on her assignments but overall it's not hard.

Professor is very strict when it comes to grading papers.While they did make lectures somewhat engaging by being silly and fun during lectures, they would get off track very easily and could make class confusing.Professor feels very much like a "high-school teacher"in there teaching methods and overall energy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Malone is very down to earth and straight-forward. All assignments build on each other and main papers are graded strictly but clearly. All main papers had outlines of exactly what she expected and if you stuck to those, then you'll do great. She gives adequate time for assignments and they never seemed too difficult. would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I absolutely LOVED this professor. As an English Major she encouraged my passion for writing. As long as you do the work and come to class your set.

I will not recommend her class if you have other difficult classes or taking more than two, this class will consume most of your time. Had to drop due the ridiculous amount of work and affecting my other courses. She has high expectations for all assignments that will deduct points or fail due to not meeting them. Avoid this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Actually the worst at UTA, avoid her at all costs!!! She is a tough grader and will not give you any help on what to fix. She contradicts her self all the time making instructions very unclear. Very unprofessional teacher that will act like she is 12 meanwhile students are powerless to do anything against her. THE WORST
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Coming from someone who loves English and writing papers, this Professor ruined it for me. She is entertaining and explains concepts well during class but she often made me feel stupid when asking for help when I was confused or needed some guidance.

She was an amazing professor who is incredibly funny, she has clear grading criteria and give amazing feedback when grading. This class is a little hard for those who cannot write so well but she is available to help and there will be a few peer reviews to help with writing.

She not only has a clear passion for English and the development of your writing skills, but she will make sure you are prepared for every assignment. If you're having a hard time understanding, then just ask and she will be readily available. If you're looking for a boring and old school professor, find someone else. Do your work. You'll be fine.

Go. To. Class. She quite often changes due dates, rubrics, and instructions to make things easier, but if you're not in class you won't notice. None of the assignments make sense unless you go to class. The short assignments aren't hard as long as you dedicate actual time to them but on the major assignments I couldn't get anything higher than a B.

Professor Malone is a tough grader, and we had a lot of essays to write but I'm not sure if that's her teaching style or apart of the ENGL 1302 curriculum. This is by far the WORST professor I have ever ever ever had. Toughest grader, she will give you zeros or low grade for no reason. Malone is funny and chill, if you need help or clarification on essays/drafts go to every class and ask her questions when there's time. She's clear on what needs to be fixed if you ask. yeah save yourself and don't take her. She's not understanding at all and will put the blame on you when she doesn't teach properly and unclear about directions. She was bad enough for me to write a review.

reviews.comment: Although I do hold a high opinion of Dr. Cichock and would recommend him to any student, I feel the need to address his pretty scary testing system. It really puts your mentality skills to the test in that you have to memorize 4-5 pages of content and manage to write it in only 50 minutes while he watches the class. Expect a long paper too.

Dr. Cichock clearly knows a great deal about what he teaches, and it is obvious he cares about the subjects and his students, which makes the students feel good. The class is mostly lectures and includes essays with each test, as well as a long research paper due at the end of the term. He grades hard, but tells you where you can improve.

Great professor! Very funny, entertaining, and engaging lectures! He gives short quizzes at various times for extra credit on the exams. The exams can be a little difficult if you don't know what to study, but if you read the book then you'll be just fine. I took him for POLS 2311 first and enjoyed his class so much that I took him again for 2312
Four grades with each worth 25%. Class was taught by four teachers. Dr. Cichock covered the politics of Russia. Good experience overall.

Last upper POLS course to complete my minor. :( Once again, there's 4 grades, 25% each of: 2 tests, 1 research paper, & final. Be ready to read & take notes when you attend lecture. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: I completely forgot to rate Professor Cichock in Spring 2017! Dr. Cichock is witty, sarcastic, and cynical which makes him a fantastic POLS professor. The tests are taken mostly from the lectures, so make sure you take copious notes. However, the lectures are interesting and entertaining, so paying attention is not that difficult.

Literally my favorite professor. I enjoyed his lectures, even though I hated POLS.

He's also really big on current events!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great prof for U.S. Gov. Only three tests make up all of your grades for the course. About a week before each test he will give a pop quiz for extra credit. Pay attention to what is going on in the news. Attendance not required, but his lectures are very important. Book is very helpful for tests. If you study you will do well in this class.

I took Professor Cichock for Summer 1, it was a Mon-Thurs class. Straight up lectures, two exams and one paper. He is a tough grader, so attending class is important to get all the info. If something comes up, he will reason with you. During lecture he can go off on tangents. He will answer any questions, he likes for you to participate.

Dr. Cichock knows his material. He gets into details about certain concept and he doesn't really need to depend on any notes or ppts. He can lecture for about an hour without any hesitation. However, if his lectures can be organized into smaller portions, then students can comprehend it little bit better. Get ready to write his essays!

Dr. Cichock is a great! His classes are solid lectures, but he is funny and very clear. He will answer thought provoking questions and shows no bias whatsoever. He will let honors students contract his class and do almost any assignment they want for the honors college. Only 4 assignments, but they're all essays- moderately tough grader.

Prof. Cichock's lectures covered a very wide spectrum but they were all interesting and helpful. He is very smart and a nice person. The exam reviews are usually given a couple classes prior to the test, go to class or make friends who take good notes. The tests aren't too difficult but you should start the final paper early. Would take again.

He's very clear during class. Doesn't throw his own opinion in during lecture and he's very helpful if you're stuck on a topic. Tests are extremely easy if you go to lecture and do the reading. Final is the last 1/3 of the course, which isn't in the book. He also loves his pop quizzes by the way.

He encourages questions about stuff going on in our Political world so we can understand the policies going on around us and questions about the lecture itself. He has pop quizzes sometimes which are extra credit for your tests.

He is a great teacher, keeps things interesting if you like political science. He will repeat things that are important, as well as if you ask him to repeat something. (He actually encourages it) Though attendance doesn't matter he has pop-quizzes for extra credit! Make sure to READ YOUR BOOK or you will NOT do well in his course.

LOVE him. Such a nice guy. Cares about how you do in his class. Answers questions. Very available to speak to with any questions you might have. Gives you essay questions in advance so you can prepare. While the material at times got boring for me since I don't have a huge interest in Russian foreign policy, I would still recommend him highly.
He is a good professor, but he is boring.
cool.... excellent.. if u are not a poli sci major or similar u might not like his courses
Great Professor... But if you make a 79.99999999999, rest assure you end up with a 'C' in the class!

Probably one of the best teachers I've ever had. When you take one of his courses, you can definetly tell that he actually cares about the student's grade. he's so brilliant! and very good looking- love going to his class.. good sense of humor as well! keep it up Dr. Cichock!

Amazing!!!!! Articulate and commanding, he makes politics seem fun! Read the book and kno the review guide... Go to class and pay attention to the PowerPoint, crucial! Love him, 3 test and 3 quizes for extra credit

Amazing!!!!! Articulate and commanding, he makes politics seem fun! Read the book and kno the review guide... Go to class and pay attention to the PowerPoint, crucial! Love him, 3 test and 3 quizes for extra credit

He is an amazing professor, articulate and fun. Go to class and listen to his lectures. The powerpoints are the most important thing. Know everything on the study guide and you should be good!

3 exams, pop quizzes for Extra Credit and the book is a helpful resource to keep up with lectures but is not needed. His slides are the most important. learn that material and the tests will be all over that.

GOTTA GO TO CLASS. really, if you dont think u can make it, DONT PLAY URSELF, take some1 else. doesnt take attendance but you will be tested on material not only not in the book, but sometimes in the book but he wants u to know HIS DEFINITION. his classes are enjoyable though, very informative.  3 exams, random bonus quizes, doesnt drop a grade.
Good teacher. Fun class. Lets you out early when he gets tired. Exams are hard. You must study but he curves tests and lets you take a bounus quiz for each exam. Printable review for exams
Take his class!!!  He makes politics fun and interesting!!  You do have to study but at least it will be an interesting class.

I took both the Foreign Policy of the Soviet Successor States and Russia Today with him. Not only is an author in this field but he is a good man (not a cocky or spaced out PhD). In order to do well keep reading relevant materials. Most of the time his test review will tell you what you need to know. *Must have class for anyone interested in Russia

He'll make you work for your A, but once you've got his tests figured out it's hard to fail.  Attendance not required but helpful.  Books not mandatory.  Intense research paper assignment.  Great prof - I'm taking another class from him next semester.

probable the best professor i have ever had. he's funny, so that keeps the class interesting and makes it easier to follow the lectures.  to pass the tests you must attend class and take notes on the powerpoint. reading the text is also very important. as long as you read the text and take good notes, you'll do just fine.
He kept my interest in the course material with good commentary, humor, and all the fun stuff. Highly recommended
Fantastic professor.  Not the easiest, but very knowledgable in his field and will take time to individually discuss whatever you'd like to talk about.  Highly recommended for a good education.
Class is mandatory to do well on the exams. As long as you write down the notes from his powerpoints, you should do okay. Can't pass without attending lectures and reading.

He is a top notch professor and expects a lot out of his students. His lectures are interesting and you learn a lot from him. But his tests are very challenging and he loves to make them hard. Best teacher I had in Poli Sci. Still keep in touch with him. Very strong professor.

nice professor... lectures are quite interesting... and the tests are beyond easy... as long as you come to class, you have nothing to worry about

Very personable and very caring. Multiple presentations in-class (very tough grader on these), one major group project that runs the course of the semester (consists of ~10 assignments total), 3 exams, 2 case studies, attendance for a grade.

Professor Retzloff is an amazing teacher, he's great at making the lectures interactive and he cares about his students as well. Make sure to focus on your service learning project and don't be afraid to ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is probably one of my favorite classes I have taken in college, Dr. Retzloff was caring, hilarious and really engaging every single lecture. He made the content of the course easy to follow and was always encouraging the students to interact with him and inspiring us to be better. He really loves what he does and cares for his students.

Dr. Retzloff gave us a group project for the whole semester and asked that we partner with a non profit. Ask him questions and keep him updated on yalls project as he will help yall. He helped us this semester and said the only way someone can fail is if they quit. He is an easy A and gives great life advice each lecture.
