Professor Retzloff is very understanding and the class consists of a group project, 2 case study, 2 exams, and attendance. The exams are very easy and the case studies are done with your group. The project is broken down into parts, you are expected to present but he gives good feedback. If you do the work then most likely you will get an A or B.

Professor Retzloff states that the course is very hard, so you must be prepared to study you cannot wing this course 2 of 3 exams are in person with lockdown browser, the final exam is online and can be taken at home. He has an essay assignment and there is a lecture and lab assessment in this course and he is the lab professor. (Doesn't make exam)

Professor Retzloff does fun lectures and is very easy going. The whole class is a service learning group project where you work with the same group for the whole semester. The project is the midterm and final. Attendance is mandatory and done via sign in sheet. Very easy A would recommend him!
If you want to learn about management on the cooperation world give yourself a favor and take with Dr. Retzloff  He cares about his student wellbeing, very respected, motivational and hilarious!!

This class is relatively easy because there wasn't much workload or exams. The final is a 3-page minimum about topics she chooses for you. However, the lab portion does require a significant amount of time. But the TA provides resources to make it easier. Overall, a good, easy class to take if you need a science class with a lab section.

Easy science credit, recommend taking online. There is a short quiz and one discussion/assignment due each week but nothing hard. Quizzes are easy and assignments can take a little time and research but not hard at all. No exams!! Would definitely take again!

There were only about 4 tests the whole semester, including the Final Exam. She gives review sheets for each exam and everything studied on the sheets are on the exams. I really enjoyed the class, her teachings were amazing and each lecture is recorded so if u miss a class don't worry. Really easy and interesting class! You pass if u do the sheets.

She is very nice. Taking her SCIE 3303 as well now. Her lectures are very engaging, but not participation-heavy. Take notes because the lectures are more useful for exams than the reading. Just pay attention and come to class. Also curves exams!
For GEOL 1330 we didn't have to pay for a textbook, used a free online resource. We did for 3303 though.

Professor Winguth's class is straightforward - her lectures are informative, and she provides helpful study guides for the exams. The material can be challenging, but using resources like Unstuckstudy alongside the textbook and lecture notes can make it manageable.
Easy A class, recommend taking online.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're looking for an easy science credit but don't want to take an in person class this is the one. Class consisted of a weekly discussion/assignment and a quiz which aren't difficult at all. Just be on top of the work every so often and you'll do just fine.
Very good lecturer and put out test guides that were very helpful. If you look over the review you will do fine on every test.

This class was awesome. It takes skill to not get an A in this class, in my opinion. One of, if not, the easiest A you can get on this campus. Take this class online, I don't know how it's like in person but if online, its fun. I love her grading criteria and I enjoyed making the presentation at the end. Such a sweet professor, made my semester.
Pretty easy class! Make sure to attend lectures and take notes in accordance with the study guides. All assignments were straightforward and the group project was pretty simple!

Professor Winguth was really sweet and was available outside of class, she provided great feedback on all assignments. I would recommend studying her lectures and taking notes before each weekly quiz.

She uses all the time given to her on just lecture and in the lecture there are mc questions that she uses to take attendance. The tests are 50 questions long but she puts a curve on every test (even if its not needed). There are a few discussion boards too. Overall a very easy grader.

I took her online Geology course. She is very organized with clear criteria. Sometimes the work load feels a little heavy but it is manageable. She is easy to reach, however sometimes she would tell me to reach out to the TA and the TA would never respond.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The professor was great, with only 3 to 4 discussions and four exams including the final. You have to study the slides and quizlets that previous students made( search geology 1330 Winguth). However, the TA grades very harshly would recommend staying in the lab and working on it and letting her look at it she takes off for every little thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The only real issue I had with this course was the lectures. The PowerPoints she used were bare of information and the lecture was mostly her droning on and on. Very little to no class participation or engagement. The tests were very difficult and had material that was not discussed in class or in the textbook.

Free textbook, clear grading, extra credit, and exam reviews are generally what will come up on the test. Dr. Winguth is a gem who really cares about what she teaches and is willing to help and answer questions. Honestly, take her global warming class -- you'll learn a lot from the lectures. How I perceive the environment now is different.

Extremely knowledgeable about topics covered. Not many assignments, only exams, brief written assignments/discussions on Canvas, and LAB grade. All materials were posted, including a review for every exam. Exams were multiple-choice but challenging. Be sure to get a solid understanding of topics covered by completing the review and studying PPTs.
Her lectures are great! You don't really need to attend, but definitely go if you are able to. Study the slides and study handout she shares and you will easily pass the exams.
This class was very easy to pass, would recommend it to anyone who isn't a science major that needs it for their science core requirement!
Honestly, her lectures were not the most exciting and the 50-question exams were hard if you don't like science.

She is very knowledgeable about what she is teaching, you do not have to go to her lectures, but if you want extra credit you need to attend class. For every exam she posts a study guide, study from those and you'll be good, however the exams were 50 question and were a little hard for me, but if you like science take her, she is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: study her study guides for the test and you'll do just fine! there are lots of quizlets that i used that were helpful. I think i averaged an 88 on the exams but I did the extra credit paper and received a 95 on the group project, which helped bump me to an a. attendance is also extra credit, which helped bump my grade. shes very nice! good luck!
A lot of material to learn, but her study guides are super helpful for exams. She has a few extra credit opportunities and curves exams. She is a great professor, take her as much as you can!
Great and professor, she gives extra credit for attendance and curves exams.

This class wasn't bad at all, you just need to watch her online lectures and do the quizzes, which can be a little specific but really aren't too bad. There's also other discussions and assignments which aren't hard either. I also took the online lab for this class, and as long as you keep up with the assignments, you'll be just fine.

I took her online and it was really easy, most of the grade comes from the quizzes so just make sure to study. Assignments are easy, it usually takes me an hour and a half max to finish them. I also took the lab online which was good as long as you keep up with the due dates. It's an easy A if you do the work.

Dr. Winguth is a great professor. She is clearly an expert on this class. The class itself is not difficult at all. Tests have been easy so far and she hardly gives out any assignments. A lab is required for this class. The lab instructor is also great, but she grades harshly.

Never had any issues with this professor. Assignments were easy and there was no final because of the lab. Labs were easy as well, and the TA grades easy. No need to buy the textbook either, there's pdf's online and I didn't even read it often. About 3 assignments were due a week and at max, they took 2 hours to do. Overall pretty average and easy.

Prof. Winguth was great and was a fair grader. She always sent out reminders about work that was due and gave great feedback. You wont regret taking her class and you will actually gain knowledge from this course.
Easy class and she clearly cares about what she is teaching. Class is done through bi-weekly modules, which is nice. The lab can be difficult but isn't worth too much grade-wise.

i took her for earth history and global warming. global warming is harder but both pretty easy if u just do the study guides and do the participation questions for extra credit in class, u shld be fine. shes a respected professor and there's not a lot of hw either, just a few discussions every now and then. her earth systems class is easy

She was kind and understanding. I didn't have many issues during the semester to test her patience. Tests will cover details from lectures. Slides go along with the lectures and are available to atudsnts. She also allows the lectures to be recorded and to be live streamed. Study guides are also available before every test. It's all very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: The weekly assignments are very easy. The professor also provides valuable feedback when grading assignments. I probably read the book only once or twice. The course ends with a final paper and presentation, which is graded pretty leniently. The professor was always willing to help over email. I definitely recommend this course and the professor!

Took this class online and it was simple, every week she laid out what we had to do. Mainly discussion boards and quizzes. Interesting class! I liked that she sent reminders every time we had something due.

Dr Winguth is a great prof, she really knows what she's talking about and her lectures are amazing. The tests are almost exactly like the reviews and she covers everything you need to know in lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory but she gives extra credit for questions answered in class. Doesn't require a lot of effort to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was an overall easy professor to understand. There was an assigned textbook but never used it. The assignments were discussion posts and quizzes every week that was fairly easy. There is a lab component to this class so it can feel like more work but overall an easy A if all the work is turned in.

Attendance was extra credit, which could help if you need that. Lectures weren't anything memorable, but everything that would be needed on the tests were covered. You aren't required to buy or read the book, but I think for many people that was the difference between a C or B and a high A, if that matters to you.

This class is an easy A! Attendance was counted as extra credit, and tests were super easy. Reviews were helpful and any questions you didn't know were on quizlet somewhere. There were assignments probably every other week and they were an easy 100 if you put in any effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: weekly assignments consisting of discussions and quizzes, not bad but sometimes pretty specific. mostly on quizlet. discussions require watching videos or doing small online activity. she's an easy grader, just answer the questions properly. also, one essay on a natural disaster, 3 pgs very easy.

Cornelia is a real gem and she does a great service for the scientific community. She is able to articulate herself very well, gives plenty of extra credit, allows for creativity, and has a good sense of humor.
Gave extra credit for attendance. Really nice and responds to emails within 24 hours.
Class is straight forward. Exams are based on reviews, bit of discussion post and couple of assignments. Fairly easy course.

Winguth is a good prof & was easy to understand (has moderate accent) The book is not required and there is a pdf version online. The hardest part about this course would be the lab. As long as you go to lecture you will pass. Attendance gets you extra credit points! Overall good teacher and I'm taking her again for GEOL 1302 next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Wonderfully intelligent professor! This class rekindled my love for geology and I'm so happy to have taken it. The class is pretty test-heavy, but the exams are open-note and very straightforward. All the material is from the lectures, but she posts the slides and study guides!

She's a great professor I would suggest def going to lectures because most of the tests are from her lectures. she does do pop quizzes but she lets you know the class beforehand. do well on the lab section too and you'll get an A.

I recommend going to lectures to take notes. Also, she has pop quizzes. Study for tests!! Attendence isn't mandatory but if you go at least 90% of the time to class towards the end of the semester she gives extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I would describe her as a pretty average professor. Her class is easy and while she recommends you buy the textbook, you don't need it for exams. She does have pop quizzes to keep attendance up, but she also posts the slides online if you miss class. Very easy class. As a person, she's nice, but nothing really stands out as "great."

Take it online and all you'll have is one lab day a week plus online tests once a month. Honestly didn't learn anything but it was an easy A and I hate science. Super easy not much more to say about it

easiest class ever. TAKE IT ONLINE. labs are fairly easy but it doesn't even matter bc the actual class is only based on tests! literally required 2% effort. took it with my friends so we did good on all the online exams. take this online classss!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing prof., I took her for geology 1301 and 1302 and it was an easy A both times, all you have to do is go to class, she gives multiple opportunities for extra credit. As long as you follow the reviews she has prepared, the tests are a breeze. The only difference between the 2 classes is that she added pop quizzes (easy)so people would show up
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took this course online and it was great! Professor Winguth has very clear expectations for her online students, and as long as you keep up with the course you will get an A. There are weekly quizzes, discussions, and assignments all of which are very simple to accomplish. As your "final" you write a 3 page paper on a catastrophic event.

Doctor Winguth gives plenty of opportunities for extra credit. Show up to majority of the classes, she will give you three extra points. She gives four homework assignments. You have the option to go to the YET and teach a class of 15-30 elementary grade kids with a group or take a Final with short answer questions. She is always on your side.

Great professor, works with you on missed quizzes if for legitimate reasons. Only graded on lab work, quizzes, exams, & attendance (extra credit). Her lectures are interesting & easy to follow using powerpoints & quizlet. "Random" quizzes but she gives hints when they'll be in lecture. Extra credit is a visit to Perot Museum with question sheet

She's a very nice professor, but her lectures are very boring. She gives three participation points at the end of the year if you show up to class often. There's a group presentation during class, a group essay, an individual reflection paper and a group service learning project at the YET. there's a total of four exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Enjoyed taking her class. One group project graded very leniently, 3 'pop quiz' (she gives you a heads up one class prior), 4 exams. She provides a study guide for each exam so as long as you use those, tests are simple. Missed probably 10 classes and walked away just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: 1st Fall semester at UTA, was pretty nervous, but Professor Winguth made it amazing. If I wasn't a math major, I would totally major in Geology (or minor). Lab is 25% while lecture is 75%. Lecture is divided by 4 quizzes, drop lowest for 9%; 3 exams at 45%; final at 21%. Just study from the material posted on Blackboard & you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I'm a geo major and this class was boring. It's super easy to study for though and Winguth is helpful and explains things clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class is easy, especially if you read the book as well. There are exam reviews before every exam that can be used to study and extra credit opportunities. Dr. Winguth is nice and keeps class interesting, adding video clips and keeping a reasonably fast pace. Tests are multiple choice and not very difficult.

Offers a lot of extra credit. Each test she provides bonus points basically curving the test. If you study the reviews and do the launchpad activities you will be fine. Also all of the questions come from the study guide and launchpad activities.

Attendance not mandatory but will give extra credit added to final grade. Gives Chapter reviews so make sure you do those. Will have to purchase online homework and will drop lowest grade on that. She's good at curving grades and giving extra credit.

She give extra credit for attendance. As long as you follow her study guides and take really good notes from both her powerpoint and skim through textbook, you should be fine. She does give online homework, but it doesn't takes up much efforts. The lab is really easy. I'm not science person and I still managed to maintain A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Winguth lectures to the T of what you need to know for her exams. There is no need for a book and there is no homework. Just show up, listen, take a quiz, and exam. Done. Easy A. However, it is hard to not fall asleep because her voice isn't crazy with enthusiasm. Would definitely recommend her if you want to learn Geology.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Class is only 50 minutes long no matter what days you take it. There's a sign in sheet every time. Tells you a couple of days in advance that there might be a pop quiz coming up. Offers extra credit. Study the previous quizzes for the exams, she takes a lot of questions from them.

This class is so easy. The information is interesting, but it's not presented in a fun way. The tests are exactly the powerpoints, so study those well and you'll do awesome on the exams. Attendance is not mandatory but at the end of the year she'll use the attendance for extra credit.

Winguth gives pop quizzes, but she warns you ahead of time so if you go to class you'll know about them. I found all of the tests and quizzes on Quizlet and just studied those. She has attendance questions but you didn't really have to pay much attention in class. She'll say you need the textbook, but I never even opened mine.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There are only 4 tests and 3 quizzes. She is super boring in lecture but if you show up you get extra credit on the final. Hard to study for tests but most of the material is given in her power points. If you're not smart about the way you study for this class it might be difficult to get an A. Most hated class of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You need to attend lectures. I noticed a clear difference in my test grades when I had to miss a couple classes but I enjoyed her class. She is clear in what is expected and gives great hints at what you can expect on the quizzes and tests - also why you need to attend class. She also makes all lectures available online if you have to miss one.

She has "pop quizzes" but if you go to class she'll tell you the class before that "you probably should study because a quiz may be coming up." She's a good professor and is passionate about geology. Study the PowerPoints and you'll do fine.

She's a really understanding person and very intelligent. Willing to go over things again if you don't understand or missed something. Attendance isn't mandatory but  you have to study for the tests or you won't have a chance. But she posts all the slides online as well as study guides. If you go through the guide, you'll definitely pass.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are clear with everything you need to know. Bought the book but haven't used it. She gives "pop" quizzes but will usually hint when they will be. Has an accent but isn't too hard to understand. Quizzes and tests are pretty straight forward, if you pay attention to lecture slides you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Hard to understand. Makes test difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Relatively easy class if you study before tests. There are pop quizzes but if you go to lecture (which is bonus points) then you will know when the quizzes are.

As someone who only took Geo1302 for a science credit, I found her lectures quite boring. She was quite nice and helpful, but don't assume this class is an easy A. You do have to study for the test, you cannot just show up and pass.

She gives an assignment and a discussion board weekly (for the most part). Nothing is really too difficult. There are no exams, just weekly quizzes in which she gives a review, but some are hard. There is one final project which is a paper and a powerpoint. I made an A in this class, you just have to put forth the effort.

Her lectures are dumb, half the time you have no idea what she is talking about, she doesn't explain things good and goes way to fast for you to even write the sentence she just said before she moves on, gives review half it help the other half doesn't and there is a lot more of the test that isn't on the review of power points. Her test are hard

Super easy A. Posts study guides at the end of each lecture. Do them and get easy A's on all the exams. Gives quizzes but drops the lowest one. Participate in Lecture Tools and get extra credit. Her lectures ate interesting and she uses lots of videos to break up the monotony.
Boring, I did all the study guides and was struggling to get an A, which didn't happen. I feel like I did so much and recieved so little.
She was a good teacher and used good detail in describing assignments.

Amazing teacher and her class is super easy. She gives all lectures and notes online to study with. She shows you pictures and videos and makes the class interesting. All you have to do is show up and take notes and pay attention to her slides.

German broad, but easy to understand. Really nice, if you ask for help and you attend class she'll help. Tests are tough, but I didn't study nearly enough for them. Make sure you attend class, she gives extra points for attendance.

Four test. Four quizzes. Lowest quiz grade is dropped. Every section had a review. She had you answer questions for points for attendance and added a number of 1-3 to your final grade, depending on how many questions you answered. She also gave us a crossword for three points on the final exam.

FIRST OF ALL IF YOU DON'T LIKE SCIENCE DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. While she is a good teach she is extremely boring. The only reason I ever attended class was to  get my participation point on Lecture tools. She gives study guides which are long, and it is HEAVY IN MEMORIZATION! She also has 125 point ACCUMULATIVE FINAL! Should have taken Astronomy!

The lectures are dull, but the class is super easy. As long as you do the study guide you will make an A on the test. The homework is easy, most answers online. She gives 3 extra credit points to your final grade if you come to class 97% of the time.

Records her lectures and supplies slide decks and script - very helpful in an online class.  Read the textbook; some test questions from it.  Provides interesting video links that relate to the material.  Weekly assignments (not too difficult).  Final paper and presentation is 20% of your grade, but she gives you time to do a good job.

Super easy class! Just show up to class, participate by answering her online lecture questions so you can get extra credit points added to your overall lecture grade. Also, don't buy the book because you're never going to use it since she provides online notes and study guides to help you.

I never got the book, just go through the review and you'll be fine. She uses Lecture Tools as a way to keep attendance and participation. Her pop quizzes aren't exactly a surprise either, since she'll give a (not so)subtle hint about those.  Also, it's an intro class where some heavy memorization is required. Read the PP slides, and you'll be fine

Reads stuff off Powerpoints and shows videos. The course itself is easy and she's more than willing to help you out. Pop quizzes, but she tells you in advance and she drops one of four. I got the textbook, but didn't use it. There's not a lot of grades taken, so make sure you get decent grades on everything. Would definitely take her again.

Her class is an easy A if you do all over her study guides & study a couple days before it. She does "pop" quizzes, but she warns you a class day before the quiz is given. You don't need to buy the textbook since she provides everything on BlackBoard. Also, show up to almost all her classes because she does offer extra credit for participation.

Great professor. The course itself is easy. She just lectures each class from powerpoint slides. It can be a little stale but she keeps it interesting with videos. She's very clear, and she just seems like a nice lady. There are "pop quizzes" but she warns you in advance. You don't need the textbook, just go to the lectures and you'll do just fine.

pretty easy prof. does have pop quizzes, but announces them the class before the quiz so it's no surprise. tests are easy as long as you follow the study guides and powerpoints she posts. very funny and nice. book not needed since everything is on the powerpoints. recommended to go to class since you can get extra credit for attendence.

Decent teacher. Took her for geology and she was pretty good. She records her lectures and puts them on BlackBoard. Does the occasional quiz, but lets you know in advance and drops the lowest quiz grade. Powerpoints are easy to follow and she shows a lot of videos. Tries to add a little humor into her lectures, which is great. Take her if you can.

She was a great professor. I took the 1st part of Geology at Northlake & from taking the 2nd part at UTA from this great professor was just as good. The labs weren't bad with the graduate student & the pop quizzes were "unannounced", but technically you knew they were coming. Study the powerpoint lectures and you'll pass easily. :

This is probably the worst class i have taken in UTA. I don't get the general objective of her class, especially after the 3rd test. It became a horrid class on memorization of continent broke up to form what continent during what period class with little emphasis on the significances of those events. Names and #s don't teach students science.

Dr. Winguth tries to make an overview of geology, metrology and oceanography interesting.  She gives homework 5 or 6 times through the semester which is not difficult.  She also provides review sheets for each chapter, take your notes using these review sheets.  Attendance is suggested because she gives random quiz questions during her lecture.

Good professor overall...  Book is decent to help you read ahead, but all the quiz and test questions come directly from her lecture slides and study guides.  Attendance is not mandatory but the quizzes are only announced 1 class prior, and she gives extra credit based on % of attendance.  Class is dry but she has a good sense of humor.

Classes are really dry and consist of mostly powerpoints. Be prepared to study a bit for the quizzes. The exam's are kind of hard as well so extra study time might be needed. She get's to the point with her course though which can be a good thing. Take it with the lab to get an easy grade. I barely did any studying and got a high B.

Good teacher but subject is very dry she does try to give you every attempt to make a good grade in  her class.  Test come from study guides and she gives extra credit in class.  Not a bad teacher to take.

Dr. Winguth is great. Lecture tends to get a little boring since there is so much material to cover. 6 homework assignments, and 4 exams. The final is comprehensive but the study guides help. She also gives back old exams to use as a study guide.
Good teacher. She is organized, friendly and helpful. You do not need the book. It's worth showing up to class because she adds good details to the powerpoints. Her accent isn't bad at all.

Very EASY class. Easiest I've taken at UTA. Everything you need is in the powerpoint slides. Reviews are very plain and simple. Super nice and sweet lady and knows what she is talking about. However, class is so hard to sit through. Very boring. Do not need text book. On homework just use the internet. I would recommend this prof.

Hard class but she gives you everything you need to pass the tests. She gives study guides which are worded exactly like the test. HW is easy and helps your average. I have not used the book at all int his class and Im doing pretty well. Gives some extra credit through out the semester.

Easy subject to take instead of an alternative single science lab class. She has a moderate accent, so sometimes it's hard to understand her. All power points and guides available readily online. Tests solely based on the lectures and power points. A lot of memorizing, but fairly easy class. Boring for non-geo majors.
She is a great professor, but her accent is awesome so it's distracting. He tests can be difficult if you don't study.

The class is not easy, but not really hard either.  She gives straight to the point reviews for tests, which are very helpful.  Extra credit opportunities help too. Notes are clear and no tricks on the test.
Boring class. Uses power points and goes over them in every class. Attendance not mandatory but tests are extremely hard

She's very nice and seems to really enjoy the subject. I thought that this class would be more interesting, but it's just nonstop lecture the entire time. She does give reviews on every test, so that helps! Attendance isn't mandatory and most people just show up on test days. She posts hw on BB, and emails you whenever  a pwrpt slide is up.

I can count on one hand how many times I showed up to this class the entire semester, but I still made an A. Everything you need for the exams is on Blackboard however there are lots of extra credit opportunities that are only handed out during class. She also is helpful and responds to emails quickly. Easy class. Highly suggest her!
Easy A! Attendance isn't mandatory, but extra credit is given in class. tests are strongly based on study guides so it helps a lot. Class is pretty boring, nothing but slides and explaining.

Good professor! Powerpoints are very useful. It is best to use her powerpoints for key information, then look that info up in the book. PAY ATTENTION TO EXAMPLES!!! She likes to test over specific examples of each topic.

Prof. Winguth has a very thick accent. While she provides helpful study guides that outlines exactly what will be on the test as well as posting notes via PDF and powerpoint slides i found it very aggravating sitting through a whole class. However, her test material and study guides are of some benefit.

Exams are now in person and using locked down browser. There is a midterm, final, and COB exam which are all a bit hard. Quizzes are online with locked down browser (no webcam). There is also a group case analysis report and presentation which are a bit lengthy. She is a "chill" professor who gives extra credit opportunities. Optional attendance

A firm but fair grader, especially for the group presentation. She does form the groups at random so hopefully you end up being paired with good people. Graded based on 3 exams (including the COB exam), 5 quizzes, a discussion board, a group presentation, and a group analysis paper. Read and memorize the book and you'll be fine on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I believe this is professors Hart third semester teaching but she makes the class really easy. You're graded on 5 quizzes, a midterm, a final exam, and two case studies but that's really it. Really easy class, and the professor is really sweet so far, makes a typically difficult 4000 class a breeze to get through!

The class was engaging and not too hard. Because I took the 8-week online course, it was just a matter of staying on top of the material. The tests were straight-forward and often taken directly from the assigned readings, so as long as you read, a good score was guaranteed. Good supplemental material + and timely, well thought out feedback
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Long readings, easy quizzes, boring videos.

The exams have nothing to do with the readings/articles/videos she assigns. Good luck with them.

The final project is a sham, she's using our information on our projects for her own research paper. We're just a means to an end for her.

I do not recommend her. Pick a different professor if possible.

By far one of the most interesting classes I've taken. She provides a space every lecture to speak on the topics she's teaching which makes it very different from other classes, and all the more engaging. I definitely recommend taking the class, very understanding and caring professor as well.

she is truly a kind professor and i am so glad i got to take her class. she engages and cares about each of her students and her diversity course, which i took thinking its an easy a and a blow off, actually taught me a lot and stimulated my interest in the subject. i wish i had the opportunity to take more of her classes!

Great class, I took her for a business elective. Super easy if you just do everything on time. I took the half semester course (8 weeks I believe) so it went by fast. Get the ONLINE VERSIONS of the book so you can control F for the quizzes and exams. I rented them because it is cheaper. You have to get them because questions are straight from there
Dr. Cocchiara is amazing. I really enjoyed her lectures; her class was engaging, and she did exam reviews. If you read the textbook and follow her lectures the class is an easy A.

Took her for Diversity and she was really cool. She has a quiz and/or reflection due every week and exams every 2-3 weeks. The exams are very nitpicky, so study the technical terms carefully. She's open to meeting and working with you if you communicate. Final project is your choice of two options (choose autoethnography) Overall, loved the class.

A lot of classmates thought she was hard for our wintermester. I think she could have offered more quizzes as opposed to the short responses but it was also a fast paced which i knew was what i signed up for. I thought she was fair for the type of course, if you have common sense then her assignments are pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I honestly wouldn't recommend to take this professor during a wintermester or any short-term semesters. She wasn't prepared, which threw many students off. Test are hard if you do not grasp the information in the book. Make sure you read or you will fail. She is probably better on-campus, but online, no. Good luck to the ones who have to take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Cocchiara is a good professor, however, we have not required a textbook we had to purchase books and only read 2-3 chapters weekly. Exams and quizzes basically count as 90% of your overall grade. You must read in order to pass both and somehow remember small details in each article for the exams (without looking at the article).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Okay professor, she changes the schedule midway through the semester. She randomly does assignments and quizzes. She encourages student to get involved in class discussions. There is one big paper and presentation at the end of the semester. She quizzes you on things from the textbook, so it highly recommended to read. Exams require you to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor

Claims to be laidback, but very strict with answers and participation policy. Theories don't really make sense, and doesn't take questioning or criticism of them well. Fosters the illusion of free discourse through short answer quizzes and tests, but wants her students to closely follow her dogma, else she counts answers as wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE DR. C. IF YOU LIKE YOUR CLASS TO BE WELL THOUGHT OUT AND STRUCTURED. SHE DOESN'T FOLLOW THE SYLLABUS. SHE ASSIGNS THINGS LAST MINUTE AND MAKES UP THE COURSE AS SHE GOES ALONG. HER LEVEL OF KNOWLEDGE ON THE TOPICS ISN'T THAT GOOD EITHER, SO SHE DOESN'T DO WELL WITH QUESTIONS OR CRITIQUES.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The best way to pass Faye's class is to just show up and not say anything. She doesn't encourage critical thinking, so don't bother critiquing any theory she presents. Also, if you're in her online class, leave your camera off. If you don't, she'll watch you like a hawk & assume you're not paying attention if you look away or get up for 10 seconds
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Attend class and you will easily learn and pass this class. Very caring she will take care of any questions you have. Exam reviews and study guides given. 4 test drops lowest.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Cocchiara is amazing!! She is extremely caring for her students and she has a true passion for teaching. She has a great deal of experience in the corporate world and with teaching. One of my favorite professors in the UTA MBA Cohort program! I would definitely love to take another class taught by Dr. Cocchiara. Definitely recommend!!!
Easily the best professor at UTA. She cares about her students and wants to make sure that they both understand the material and do well. Would recommend.

Dr. Cocchiara is the best OB professor ever. She is eloquent with her voice, explains the topics well, and encourages to apply OB behavior in our lives, both personal and the work place. If she had to teach many classes related to management, I would so take her again.

I don't see why this professor has such so many awful reviews. Comp Sci requires practice and studying after class whats taught during class will never be enough. He did great at explaining concepts and the lectures were recorded so you could watch and practice with him. He even had lecture slides and practice problems posted on Canvas to view.
Great professor for an introductory course. Explained some concepts that I didn't know beforehand well.
Conly's very easy to approach. Boring lectures, but tests are open-note.

Classes are very boring. The biggest issue with this class is that you have to write the code on paper when giving the exams, which I think is not necessary. I didn't pay much attention in class, just learned online. The final exam is optional. You can bag an A, but you have to put in some effort. Chris is pretty nice though, very chill.
Great Professor and is approachable
The course was a very well-designed overall product.
The most chill professor I have taken so far! He is a very nice and relaxing guy. Take him, I promise you will not regret it!

Super relaxed guy who will not breath down your group's neck during the semester. Is more of a hands off kind of guy unless you need help. Finish your project on time and make sure you turn in the deliverables on time as well, they are easy to do.

His class is tough for new time programmers, but I felt as if I learned a lot from Chris. I attended most lectures, although you could safely not attend and just go over the slides he goes in class. I enjoyed the way he tried to introduce modern concepts into his programs. It's not the easiest subject, but an A is possible with hard work.

This class is really hard to pass. Although I got an A, it required me a lot of my work and time. You will get a good grade if and only if you teach yourself his slides (don't expect much from his lectures), understand them, and do all the homework by yourself. All the exams will be pretty easy if you do so but believe me, it's a hell lot of a work

He is the worst teacher I ever had, his lectures are boring as hell and he expects us to know programming prior. He does not really care about his students. His hws are really hard and exams are tough too. the students that came to class always slept as he was boring and he didnt care what he was teaching. He failed alot of his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He wasn't the best, he could be better, but he wasn't that bad either. Didn't get much from his lectures but his power point slides were amazing, would go through it at home and understand everything. If you are good in self study, his lecture slides is a good material. Just understand and do all the assignments by yourself, exams are easy A's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good academic advisor, but, in my opinion, not a java programming instructor.
Professor does not care about students, he cancel 6 to 7 classes in a semester and then covered the important topics of Java very quickly.

Unless you are super genius or have a good experience in programming from before, I strongly recommend you all not to take this professor's class. He does not care whether the students are understanding or not and simply goes on teaching at his own pace. Monotone, and gives heavy tests compared to the level of his teaching in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Probably the most boring class I took this semester. Half of the students in his class come there just to sit on the last bench and sleep, and the professor does not even care. The average in our class for the tests were - 66, 78, 55. This will show how tough the tests are. Difficult and depressing for new programmers.

To be honest this professor does not care about students. Cancelled 6 to 7 classes in a semester and then covered the important topics of Java very quickly. Solves only one or two basic power point codes in the class and gives heavy homework and exams. Do not take this class if you have little or no programming experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: motone prof,boring lectures,all lectures' ppt slides,exam practice questions&examples on blackboard,no need to show up to class. final grade - 16% assignments(around 10,each due every week) and 84% exams (total 4 exams). Exams- not too hard,similar to backboard posted questions,does curving sometimes, 10 pts bonus question- possible score- 110/100
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His lectures are boring. He is also VERY tough on grading. Only take this professor if you did not find classes from any other professors, or if you want low grades.

I retook this class this semester and think I have learned more about this coding language. Chris is a rather quiet and reserved person and speaks monotone in class. He is open during his office hour to re-teach you, as I don't get as much in class. His homeworks are much harder than exams, but is a good practice for exams (88% of final grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Conly is an extremely helpful professor, if you attend his office hours. I didn't get much out of his lectures. Home works are easy compared to the tests but the material is still representative of what you see on the tests. Spend a lot of time doing programming similar to what's on the home works and go to his office hours.

I am retaking this class after dropping it last semester, with the same teacher. I have learned more about java. Although, he speaks monotone in class, I appreciate Chris for patiently re-teach and answer my questions I have on any concept of the class. He curves at the end base on class grade average  (class grade average  C).
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good professor, but if new to java attend class and office hours.

Come to lecture and do the hw. For exam, do practice problem by writing it out and testing it on the computer to make sure it compute correctly. Take good notes and organize it so you can access it easily during exam. Tip: Don't let the first midterm determine your ability.
he is very tough grader, although attendance is not mandatory, you should attend class or else you wont understand JAVA

This is my first semester taking java and find it extremely challenging. Chris has potential to be helpful with students like me who struggles with it, but he makes the class seem too easy, but I understand that he was a TA and first year teaching JAVA. The homework is only 12% of grade and exams are 88%, both are very challenging.
He is a amazing professor.

Professor Conly, though he goes by Chris, is a PhD student lecturer in the CSE department. I highly recommend taking any class he teaches, as he really cares about the students. He is always happy to help students inside and outside of class, especially during office hours. Don't buy the book, as homework comes from class lectures. Thanks Chris!

Attendance is not mandatory and videos are not posted. The class can get boring because he really just goes up there and talks, but he does try to make jokes to keep your attention. He is very chill, with homework assignments being due on Sunday nights and he will change due dates if needed. Homework and exam practice material is exactly like exam.

He was pretty chill. I stopped going to his class and just went for the tests, he doesnt really post what slide they are on so you are just supposed to go through the whole thing. He skips some slides but hes funny. I actually loved this class!

Limnology was not super interesting tbh but he did make certain parts entertaining. The lack of study guides was not my favorite aswell because it's a lot of content and there's no indication as to what the objectives are for the exam. Otherwise, I would take again

Roelke was funny during lectures but I believe that he was a bit too chill with us. We got no information besides what was on canvas for the group project, which made it difficult. If there was some sort of discussion on assignments and maybe even examples given, it would be better. I also didn't enjoy the lack of study guides. "Study everything"

The professor explained topics clearly and told us exactly what to study for exams, which made preparation easier. His jokes made the class fun and helped me remember the material. The course materials were well organized, even in the fast summer format. Overall, the class was engaging and enjoyable. I would take another course with him for sure.

Very fast paced prof, but most of the slides are either images or unnecessary info. Prof Roelke will specifically tell you what's on the exams, which are practically word-for-word from the slides. The final replaces the lowest exam. He also has graded practice exams with multiple attempts, but you won't see the correct answers. Very funny otherwise

One of my fav classes at UTA!! It is a difficult class, but you will be fine if you study the slides. Lec exams are directly from the slides, and sometimes, he tells you what will be on them. Memorize the info on the slides, and you'll be fine. He's also really funny and shows us entertaining videos, so it keeps lec fun as well.

I was worried about biology before taking this course. I'm so thankful to have had this professor. His course is easy to navigate and he gives plenty of supplemental materials to help you learn. Quizzes have 2 attempts which really helps. Lowest quiz and exam grade are dropped so I did not have to take the final which was so nice! Highly Recommend
Great dude, super funny but sometimes TOO chill. Basically gave us barely any info on the group project til last min … super easy tho. Almost impossible to not get an A.

This professor is one of the best! Always responds quickly to emails. The test and quiz are simple and easy to take. Study material simplified and lectures so easy and will help you remember things using lectures and study guides and looking over the vocabulary. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. R was very clear in his expectations and grading policies. He gives plenty of materials and extra ways to learn and review the materials. He's flexible and caring. Comes off strong at first but truly is willing to work with you. Always available if needed.

I've taken Roelke for two classes now and he's honestly one of the best professors at the university. His classes can be material heavy but the material itself is not difficult. Lecture isn't mandatory but his lecture style is so interesting you'll want to go regardless. Grade consisted of exams(that were curved) and a final project. Overall,10/10

His class is only difficult if you can't lock in. One of the funniest professors I've ever had and he explains content clearly and uses examples more familiar to students. Lenient grader for sure, he drops assignments and rounds grades. He somehow managed to make his lab entertaining too. If you get the chance to take any of his classes you should!

Roelke is awesome, keeps your attention during lectures and answers any questions you have. Tests are only hard if you don't study, so make sure to do that. Tests are based off of the slideshows he does in class.

He is good at instructing you on what you must learn to excel in exams and homework. You get multiple tries on the homework and have your lowest grade dropped. Even without these, the material is easy to understand and should not be an issue when tested if studied. Just as expected from an online course, the material is self-taught. Would recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy! Does not attribute grades to mean we are "smart" or "right" for science like other professors. Also, he is humble and kind! Country folk kinda guy

His lectures were not mandatory, but they were entertaining and definitely contained information that was not available on the powerpoints, but were on the exams. Lectures were easy to follow and understand. There were 4 exams and one final project, all of which were easy and straight foward. He also allowed a curve on the exams which helped.

He is very good at lecturing, making the lectures relatable and relevant, and making this subject understandable for everyone. As long as you keep up with the work that isn't difficult and you attend the lectures, there is no way you can fail. He can be quick-tempered and sarcastic, which, if you have him for the lab, is the only bad side

Professor Roelke was great! You're graded on five online quizzes, four in-person quizzes, your lab grade, a signature assignment, and four exams. The online quizzes are unlimited attempts he also graded all the exams on a curve. All in-person quizzes were right before the exams. He's very understanding when life happens if you communicate with him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He made all the material relatable and try's to get the class engaged. His attendance isn't mandatory but went anyways because I honestly enjoyed being there. Definitely a joker and knows his material well. Great professor and will be taking him again next semester

Dr. Roelke was super easy going. Simply by submitting an assignment you would get at least a B. His tests were easy if you understood the learning objectives and the one group project took 10 minutes of work. He seems to be a nice guy and does his best to keep the class engaged.

This was a generally easy course that has PowerPoints, videos, textbooks, and study guides. There are quizzes weekly but they are generally easy and have a second attempt, tests as well but grades are curved. As long as you do your notes and practice with the homework assignments, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Roelke is a 10/10. Attendance isn't required, and at first I used to skip every lecture and still get a good grade. However, the lectures are just so entertaining that I have to go to all of them. He always looks like he is on the verge of asking if you're "working hard or hardly working". He does have quizzes often, but they are easy.
Roelke's Zoology class requires a lot of memorization, but his engaging lectures and willingness to curve exams make it manageable. unstuck study was a lifesaver for study prep.

The professor is great! He makes lectures engaging and provides all the necessary resources to help us get a passing grade. Students who struggle often have poor attendance and don't practice enough with the quizzes or practice tests he offers. He does his part to help us, but the rest is up to us.
he's pretty chill. lot's of dad jokes. tries pretty hard to engage the class so try to talk in his class

I've had Corey for 8 courses now. He is consistent, extremely intelligent, and understanding. I always get an A in his class by writing/studying flashcards for every ppt slide/term he gives us. It is a lot of work, but put in the effort, and he'll reward you with a good grade. He curves pretty much a whole letter grade at the end of the semester.
He is the most ok professor I have ever had and would definitely take a class taught by him again.

This class is very heavy. Study hard and don't miss any class because he has things he says in class that will show up on the exam. I didn't pay much attention on the 2nd exam and there were a bunch of questions I missed cause of that. Had to lock in the next 4 exams (theres 6 exams) so I could get an A. He does give a fat curve at the end though.
Great lectures. Tests are very information heavy, but totally doable. Labs aren't too bad either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
Roelke's mad chill and willing to work with u

Zoology content is easy but the tests go over a HUGE VOLUME of content that's honestly overwhelming

like memorizing the name of a crab arm isn't hard but doin that for 50 species is

U literally just gotta make a quizlet over every single word he says on the pptx and lectures

Curves r mad generous
He was very easy, just study the practice exam because the actual exams are the same. I didn't go to class a single day or study the material too much because I had other demanding classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Corey is a really chill guy who has lots of interesting stories and examples during lecture. Class is straightforward, with weekly module quizzes based on lecture ppts, the textbook, and the two books required. Both books were kind of boring, but the class isn't impossible if you don't read them. Would recommend this professor!
Weekly homework and quizzes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly, Roelke is by far the best biology professor I've had while at UTA, the man literally cannot be bothered to take himself seriously and makes dad jokes for the first 5 minutes of class, with that being said Zoology has a lot of content that requires straight-up "Learn it and burn it" tactics to succeed. Push comes to shove don't drop.

He gave us 4 exams and one presentation, he curved every exam around 10~20 points depending on the average. Presentation was 5 minutes on a water body of your choice, no rubric just talk about why you think its interesting. Only the exams and presentation are your grade although he did offer a nice amount of extra credit after the last exam.

Very biology-oriented for sure. You will know a great amount of plants and animals by the time you leave his class. He knows a lot and will expect you to do the same. Study everything he says and shows. Memorization-heavy, but he sure knows how to lift the mood up with his humor.

This class was probably the only class I ever studied for in my upper divisions. Students do not seem to understand how to think critically, which isn't his fault. I would zone out in class and perform well on exams. He is a very funny guy! I will miss his class and odd sense of humor.

The students who kiss up to him will say he is not challenging, but this class is VERY challenging. The amount of memorization you will have to complete is insane. Look, if you want to take this class then do so, but do not think it is going to be a grade booster. Nice guy, but his tests are insane. Watch one of his students thumb down my vote..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
This professor lectures and discusses many tangents NOT related to the material. The powerpoint have few words on them that do give clear direction on what he wants you to know. The tests are nothing like lecture, expect to be given 5 answer choices that all seem valid. 

No study guides; "study everything".
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was FAR from easy! A LOT of memorization but if you study HARD you will do great! I missed a few lectures in the 5 week summer course which made me miss a FEW questions on tests...but he keeps his lectures ENTERTAINING! He is hilarious and loves what he does!

Professors Roelke is very passionate about his subjects. He love to tell his experiences stories, a lot of them are funny story. Would recommend attending class because some of his test questions would base of whatever he cover in class only.
Dr. Roelke is the bomb

The professor doesn't matter for this class but I feel like Roelke's lectures were a waste of time. This class makes you memorize the whole textbook, two other books, to test you on the most specific details. This class is a lot of work compared to 1441. The only good part is that he does a tiny review before the test that will help you 25%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was one of my favorite classes/professor I have ever had. The class itself was difficult but he made it fun and exciting.

This guys lectures were intriguing and hilarious. You can tell he loves biology. But beware, this class is hard! There is lots of extraneous information in his slides, and he also blasts through important slides a little too fast. Part of the class is reading 2 books, which are relatively light readings. Chapters are also on average 100 slides long
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Roelke's lectures were really entertaining. His lectures though were not really helpful toward exams. There are also lots of quizzes in this course every week and 2 extra small books to read as well. I made an A w/o reading the textbook or small books. Dr. Roelke is kind and funny, but don't expect to get good email replies from him.

I didn't attend a single class because it's all self-taught. Your grade consists of 2-3 short quizzes each week (about 30 quizzes total) and 4 online exams, with the lowest exam grade being dropped. It's biology so a lot of studying and memorizing is to be expected but it wasn't that bad. The lab is harder and more time-consuming than the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Boring instructor, often seemed to make stuff up on the fly. Made several inappropriate comments throughout the semester. Take one of the other instructors if you can!

Professor Roelke is a great teacher, every morning he asks students how they are doing and whats new in their life. Professor Roelkes lectures aren't required but you should totally go, each day is a new adventure with him, one class he brought a box of pigeons. You should totally take him!

i took roelke twice! once for my bio lab, and for my ecology lecture prof. his lectures are alright and he's pretty funny. very straightforward which some people may not like, but i prefer it personally. the course is completely laid out on canvas. there's a lot of info, but it is a science class so it's expected. the lowest test grade is dropped!

can be kind of condescending 1-on-1, but overall friendly and helpful. exams are straightforward and not difficult if you study. course is VERY HARD and his slides have excess info so be systematic. curves exams so the average is above a C. lectures are fun to attend, even if his jokes are sometimes corny.

He was very nice, the only thing that was the slightly irritating is the fact that he does not record his lectures. However, he posts all his powerpoints, hints at what will be on the test, and has many quick quizzes each week so you will be able to gauge what you need to study.

I've taken Corey for Bio1442(B), Zoology(A), Biology of Texas(A), Undergrad Research(A-B don't know yet), and just enrolled in his Limnology class for the fall. He is a great Professor and everything you need to know is in his lectures. He gives PowerPoints which go over everything you need to know for exams. Tests are pretty easy too!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Roelke is the best professor I have had during my 3 years at UTA. I have had him for 3 different courses now and in every class he gives fascinating lectures. He has helped solidify my educational and career goals as a biologist. He has absolutely opened up my eyes to the world around us. 10/10 recommend and would take again.

Professor Roelke was an amazing professor. His lectures are exciting and interesting. He was a joy to talk to and provided allot of extra credit. I would have had an easy A, but the labs are very information heavy, and I didn't study nearly enough for it, which ended up bringing me down to an B. Very easy A if you study.

I enjoyed this Biology online class. The material was very informative, and Professor Roelke provided different options for learning and studying the same material for each unit. There were PowerPoint presentations (which I found most helpful), videos, study guides, and textbook materials provided as useful tools. Grade curves provided on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is very generous with curves; that is one of the best qualities of his class for sure. You will have to study very hard for this class. Information overload. Be careful on taking this class. Only take it if you truly need it, as there are easier alternatives. The exams are quite difficult, most are not satisfied with their grade in this course

I took zoology online with Dr. Roelke and I enjoyed his lectures and I think his exams are really fair. I don't think that reading the book is necessary to make an A, I just focused on the lectures. Dr. Roelke is very polite and professional in his communications with students.

Roelke is a great professor. He is super helpful and gives extra credit. There is a lot to do for this class. There are about 15 quizzes and 7 practice quizzes before each test. The quizzes are on Lockdown Browser. Study for the tests and quizzes and you'll be fine. Lab is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Cool guy, power points and lectures were posted at the beginning of the semester to watch and look at whenever. Tests are long and kind of vague but he curves so theres some wiggle room. Zoology is a lot of info so be prepared to take in a lot.
I don't think he is a bad instructor. He is clear on his expectations, and the tests are hard if you don't memorize the books. Basically you have to teach yourself the material. Good luck.
Pls I am warning you.. this professor is not the way to go. Never responds to emails to where you have to go to his office. You will fail unless you were born knowing/talking biology. Ooof

Everything you need for exams will be told in lecture and in the slides. Some questions are based off videos that he will assign to watch and others based on jokes from lectures. You can get by with just the slides but will miss out on his comments about pictures, etc that can be on the exams. Curves were given on every exam and the final lab grade
Dr. Roelke is a great professor! Watch his lectures for what to study. Lab is easy, study for practicals based on your TA's powerpoints.

I LOVE Roelke. I had him for limnology, and it was such a good experience. It was entirely online due to COVID, which was really nice. All of the tests consist of information taken from the slides, along with some videos he sends for us to watch. Overall, he is hilarious, he puts jokes in tests and lectures, and he cares about his students.

Class is based off of 3 tests and a lab grade. DO NOT TAKE. Lab tests are all fill in the blank with no word bank or anything. Half of the animal orders and classes you can't even pronounce but he expects you to memorize how everything is spelled. He claims the class is hard to fail .. it's hard to pass unless you have photogenic memory.

It sucks that we had to take a class like this online due to COVID, but Dr. Roelke made lectures fun and super interesting. You'll really have to work to get an A, but makes sure everyone passes as long as they're putting in the effort. Lectures are a must as he will give hints about what to note for the test.

Honestly, he is a really weird guy. He is an okay professor, but his lectures were so boring. All he ever did was read off the slides and crack a few jokes that sucked. His tests were tricky and very blunt. Wouldn't take him again. Attendance is not required, but don't skip!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Roelke is a solid choice when choosing between the 1442 professors. He is hilarious and tries to make things as simple as possible. Go to class if you can because his lectures really do help, but reading the book and taking notes over it is what solidified my A. He gives great reviews before exams. Put in the effort and you should have no trouble.

AVOID HIM if possible. I am a straight A student, worked super hard teaching myself because his lectures and reviews are horrible, barely got a B. He is very condescending. Does not help you. Lies to you and says there is hope just so he no longer has to deal with you. Reviews NEVER helped with the test. Department is a mess. Test questions tricky
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Did I enjoy this class? No. Standardized testing and labs where it is given busy-work assignments is not it. However, I'd take Corey again because he does not sugar coat. Unfortunately, this class wants us to read 40+ pgs per chpt and be asked questions of the smallest details on the exam (my biggest pet peeve). Overall, this BIOL dpt. needs work.

The quizzes are very hard - average grades were in the high 60s for a class of 90 students. The test questions are VERY TRICKY, and some had typos! Presumably the extreme specificity of questions is due to the class being online without proctored exams, but still. This class stressed me out. Upside is I now feel like I've mastered the content!

Roelke is by far the most difficult professor that I have ever taken. Not only are his tests super hard and over detailed, his class is just simply unorganised. He does not have test dates in the syllabus and he'll tell you about the next test 3-4 days before! The lab just adds on to the misery. If you have a choice, do NOT take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the hardest classes I've ever taken. Roelke is a cool guy and super smart, but his lecture style is not the best. He flies through the powerpoints so get ready to read the chapters of the book if you want to pass the exams and the departmental final. I had to teach myself the material-if you need tutoring go to it because that will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took his online Biology class for nursing majors. There are tons of power points and videos. Power points are what you need to study for questions asked on exams and quizzes and the videos are what help you actually understand whats going on. Given that this is an online class, he does not make it easy (understandably so), so study!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: PHEW! Zoology was a ride. Go to class, memorize the slides at home, memorize taxonomy and stuff for lab. go to class to watch the videos and hear his jokes cause sometimes he puts it on the test. easy points!! hes a funny, snarky guy. I liked the class and will definitely say "Hi" if I see him in the halls!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's an alright teacher, and he's pretty engaging to listen to, but all he does is read off of the standardized powerpoint and show a few videos. This course is entirely memory based, so I stopped showing up near the end and just studied on my own. Get the powerpoints on blackboard, know them well, and you'll be fine.

BIOL 1442 with him isn't bad at all. You don't need the book, just his PowerPoints. The exams are literally just the PowerPoints so showing up to class is very optional. He kinda just reads off the slides with the occasional short story or random video. He's interesting, chill, and easy to talk to. He's pretty funny too. Easy to contact.

Definitely not an easy A. The lab is way harder than the actual lecture. No need to read the book most of the test is based from the lectures. Lecture attendance is not necessary but its very beneficial. Record the lectures!!!!!

He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities. I did them all. He never added any of it. When I asked him about it, he refused to honor it and was very rude. He called my lab table "the reject table" and made jokes out of not giving us any lab samples or making us wait to get them. But he's an entertaining lecturer. That's something, I guess.
Tests are tough and all we do is watch weird videos. Departmental bio is such a bad idea

Lecture isn't too difficult but you HAVE to put effort in lab. There's a ton of information that he splits into six tests throughout the semester but as long as you keep up with the material you should be fine. Lab is difficult and counts for 40% of your grade. GO TO CLASS because he tests over random things he mentions.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This class is A TON of information to memorize, but Role at least makes it bearable. His lectures are funny and he throws in the things he talked about in class as easy test questions. You need to study the slides a ton but don't bother with the book. Attendance not mandatory but he does ask questions on the test about stories he told/videos

Memorize EVERYTHING! Like if he's giving a lecture & uses some off the wall example, memorize it! ALL the little things your think are insignificant, memorize them! THEY WILL SHOW UP ON THE EXAMS. He's super funny & lectures are great. Lots of vids & even a movie! Clear cut grading criteria. Usually a curve. If you fail, it's your own fault tbh

Dr. Roelke is a great lecturer! Go to class, most of the info on the tests are on the slides but he purposely bases some questions strictly on the lecture. He talks really fast; recording the lectures would help a ton so you don't miss anything. Lots of memorization. Don't buy the book, just borrow it from the SECC, read the pages he recommends.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Although he keeps the class entertaining more than the other professors do, this is practically a self teach class where if you have the book and he post the power point slides; I would focus more on getting an 80 or above in lab (which is easy) if your not good on test, than you would not have to worry too much about your lecture grade.

Went to 5 or so lectures the whole semester, because his lecturing was useless for the tests. Reading off the powerpoints is something I can do on my own. Anyways, he's a good person, but as a professor, he goes too fast and goes off topic way too much. Tests were kinda hard. Self-study is the best way to go. Don't study last min.

Easy A. Only 4 grades: 2 exams, one presentation, and the iNat project(just taking pics of animals/plants). The first exam was the hardest part of the class. Half the questions were not talked about in class. Memorize all the plants and animals on ppts. Go to the local field trips, he will give hints about whats on the exam. Extra credit. Made a 99

If you want to make an A, you need to know everything on the slides. He does make you read specific pages from the book, but I made an A without the book. He always curves the avg to a 70. Lab is easy if you put in the work every week. Go to class- he tests on videos he showed in class and sometimes the jokes he made. Take pics in lab and label!!
Roelke is very good, however, he tends to go off topic in his lectures. You end up watching a ton of pointless YouTube videos and talking about things that will never show up on the exams.

Professor Roelke makes this class very entertaining, however make sure you do well in lab as you would in lecture. Lab in my opinion was the hardest part of the course because it contained a lot more information than lecture did. Other than the 2 practicals in lab, there are 6 exams every two weeks.

Roelke is a funny guy that knows zoology well. The class itself is a beast with 6 exams, plus all the lab stuff. As long as you come to class and pay attention, he's a friendly guy and will help you. He likes to give out extra credit by asking for funny jokes or dressing up in costumes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The textbook wasn't needed. Dr. Roelke posts his slides online, but he is very good at explaining w/examples in class. Attendance is taken with the clicker through questions on slides. He doesn't update hw and participation grades often, which I wish he did. Other than that, study and come to class. He's a funny dude and will break it down for you!

Grades are based only on exams and the exams are based almost entirely on what he says during lecture. Take notes on everything he says including stories, video clips and mythical sea monsters. He's not interested in interacting with students, so not a good choice if you're actually excited about the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Roelke is an outstanding professor, both in his lectures and in teaching the material, and is extremely passionate about his work. His teaching style and humor are akin to one another; amazing. Biology majors are fortunate to have a tutor such as he.

Never wrote a review before but this guy definitely deserves one! He's easily the best professor I've ever had and would definitely take him again for zoology:) He really cares about making sure his students leave his class with actual knowledge that they both care about and use. Over all super genuine guy, funny, and great teacher.

This is a really fun class but it's crazy hard. Roelke is a great professor who really knows his stuff. Go to class because he gives hints about what will be on the test, and sometimes gives you test questions ahead of time.

I've had him for two different classes. Your grade consists of 4/5 exams + your lab grade; lab and lecture are both worth about 50/50 so if your're not doing well in lab, do well on your lecture exams and you should be fine, or vice versa. Both times I took him, he curved our final letter grade. Study what's on his PPTs and you'll be good!

Dr. Roelke is a walking encyclopedia. He is funny as hell and probably one of the best lecturers on the campus. The class is difficult, be prepared to read and study or you won't pass. The tests are a bell curve, but once you do bad it's hard to recover.  There is a lab attached, it's just as difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Easiest biology class ever. However, tests are in every 2 weeks so don't slack off. He curves if the class average is lower than a 70. Very fair professor. Doesn't do drops. Make sure to do well in Lab. A B can turn into an A. Always attend class due to questions in the exam may appear and watch the videos in ppt. Use that to study. Good luck! :D
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY
